title: Payton Tolle’s Case To Be the Red Sox's Game 1 Starter | Just Baseball
author: Jordan Leandre
body:
They haven’t clinched a postseason berth yet, but it looks more likely by the day that the Boston Red Sox have a date with the New York Yankees in the Wild Card round again.
This will be the third matchup between these two arch rivals in the Wild Card round since 2021, with each organization winning once. The Red Sox got the best of Gerrit Cole in 2021 at Fenway Park, while the Yankees won two straight elimination games to knock off Boston in the Bronx last year.
This series promises to be low-scoring. These two teams are top three in baseball in staff earned run average. The Yankees have nearly three-quarters of a run lead on the Red Sox among starters, while the two bullpens are separated by 0.01 earned runs per nine.
A lot will be made of how these two staffs line up in a couple of weeks. The first two games for the Yankees, as deep as their pitching staff is, seem destined to be Cam Schlittler in Game 1 and Max Fried in Game 2. However, the Red Sox have serious questions to answer about how they want to line up.
Preparing for this series to go the distance is difficult. If you sweep, you line yourselves up well for Game 1 of the American League Division Series. However, if you get swept, one of your best pitchers may never see the hill.
The conundrum is as follows: Sonny Gray has been their best arm wire-to-wire. Payton Tolle is by far their hottest arm, seeming to get stronger as the season wears on. Ranger Suárez is riding two great starts in a row and is their high-priced free agent with elite postseason pedigree.
But of the three, there’s no question who should pitch opposite Schlittler in Game 1: Tolle.
Stats updated prior to games on September 19.
Game 1 Is a Tone-Setter
The dialogue surrounding Game 1 is that it’s almost a “scheduled loss.” To be frank, it’s hard to argue against the logic. In four starts against Boston this year, Schlittler has a 0.74 ERA, a .174 batting average against, and a 27.3% strikeout rate across 24.1 innings.
Let us not forget the sheer domination he exhibited in Game 3 against the Red Sox last year, either. Across eight innings, he allowed five hits, no runs, and struck out 12.
But the mindset for Boston can’t be that it has no chance of winning. Sure, they’ve been one of the league’s best road teams this year, but the Yankees have the best pitching staff in baseball this year for a reason. By comparison, sure, it’s easier to win against someone not in the Cy Young race. But Max Fried habitually finds himself in the discussion for a reason.
The Red Sox’s mindset should be that runs will be at a premium, so matching the Yankees ace zero-for-zero is paramount. Of the three options, Tolle presents the best opportunity to do so. While Gray has Tolle beat overall in ERA, the Red Sox rookie southpaw is, by far, the hottest arm on the staff.
Since the All-Star break, Tolle has a 2.90 ERA with a 28.2% strikeout-to-walk rate. That ERA drops to 2.53 over his last nine starts. That 2.90 ERA, however, is nearly a third of a run better than Gray’s, and over half a run better than Suárez’s.
Sheer run prevention is the name of the game in this series. Tolle is their best option.
Tolle’s Attitude Is Perfect for the Moment
Every time Tolle speaks, he endears himself to the baseball world even more. But as goofy as he can be in media sessions, he’s all business on the field. Furthermore, he can appreciate the moment he’s in at any given time.
Look no further than his recent start against the Kansas City Royals. Eight pitches, eight strikes, six whiffs, all fastballs. He had the wherewithal to glance at pitching coach Andrew Bailey, grin, lock back in and pick up the final strike of an immaculate inning.
Sure, it’s one pitch in the first inning against a team out of postseason contention, but talk to anybody who’s played, and they’ll tell you how aware they are of when they’re on the brink of something cool. Tolle said as much after the game.
But that moment should tell the world he’s unafraid of going into the Bronx, facing off against Schlittler, and going band-for-band with the likely AL Cy Young.
Tolle clearly cares about what he does, but it’s that somewhat unserious attitude that makes him perfect for the high stakes of setting the tone in a postseason series.
This moment, honestly, seemed set in stone the moment he made his MLB debut last season against Paul Skenes. While any postseason start is high leverage, he’s always finding himself making big starts against the game’s best. He’s always met the moment, and the Red Sox should let him continue that trend this postseason.
The Yankees Struggle Against Hard Fastballs
The Yankees are a deep, talented team even if not all players are at full strength or potential going into October. One area where they struggle, however, is against hard fastballs.
This season, the Yankees have the highest strikeout rate on fastballs 95 mph or harder, to go with the second-worst expected batting average. Only the Chicago White Sox are worse against such fastballs.
They’re even worse this season on hard fastballs thrown by left-handers. Their 33% strikeout rate is the second-highest behind the 61-93 Athletics, while their .191 expected batting average ranks only higher than the Cleveland Guardians.
Tolle isn’t positioned with an elite-level fastball from a velocity standpoint, but it’s comfortably above average. This season, he’s in the 71st percentile with an average fastball of 95.7 mph. Opponents struggle mightily against it as well, hitting just .190 with a .248 expected wOBA and a 30.4% whiff rate.
Tolle throws his four-seam and sinker a combined 68.4% of the time. While that leaves him susceptible to predictability, he varies that look with a cutter that comes in at 88.6 mph on average. He throws that offering at a 19.4% clip.
His strength is his fastball, along with 98th percentile extension. That plays directly into the weaknesses of the Yankees lineup. With Game 1 very much being a tone-setter, there’s no question who the Red Sox should send out there.
Lining It Up After Tolle
Following Tolle, the Red Sox have their two veterans waiting in the wings. Win Game 1, you’ve got two proven performers to help you win one more game to advance. Lose Game 1, you’ve got two experienced professionals tasked with staving off elimination.
The order after Tolle almost doesn’t matter. Could they vary looks and go to Gray to keep the Yankees off the lefty scent? Maybe, but then you potentially run into the same problem of playing with your food. That said, Suárez is much craftier than Tolle, and prone to the hanging breaking ball.
The Yankees have a 99 wRC+ as a team against right-handed pitching, and a 107 against lefties. Gray also took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Yankees back in late June, while Suárez was touched up in his last start against them.
What can be said either way is that having two accomplished veterans to follow the rookie gunslinger is a good position for the Red Sox to be in.

title: Red Sox eager to regain mojo in rubber match vs. 'relentless' Rays
body:
Field Level Media
                
20 Sep 2026, 20:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
Jahmai Jones said he feels the Boston Red Sox have grown this week, and perhaps he has a point.
After Trevor Story's late homer led Boston to a win in the finale of its previous series, the Red Sox will look to capture the decisive contest of their current set on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Rays in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Jones homered from the designated hitter position in Friday's 4-2 victory over the Rays. He said the two games more resembled the way Boston has played during the second half of 2026.
'We've had some big performances. I feel like it's a different guy every night,' said Jones, who notched his sixth homer of the season in a night in which Roman Anthony went deep and had three RBIs.
'Everybody in here knows what we're playing for. I feel we've had a lot of tight ball games. That last one in Texas (on Thursday) and then (Friday showed) who we are and what our baseball is.'
The Red Sox (84-71) saw their momentum slowed on Saturday, however, with a 2-1 setback to the Rays (94-60). They enter the game comfortably in line for the second wild card in the American League.
Richie Palacios had an RBI single in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero with the winning run. It marked the third walk-off win of the season-ending homestand for Tampa Bay.
'We're just relentless. No matter what's going on in the game, we always feel like we have a chance to win,' Palacios said. 'Three walk-offs is amazing, and we're just going to continue to do what we do.'
Tampa Bay has won seven of its past eight games overall to move five games ahead of the second-place New York Yankees in the American League East. The teams each have eight games remaining on their schedule -- four of them against each other. The teams open their series Tuesday in New York with a doubleheader.
'It's very encouraging. It's a good feeling,' Rays manager Kevin Cash said following Saturday's game. 'You want to get as many reps at that as possible, because we know the games that we're going to continue playing this year are going to be against good teams and in tight ballgames.'
Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) is scheduled to start on Sunday.
Jax scattered two hits over five scoreless innings and struck out seven in five innings of a no-decision against the Athletics last Tuesday. The Rays won 2-1.
He is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in two starts against Boston this season. He is 0-2 with a 7.86 ERA in 16 career appearances (three starts) against the Red Sox.
Boston left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-6, 4.99) is the scheduled starter on Sunday. He has lost his past six decisions heading into Sunday's game, most recently a 4-2 setback to the Texas Rangers on Tuesday. He yielded four runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings and threw 68 pitches.
Sandoval is 0-3 with a 3.67 ERA in nine games (eight starts) against the Rays.
The Red Sox would love to welcome back Ceddanne Rafaela, who suffered a right quadriceps strain on Sept. 2 in a game against the Seattle Mariners and was placed on the 10-day injured list. He was hitting .282 with 16 home runs, 32 doubles and 70 RBIs to go along with 17 stolen bases.
--Field Level Media

original_body:
Field Level Media
                
20 Sep 2026, 20:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
Jahmai Jones said he feels the Boston Red Sox have grown this week, and perhaps he has a point.
After Trevor Story's late homer led Boston to a win in the finale of its previous series, the Red Sox will look to capture the decisive contest of their current set on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Rays in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Jones homered from the designated hitter position in Friday's 4-2 victory over the Rays. He said the two games more resembled the way Boston has played during the second half of 2026.
'We've had some big performances. I feel like it's a different guy every night,' said Jones, who notched his sixth homer of the season in a night in which Roman Anthony went deep and had three RBIs.
'Everybody in here knows what we're playing for. I feel we've had a lot of tight ball games. That last one in Texas (on Thursday) and then (Friday showed) who we are and what our baseball is.'
The Red Sox (84-71) saw their momentum slowed on Saturday, however, with a 2-1 setback to the Rays (94-60). They enter the game comfortably in line for the second wild card in the American League.
Richie Palacios had an RBI single in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero with the winning run. It marked the third walk-off win of the season-ending homestand for Tampa Bay.
'We're just relentless. No matter what's going on in the game, we always feel like we have a chance to win,' Palacios said. 'Three walk-offs is amazing, and we're just going to continue to do what we do.'
Tampa Bay has won seven of its past eight games overall to move five games ahead of the second-place New York Yankees in the American League East. The teams each have eight games remaining on their schedule -- four of them against each other. The teams open their series Tuesday in New York with a doubleheader.
'It's very encouraging. It's a good feeling,' Rays manager Kevin Cash said following Saturday's game. 'You want to get as many reps at that as possible, because we know the games that we're going to continue playing this year are going to be against good teams and in tight ballgames.'
Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) is scheduled to start on Sunday.
Jax scattered two hits over five scoreless innings and struck out seven in five innings of a no-decision against the Athletics last Tuesday. The Rays won 2-1.
He is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in two starts against Boston this season. He is 0-2 with a 7.86 ERA in 16 career appearances (three starts) against the Red Sox.
Boston left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-6, 4.99) is the scheduled starter on Sunday. He has lost his past six decisions heading into Sunday's game, most recently a 4-2 setback to the Texas Rangers on Tuesday. He yielded four runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings and threw 68 pitches.
Sandoval is 0-3 with a 3.67 ERA in nine games (eight starts) against the Rays.
The Red Sox would love to welcome back Ceddanne Rafaela, who suffered a right quadriceps strain on Sept. 2 in a game against the Seattle Mariners and was placed on the 10-day injured list. He was hitting .282 with 16 home runs, 32 doubles and 70 RBIs to go along with 17 stolen bases.

title: Red Sox Welcome Back Key Arm as Playoff Push Heats Up
author: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
body:
The Boston Red Sox will face off against the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday in a rubber match on the road and the Red Sox got a reinforcement back just in time for the series finale.
Boston has been missing 2026 breakout flamethrower Tyron Guerrero since Aug. 31. That will change on Sunday afternoon. The Red Sox announced that Guerrero is back and righty Wyatt Olds has been sent down to Triple-A in response.
"The Red Sox today reinstated RHP Tyron Guerrero from the 15-Day Injured List. To make room, Boston optioned RHP Wyatt Olds to Triple-A Worcester," the Red Sox announced.
The Red Sox Got A Key Back
Over the last few weeks, much has been said about the reinforcements coming. Guerrero's return is the first example of this. The 6'8'' righty has a 3.26 ERA and a 36-to-7 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 38 2/3 innings pitched. It had been seven years since Guerrero had pitched in a big league game before the 2026 season. He last pitched in the majors back in 2019 with the Miami Marlins. He's been a breakout story for the Red Sox and now he's back.
Olds has been very good when he has been active on the big league roster this season. He has a 1.20 ERA in 13 appearances this season as a rookie, to go along with a 20-to-7 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 15 innings pitched.
Guerrero is the first reinforcement back for the bullpen, but he isn't likely to be the last. Garrett Crochet and Tanner Houck are two other guys who could be back in the not-so-distant future. Houck is closer than Crochet is. Houck has been on a minor league rehab assignment. Crochet has been tossing bullpens, but hasn't advanced to facing live hitters just yet.
Olds has been good, but it was known that difficult bullpen decisions would be coming. This is the first and we should see more in the coming days.
Guerrero went from unknown among the Red Sox's fanbase, to a high-leverage guy for Boston fairly quickly. Now, he's back as Boston has a chance to clinch a spot in the postseason on Sunday afternoon against the Rays. If the Red Sox take down Tampa Bay, they will officially punch their ticket. Boston's magic number is down to one. A win will get them into the playoffs. Even if they lose, they can make it in on Sunday with losses by other clubs fighting for the Wild Card spots. It could be a big day for Boston and Guerrero's back.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

title: Red Sox's Curtis Mead Quietly Inching Closer to Playoff Return
author: Jackson Roberts; Unknown
body:
Curtis Mead has arguably been the most frustrating non-factor for the Boston Red Sox this season, because he never got his chance to make an impact.
In his very first game after being acquired in a trade with the Washington Nationals, Mead fractured his left wrist on a high-and-tight fastball against the Athletics. He quickly found himself in an uphill battle to return to action before the Red Sox's season ended at some point in the playoffs, but he's started making some progress.
According to a Saturday MLB.com injury update, Mead has begun hitting off a tee, which slipped under the radar amid a slough of injury news about Willson Contreras, Garrett Crochet, and others. Good news, to be sure, but far from a guarantee he makes it back for a game this year.
Mead's return not imminent, but progress made
Interim manager Chad Tracy said earlier this week that the tee work was beginning on Wednesday, per Boston Sports Gordo on X. That means we're a few days late to this particular story, so apologies to our readers — but not much slips by us, so it was a particularly quiet announcement.
Mead's breakout season (.851 OPS, 17 home runs in 88 games) was halted at the worst possible time. The Red Sox were looking to add an impact bat at the trade deadline, and Mead's absence has been nearly as awkward as Adley Rutschman's struggles.
Would Mead be the slam-dunk starter at second base even if he came back fully healthy this week? That's another real issue to consider, since Nick Sogard has done a nice job over the last month-plus. Perhaps Mead would at least be in the lineup against left-handed pitchers over the struggling Andruw Monasterio and/or Isiah Kiner-Falefa.
The Red Sox will have interesting decisions to make at the fringes of the roster for the first couple of rounds of the playoffs, no matter what. If Mead re-enters the picture, we could see someone who feels like they earned their spot get the axe, but that's the cost of doing business in a year when the American League could be up for grabs.
Jackson Roberts is a former Division III All-Region DH who now writes and talks about sports for a living. A Bay Area native and a graduate of Swarthmore College and the Newhouse School at Syracuse University, Jackson makes his home in North Jersey. He grew up rooting for the Red Sox, Patriots, and Warriors, and he recently added the Devils to his sports fandom mosaic. title: Game 156: How the Red Sox can clinch a playoff berth, plus lineups and notes vs. Rays - The Boston Globe
author: Cam Kerry
body:
The Red Sox’ magic number is one.
The Rays, armed with the best record in the American League, are 8-2 in their last 10 games, including a 2-1 win Saturday over Boston. Brayan Bello gave the Sox a solid effort, fanning 11 over eight innings of work.
But in Sunday’s series finale, Boston can clinch a playoff berth. It’s simple: Just win. That’s the easiest option. If Boston loses today, a loss by the Astros seals a date in the postseason. Houston plays the Braves Sunday with first pitch at 2:10 p.m.
Patrick Sandoval will start for the Red Sox Sunday. He has gone six innings just once in his last six starts. He has allowed four runs in his last two starts. He has faced Tampa Bay once this season, surrendering four earned runs in five innings on July 18.
Here’s a preview of Sunday’s action.

title: Boston Red Sox Announce Jarren Duran Move on Sunday
author: Simeon Kotto
body:
The Boston Red Sox and Tampa Bay Rays head into Sunday’s series finale at Fenway Park with the three-game set knotted at one win apiece after Saturday’s 2-1 Rays victory.
Left-hander Patrick Sandoval takes the mound for Boston against Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax, a matchup that carries extra weight with the regular season winding down and playoff positioning still in flux.
Interim manager Chad Tracy has kept the bulk of his starting nine intact, but he has made a modest yet noticeable adjustment involving outfielder Jarren Duran, via Underdog MLB.
After sitting out the series opener and batting eighth on Saturday, Duran will slide up one spot into the seventh hole. He will hit in front of Isaiah Kiner-Falefa and Nate Eaton while remaining in center field, the position he has occupied since injuries to Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White opened the job.
The rest of the order features Roman Anthony in left, Mickey Gasper at designated hitter, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Trevor Story at shortstop, Nick Sogard at first, and Cooper Durbin at third.
The move comes during a difficult individual season for Duran. Entering Sunday he is hitting .206 in 144 games, with 65 runs, 110 hits, 20 home runs and 69 RBIs. His slugging percentage sits at .364 and his OPS at .626.
Speculation about a possible trade lingered for weeks before the August 4 deadline, yet Duran remained in a Red Sox uniform and has continued to receive regular playing time as the club pushes toward October.
Boston sits at 84-71 with seven games left and occupies what currently looks like the second American League Wild Card spot. Should the standings hold, the Red Sox would open the postseason on the road in a best-of-three Wild Card series against the New York Yankees.
Every remaining game, including Sunday’s finale against a familiar division rival, therefore carries playoff implications.
Tracy’s decision to bump Duran up in the order is a small tactical shift rather than a wholesale overhaul, but it signals a willingness to tinker as the club tries to generate more consistent offense down the stretch.
Whether the extra spot in the lineup produces results remains to be seen.
Duran’s season-long struggles have been well documented, yet he has shown flashes of the power and speed that once made him a fixture in the middle of Boston’s order.
A productive afternoon against Jax and the Rays would give the Red Sox a series victory and a bit of momentum heading into the final week.
With the calendar now late September and the postseason picture still taking shape, even incremental lineup changes can feel significant.

title: Red Sox Receive Major Injury Update on 30-Year-Old Pitcher During Rays Series
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The Boston Red Sox have split the first two games of their series with the Tampa Bay Rays.
This now sets up an intriguing rubber match to take place on Sunday afternoon at Tropicana Field as the two teams meet for the final time this regular season.
Ahead of the matchup, the Red Sox got some very encouraging news down in Triple-A Worcester regarding one of their handful of injured pitchers.
Red Sox Get Update on Kutter Crawford
It’s been a whirlwind two-year span for right-handed pitcher Kutter Crawford.
njuries have forced him to battle through setbacks, and after three consistent years with the Red Sox, he hasn’t pitched for the team since 2024.
Crawford missed the entire 2025 season due to knee issues and right wrist surgery. He then opened the 2026 season on the injured list, and while he returned on April 11 to make a rehab start, he immediately went back on the shelf afterward.
Now, WooSox reporter Tommy Cassell has revealed that Crawford will make a rehab appearance for Worcester on Sunday, if the game takes place.
Via Tommy Cassell: “Red Sox pitcher Kutter Crawford is scheduled to make a rehab appearance and pitch today for the WooSox (if they play). The 30-year-old right-hander hasn’t pitched since April 11, which was also a rehab outing with Triple-A Worcester.”
Red Sox pitcher Kutter Crawford is scheduled to make a rehab appearance and pitch today for the WooSox (if they play).
The 30-year-old right-hander hasn’t pitched since April 11, which was also a rehab outing with Triple-A Worcester.
— Tommy Cassell (@TommyCassell_) September 20, 2026
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston enters Sunday with an 84-71 overall record, and their focus is beginning to shift toward postseason mode.
For Crawford, making it into any high-leverage spots at the major league level this year would be quite the miracle. However, simply ending the season with some rehab starts under his belt and potentially finding a way onto the Red Sox taxi squad would be a major development for a player who hasn’t had much luck over the last two seasons.
His exact workload for Sunday remains unknown, and he’ll likely need to make at least a few more appearances before the Red Sox even consider calling him up.

title: Red Sox's Wyatt Olds: Sent to Worcester
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Boston optioned Olds to Triple-A Worcester on Sunday.

title: Red Sox Reinstate RHP Tyron Guerrero from 15-Day IL
author: By
body:
Red Sox Reinstate RHP Tyron Guerrero from 15-Day IL
BOSTON, MA—The Boston Red Sox today reinstated right-handed pitcher Tyron Guerrero from the 15-Day Injured List. To make room, Boston optioned right-handed pitcher Wyatt Olds to Triple-A Worcester.
Guerrero, 35, was placed on the 15-Day Injured List on September 1 with right shoulder inflammation. The right-hander has recorded a 3.26 ERA (14 ER/38.2 IP) with 36 strikeouts in 38 games for Boston this season. He has also posted a 0.92 ERA (2 ER/19.2 IP) with 22 strikeouts in 15 relief outings for Triple-A Worcester this year. Originally signed as an international free agent by the San Diego Padres in May 2010, the Colombia native owns a 5.10 ERA (82 ER/144.2 IP) with 147 strikeouts in 151 career Major League games with the Padres (2016), Miami Marlins (2018-19), and Red Sox (2026).
Olds, 27, has posted a 1.20 ERA (2 ER/15.0 IP) with 20 strikeouts in 13 relief outings for Boston this season, his Major League debut. The right-hander has also posted a 5.33 ERA (30 ER/50.2 IP) with 74 strikeouts in 39 games this year for Worcester. Selected by the Red Sox in the seventh round of the 2021 First-Year Player Draft, the Oklahoma native owns a 5.88 ERA (254 ER/389.0 IP) with 489 strikeouts in 185 career minor league games (42 starts).

title: Red Sox News & Links: Willson Contreras still struggling with hand injury
author: Dan Secatore
body:
X-rays on Willson Contreras’s hand were negative, but don’t take that to mean everything is sunshine, rainbows, and Swiss cheese. Contreras’s hand still shows visible bruising and he cannot grip a bat. He hopes to take some initial swings today. “Hand’s still really sore. Woke up feeling a little better,” he said. “I can squeeze a little better than [Friday], but it’s going to take a few days… I’m going to do everything in my power to get back on the field before the playoffs.” (Peter Abraham, Boston Globe)
Contreras won’t be on the field for a few days, but he’s still in the clubhouse. That wasn’t the case for Roman Anthony, who was sent to Fort Myers during his rehab, where he worked hard to stay connected to the team. “Just staying in touch with them and seeing what they were doing, I think it’s just the relationship we have,” Anthony said. “As a group, we’re all so close. For me, obviously, Fort Myers wasn’t the most ideal situation, but that’s part of it, and I had a good group of guys down there, and up here.” (Tara Sullivan, Boston Globe)
But now that he’s back in the big leagues, it’s time for Roman to start producing more consistently. He did some extra hitting work before this series against the Rays began and the team is confident he’s going to really get going. “I mean, you see what he can do. It’s the game of baseball, there’s ebbs and flows,” said Chad Tracy. “He came off the rehab, and for like five games, he looked fantastic. Then he went through some stuff, and now he’s starting to look good again. When he’s going well, you see the impact he can make.” (Jen McCaffrey, The Athletic)
Garrett Crochet isn’t with the time right now, but he’s still trying to get back with them. He donned his full uniform yesterday at Polar Park in Worcester and threw 20 pitches, topping out at 92 MPH. The Sox hope he can throw to live hitters at Fenway later this week. Tanner Houck, meanwhile, threw 3.1 innings for the WooSox in his final rehab appearance. (Ian Browne, MLB.com)
A healthy Crochet and Houck could make for a formidable bridge to the back of the bullpen. And after yesterday’s outstanding start, Brayan Bello has also shown that he’s ready to be a part of the postseason action. “For me, it’s just showing the team that I’m ready for these kind of games,” Bello said. “Also, them giving me the opportunity to pitch today was a good step for that. And I thank them for giving me the confidence and the opportunity to start again.” (Rob Bradford, WEEI)
If Crochet and Houck do make it back to the roster, hopefully their transition will be as seamless as Trevor Story’s has been. “The point of getting the surgery was to come back and try to be the player that I know I can be,” he said, “and it’s starting to show.” (Hayden Bird, Boston.com)

Tanner Houck, meanwhile, threw 3.1 innings for the WooSox in his final rehab appearance. (Ian Browne, MLB.com)
A healthy Crochet and Houck could make for a formidable bridge to the back of the bullpen. And after yesterday’s outstanding start, Brayan Bello has also shown that he’s ready to be a part of the postseason action. “For me, it’s just showing the team that I’m ready for these kind of games,” Bello said. “Also, them giving me the opportunity to pitch today was a good step for that. And I thank them for giving me the confidence and the opportunity to start again.” (Rob Bradford, WEEI)

title: Boston Red Sox Announce Jarren Duran Change Before Rays Series Finale
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The Boston Red Sox lost 2-1 against the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday to even the series at one game apiece entering Sunday’s finale.
On the mound for the Red Sox will be left-hander Patrick Sandoval, while the Rays will send out righty Griffin Jax.
Ahead of the matchup, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy didn’t make many major changes to his starting lineup but made a few tweaks, including one involving outfielder Jarren Duran.
Red Sox Announce Duran Change
After not playing in the series opener and batting eighth on Saturday, Tracy is moving Duran up one spot in the batting order to the seven-hole, where he’ll hit in front of Isaiah Kiner-Falefa and Nate Eaton.
Duran will once again start in center field, where he’s continued to play since injuries to Ceddanne Rafaela and Eli White.
Here’s the full Red Sox lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Red Sox 9/20 R. Anthony LF M. Gasper DH A. Rutschman C T. Story SS N. Sogard 1B C. Durbin 3B J. Duran CF I. Kiner-Falefa 2B N. Eaton RF P. Sandoval SP.”
Red Sox 9/20
R. Anthony LF
M. Gasper DH
A. Rutschman C
T. Story SS
N. Sogard 1B
C. Durbin 3B
J. Duran CF
I. Kiner-Falefa 2B
N. Eaton RF
P. Sandoval SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 20, 2026
Duran’s 2026 Season
It’s been a challenging year for Duran. And he didn’t even know if he’d remain in a Red Sox uniform beyond the Aug. 4 trade deadline after his name surfaced as a possible trade candidate for weeks.
Yet, he’s still in Boston, and entering Sunday afternoon, he’s hitting .206 across 144 games with 65 runs, 110 hits, 20 home runs, and 69 RBIs while slugging .364 with a .626 OPS.
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston holds an 84-71 overall record with just seven games remaining in the regular season. They’re currently in position to likely be the second Wild Card team in the AL.
If the current standings hold, the Red Sox would travel to the Bronx for a best-of-three series against the New York Yankees in Round 1.

title: 5 players who are entering their final days as a member of the Red Sox
author: Stephen Parello
body:
The Boston Red Sox roster is about to get a bit more crowded as several players are set to return from the injured list before the end of the season. Additionally, even some players who make the cut and play in October might find themselves looking for new homes this winter for a variety of reasons.
One thing the Red Sox have is a solid amount of depth. It's what allowed the club to survive so many injuries and mount a rally after such a horrendous start to the season.
On the flip side, sometimes too much depth is a bad thing. There are only so many roster spots to go around, and at a certain point, Boston needs impact players and not just guys who can hold down the fort in case of emergency.
5 players who are entering their final days as a member of the Red Sox
Masataka Yoshida
We'll start with a controversial one. Getting rid of Masataka Yoshida outright would mean eating $18 million in 2027. Even moving him in a trade would likely result in the Red Sox paying down a good portion of his contract. That doesn't exactly sound like something John Henry would go for.
However, there are just too many reasons why the 33-year-old is no longer worth a roster spot. Injuries have played a major role in Yoshida's Red Sox career. On top of that, it's hard to justify a platoon DH without much power and no defensive ability taking up a roster spot, especially given Boston's outfield logjam. There's a chance he's back from the IL prior to the playoffs starting, but it's hard to see how he fits the postseason roster.
Patrick Sandoval
Patrick Sandoval was a worthwhile dart throw as an injury stash when the Red Sox signed him ahead of the 2025 season. With that said, he's shown that he's not much more than a fifth starter at this point. Boston has an abundance of pitching depth, especially of the left-handed variety, making it a near-certainty that the free-agent-to-be is seeking employment elsewhere this offseason.
Isiah Kiner-Falefa
This is a tough one because, in many ways, Isiah Kiner-Falefa has exceeded expectations this season. The utility infielder is having a career season at the plate and has been a spark plug for Boston. However, does his value hold up as well if his bat falls off more in line with his career averages? There is some intangible value to keeping him around, but it's hard to pony up for a cheerleader when the club has other younger and cheaper options.
Triston Casas
Not technically in a Red Sox uniform due to his litany of injuries, but it's fair to say that Triston Casas' days as a member of the organization are numbered. He can't be counted on to stay healthy. It's unclear what his production would look like after so much time away. Finally, Boston could really do without the headaches. This is a clear non-tender case.
Jahmai Jones
It's starting to become clear why Jahmai Jones never got much of an opportunity to carve out a big league role before 2025. Jones is supposed to mash lefties while playing some outfield and DHing, but for much of the season he's done nothing of the sort. Even his breakout 2025 campaign came over just 150 plate appearances. It's not exactly worth going into arbitration with a player who's failing at executing the one skill he supposedly has.

title: The Blue Jays have slipped in the standings - Dose.ca
author: Dose
body:
After suffering their second loss in two nights to the Texas Rangers, the Toronto Blue Jays are now three games away from making the playoffs.
Meanwhile, the Chicago White Sox defeated the Detroit Tigers 3-1.
Yesterday's 6-2 loss in Arlington stings, and this win by the Rangers puts them in first place in the American League West this morning. It's now up to the Houston Astros to deal with the pressure of clinching a playoff spot. The other Texas team is just two games away from its goal.
With only seven regular-season games left to play, let's just say time is running out for John Schneider's squad. Does the team's 76-79 record perfectly reflect its performance so far? In my opinion, this record reveals a team that has been searching for its identity for much of the season and has had to deal with a number of injuries to key players. Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s disappointing season adds to the reasons that will be discussed in a few days.
Let's let the 2026 season run its course—the time for reckoning will come soon enough.
Yesterday, the Toronto offense once again lacked energy. Ever since setting foot on Texas soil, the Jays' hitters have been sluggish and unable to find a response to the Rangers' pitchers' offerings. In contrast, Skip Schumaker's men are playing with conviction and scoring early in the game, giving themselves every chance to win.
In the West, the Rangers have been playing much better baseball than the Astros lately, and seeing their roles reversed yesterday comes as no surprise to me. The Blue Jays arrived in Texas at the wrong time and with the wrong attitude. It looks like they're running on fumes.
The Jays' bats managed just six hits in this game. Alejandro Kirk and Davis Schneider drove in the team's runs. Schneider hit his fourth home run of the season, a solo shot off Rangers reliever Robert Garcia. Schneider was batting as a pinch hitter at the time.
José Soriano pitched five innings for his team and allowed six runs to the home team, five of which were earned. The Rangers scored all their runs on just five hits throughout the game. When it comes to capitalizing on opportunities, it doesn't get much better than that.
Due to the situation affecting his starting rotation, John Schneider has no choice but to turn to his bullpen for another “bullpen day” today, to close out this series against the Rangers. Spencer Miles will start for his team and face the always tough Jacob deGrom. Spencer Arrighetti will also see action.
Tomorrow, in Baltimore, Trey Yesavage will return to action against the Orioles. A long-awaited—but belated—return.
Everyone knew the race for the playoffs would be exciting in the American League, but Jays fans would certainly have preferred a better scenario than the one we're seeing right now. The final home stand against the Reds is likely to be largely meaningless, much to the chagrin of the team's fans.
- Yankees lose.
- What a play!
- Orion Kerkering to Triple-A.
- Big outing for Brayan Bello, but the Red Sox lost.
- Todd Helton's statue in Colorado.

title: Wilyer Abreu News: Idle Sunday
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Wilyer Abreu News: Idle Sunday

title: Red Sox Get New Willson Contreras Update During Rays Series
author: Keith Watkins
body:
The Boston Red Sox are hoping to get one of their key bats back before the calendar flips to October.
Contreras' Injury and Recovery Timeline
Willson Contreras has been dealing with a hand injury after getting hit by a pitch on his right hand earlier in the week in Texas, an injury that's still visibly swollen and bruised days later. According to Peter Abraham of the Boston Globe, Contreras showed reporters the spot on his knuckles where the pitch connected. "When I got hit, I felt my hand going numb. I thought it was bad because that's a sign of a fracture," Contreras said. "That's why I came off the game."
Initial X-rays came back negative, though further imaging is being held off until the swelling subsides. Contreras sounds confident there's no fracture, drawing on past experience with broken bones to gauge the severity this time around.
The first baseman is hoping to take swings as soon as Sunday, though the nature of the injury complicates things given it's on his top hand, the one that absorbs the shock of contact. He's even considered wearing a protective guard over his batting glove if he does return. With Boston off Monday and playing the Rays again Sunday, Tuesday's game against the Guardians looks like the most realistic target for a potential comeback. "I'm going to take it day-to-day. Of course I want to come back and play with the guys and be there for them," Contreras said. "It's a part of baseball."
Contreras has now been hit by a pitch 24 times this season, tied for third-most in the majors, and 47 times across the last two seasons combined. Much of that stems from how close he stands to the plate, and he's voiced frustration about the pattern, at one point suggesting Boston's pitching staff should retaliate on his behalf.
Willson Contreras has more range of motion when he squeezes his hand today than he did yesterday. It remains a day to day monitoring for improvement. He is fairly confident it isn't fractured. He will do everything he can to play through this once symptoms allow.
— Ian Browne (@IanMBrowne) September 19, 2026
Other Red Sox Injury News
Contreras isn't the only Red Sox player working his way back. Center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela has been out since Sept. 3 with a strained right quadriceps. He faced live pitching for the first time since the injury during a Saturday workout in Worcester. "I felt comfortable," Rafaela said. He still needs to test a full-effort sprint before he's cleared. He plans to attempt that Sunday, with a possible return targeted for Tuesday against Cleveland.
On the pitching side, Tanner Houck continued his rehab from elbow surgery. He worked 3.1 innings in a minor league outing that included two strikeouts and no walks. It was his fourth appearance in that process. He could factor into Boston's bullpen plans for the postseason. Left-hander Garrett Crochet hasn't pitched since April 25 due to shoulder inflammation. He's targeting live hitters early this week, likely at Fenway Park. Whether that's enough to earn a postseason roster spot remains unclear. Right-handed reliever Tyron Guerrero could be activated as soon as Sunday after being out since Sept. 1 with a sore shoulder.

title: MLB roundup: D-backs walk off Yankees on World Series anniversary night
body:
Field Level Media
                
20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.

Field Level Media
                
20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.

Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1

Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.

title: Garrett Crochet Watch Heating Up as Red Sox Enter Final 7 Games
author: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
body:
The Boston Red Sox got another promising day from lefty ace Garrett Crochet on Saturday on his quest back to the big leagues before the 2026 season comes to an end.
Crochet hasn't pitched in a game since April 25 due to shoulder/lat injuries. Since then, he has been working his way back and recently has been throwing bullpens. On Saturday, he tossed his latest over in Worcester at Polar Park. Crochet tossed about 20 pitches and reached 92 miles per hour. On top of this, WooSox pitching coach Dan DeLucia gave Boston fans some hope by saying he looked "great," as shared by Tommy Cassell of the Worcester Telegram and Gazette.
"Crochet, dressed in a full white Red Sox uniform, tossed roughly 20 pitches and sat in the 91 to 92 MPH range," Cassell wrote. "'He looks great,' DeLucia said. 'It was pretty much what we expected. Like, that was the expectation, go out there and kind of make it an in-between side start. No, actually probably a tick above what I think the expectations were, but for the most part, as expected the fine-tuning things, getting on the mound again.'"
The Red Sox Got Another Positive Day From Garrett Crochet
So, what should Red Sox fans make of this?
This is yet another positive. At first glance, the 91/92 MPH fastball may jump out to fans. Of course, that's not up to his peak and is approaching 100 MPH. But that's okay. The fact that DeLucia commented on the throwing session and even said that it was "probably a tick" above what they expected is a sign that he's continuing to make the progress the club has hoped for.
When it comes to Crochet, he has been throwing bullpens for weeks at this point. Earlier in the week, he advanced to a multi-inning up-and-down his last time out. The big lefty followed up on Saturday with a lighter workload. Earlier in the week he got up to 30 pitches and followed with another 20, or so, on Saturday.

title: Benge breaks Mets rookie hits record in victory | Arkansas Democrat Gazette
author: The Associated Press
body:
NEW YORK -- Carson Benge had three hits to break Pete Alonso's Mets season rookie record, homering along with Francisco Alvarez as New York again prevented the Philadelphia Phillies from gaining ground in the National League wild card race with a 10-3 win Saturday.
Benge raised his hits total to 156, one more than Pete Alonso in 2019.
Alec Bohm had a pair of run-scoring singles and Bryce Harper delivered a sacrifice fly for the Phillies, who entered Saturday tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres for the three NL wild cards, five games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Alvarez's three-run home run off Andrew Painter (3-10) put the Mets ahead for good in the fifth.
Benge doffed his cap to an ovation from the crowd of 37,468 following the record-breaking hit, an RBI infield single in the eighth.
CUBS 5, REDS 2 Matthew Boyd ended a six-start winless streak, Dansby Swanson hit his first home run since coming off the injured list and visiting Chicago moved closer to its second consecutive playoff berth by beating Cincinnati. Michael Busch hit a tiebreaking home run off Nick Lodolo (3-6) in the sixth inning for a 3-2 lead, reaching 20 home runs for the third time in four seasons. Swanson added a ninth-inning drive against Zach McCambley, his first since Aug. 12.
NATIONALS 8, CARDINALS 5 (11) Washington scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning to break a 4-4 tie, then worked out of a bases-loaded jam with no outs in the bottom of the inning to get by host St. Louis. Jose Terra hit a two-run double to break the game open, giving the Nationals a 7-4 lead. Dylan Crews' sacrifice fly scored Jacob Young to make it 8-4. JJ Wetherholt hit an RBI single in the bottom of the inning to provide the final margin.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
RANGERS 6, BLUE JAYS 3 Five relievers held Toronto to six hits after Cal Quantrill left 12 pitches in because of right lat tightness, and Texas moved into sole possession of the AL West lead for the first time since late August with a win over visiting Toronto. Texas has won six of seven and moved a half-game ahead of Houston, which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers have a winning record for the first time since before play on Aug. 11.
WHITE SOX 3, TIGERS 1 Sean Burke pitched six effective innings, Miguel Vargas homered and Chicago topped visiting Detroit. The White Sox dropped at least 101 games in each of the last three years. They could become the first big league team to make the playoffs after finishing with at least 100 losses in each of the previous two seasons. Burke (10-7) allowed one run and five hits in his second consecutive win. Grant Taylor got four outs for his 10th save.
RAYS 2, RED SOX 1 Richie Palacios dropped a fly ball into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give Tampa Bay a victory over visiting Boston. The Rays, who've won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth. First, Caminero's foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong's passed ball moved Caminero to third.
GUARDIANS 12, ATHLETICS 6 Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had his second career four-hit game, Chase DeLauter had a three-run home run, and host Cleveland remained in first place in the AL Central with a victory over the Athletics.
INTERLEAGUE
BRAVES 6, ASTROS 3 Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and visiting Atlanta beat Houston to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead. Trailing 2-1, Atlanta loaded the bases against AJ Blubaugh (5-3) and Acuna homered off Bryan Abreu for his second grand slam this season and the fifth of his big league career. Acuna singled and walked twice in his first three plate appearances. He has homered in three of his last four games.
BREWERS 1, ORIOLES 0 Visiting Milwaukee tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds. Hinds lost Joey Ortiz's fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.
PIRATES 6, ROYALS 5 Brandon Lowe hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth to lift host Pittsburgh to a victory over Kansas City. Lowe jumped on a pitch from Steven Cruz (2-4) and sent it into the seats in right field for his 33rd home run of the season, the second-most by a player in their first year with the Pirates.
ROCKIES 5, MARINERS 3 Host Colorado used a four-run seventh inning to earn a victory over Seattle. The Mariners built a 3-0 lead, thanks to a two-run home run from Cal Raleigh in the first and a solo shot from Randy Arozarena in the third. Cole Carigg hit a two-run single in the seventh that gave the lead to Colorado, which got an RBI single from TJ Rumfield to tie the game at 3-3 earlier in the inning.
DIAMONDBACKS 5, YANKEES 3 Pavin Smith hit a two-run home run to right-center field in the bottom of the ninth inning to give host Arizona a victory over New York. Jordan Lawlar's triple in the bototm of the fifth scored Nolan Arenado to give Arizona a 2-1 lead, but Heliot Ramos hit a solo home run in the sixth to tie the game at 2-2. Austin Wells hit a home run later in the inning, giving New York the lead, but Arizona tied the game in the bottom of the inning when Ketel Marte scored on Corbin Carroll's sacrifice fly.

title: Yankees’ division dreams hanging by a thread after walk-off loss: ‘It’s gonna be tough’
author: Gary Phillips
body:
PHOENIX — Both the Yankees and Rays saw their respective games end in walk-off fashion on Saturday, but only one of the division rivals emerged victorious.
It wasn’t the Yanks, who suffered a 5-3 loss to the Diamondbacks when Michael Fulmer surrendered a game-ending, two-run home to Pavin Smith with one out in the ninth inning. Aaron Boone said that he considered using Clarke Schmidt, one game back from Tommy John surgery, instead, but he went with the journeyman Fulmer because he’s had more experience in those situations.
“I just felt like Fulmer’s been in these spots and throwing the ball really well for us, and Smith got him there,” Boone said of the reliever, who has a 3.09 ERA this season.
Meanwhile, at Tropicana Field, the Rays pulled off a 2-1 win over the Red Sox thanks to a bloop single from Richie Palacios in the ninth. Tampa now has a five-game lead over the Yankees with just eight games left in the regular season.
The American League East foes will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium from Sept. 22-24, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday. Boone acknowledged that his club will probably have to sweep the Rays for a crack at a division title.
“We sweep, then it gets interesting,” the manager said with the Yankees’ postseason ticket already punched.
But the odds are already stacked against the Yankees with the team finishing its series in Arizona on Sunday. They entered Saturday with a just a 2.8% chance of winning the division, according to FanGraphs.
Making matters tougher is that the Rays, owners of the AL’s best record, currently lead the season series between the two teams, 6-3. There’s also the fact that the Yankees will be without Aaron Judge, who returned to the injured list with calf strain on Saturday.
“They’re playing tremendous baseball, so it’s tough to climb up in the standings when they keep winning,” Cody Bellinger said after going 0-for-4 on Saturday. “So mathematically, it’s pretty tough, but gotta keep on rolling.”
“We gotta go on a good run. It’s gonna be tough,” added Cam Schlittler, who allowed one earned run over six innings but committed a costly error on Saturday. “I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job with it. So there’s still a chance, but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
The good news for the Yankees is that their best starters are lined up to face the Rays. While they haven’t officially announced their probables for the series, it looks like Max Fried and Carlos Rodón will pitch the doubleheader before Gerrit Cole and Schlittler, the Cy Young frontrunner, close out the four-game set.
The Rays, however, are set to throw a few of their best with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez, Ian Seymour and Freddy Peralta slotted for the highly-anticipated matchup.
While they’re not officially out of the division race yet, the likeliest scenario is that the Yankees end up hosting Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year. It is not where the team wants to end up after finishing 2025 with the same record as the Blue Jays but losing the season series tiebreaker, but Bellinger remained confident that the Yankees can still win their first title since 2009.
“Obviously, the goal is to win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days,” he said. “That’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”

But the odds are already stacked against the Yankees with the team finishing its series in Arizona on Sunday. They entered Saturday with a just a 2.8% chance of winning the division, according to FanGraphs.
Making matters tougher is that the Rays, owners of the AL’s best record, currently lead the season series between the two teams, 6-3. There’s also the fact that the Yankees will be without Aaron Judge, who returned to the injured list with calf strain on Saturday.
“They’re playing tremendous baseball, so it’s tough to climb up in the standings when they keep winning,” Cody Bellinger said after going 0-for-4 on Saturday. “So mathematically, it’s pretty tough, but gotta keep on rolling.”
“We gotta go on a good run. It’s gonna be tough,” added Cam Schlittler, who allowed one earned run over six innings but committed a costly error on Saturday. “I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job with it. So there’s still a chance, but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
The good news for the Yankees is that their best starters are lined up to face the Rays. While they haven’t officially announced their probables for the series, it looks like Max Fried and Carlos Rodón will pitch the doubleheader before Gerrit Cole and Schlittler, the Cy Young frontrunner, close out the four-game set.
The Rays, however, are set to throw a few of their best with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez, Ian Seymour and Freddy Peralta slotted for the highly-anticipated matchup.
While they’re not officially out of the division race yet, the likeliest scenario is that the Yankees end up hosting Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year. It is not where the team wants to end up after finishing 2025 with the same record as the Blue Jays but losing the season series tiebreaker, but Bellinger remained confident that the Yankees can still win their first title since 2009.
“Obviously, the goal is to win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days,” he said. “That’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”

title: Dom Amore’s Sunday Read: Coach that launched Sun has his day; big skates to fill at UConn, and more
author: Dom Amore
body:
Mike Thibault was with the Lakers during the early 1980s “Showtime” period, and he was with the Bulls when they drafted Michael Jordan. Then he moved around to different leagues, circumstances, and went back to the NBA as a Bucks assistant.
In 2003, he signed on to be the head coach the original Portland Fire of the WNBA, but Paul Allen, one of the richest men on earth, folded the franchise. Thibault learned the new Connecticut franchise wanted to talk to him, so he flew across the country, made the long drive in pitch darkness down Route 2 to find a shining city on hill.
“Then I look up and see the bright lights of the Mohegan Sun and the hotel and I thought, ‘Oh, this is different,'” Thibault said. “I stayed in the hotel the night before I was going to talk to them, and I went to the casino and won about $80, and the joke was, I told them, ‘well, if you don’t hire me, at least I got a little bit of your money.'”
All of Thibault’s quips landed and he became the first coach of the Connecticut Sun, leading them to the playoffs the first year, to the WNBA Finals in the second and third.
“It was pretty cool to be a part of that first non-NBA (affiliated) WNBA team,” he said, “having to fend for yourself without the backing of an NBA team in the market. I didn’t have trepidations about coaching women, I figured I would coach them just about the same way I coached men. I had been in the NBA, and then in the CBA, now the G League. I had never given much thought to coaching on the women’s side. But if I stayed in the NBA, I probably would have been a career assistant coach. I wanted to be a head coach. So I said, ‘why not?’ I was at a time in my life where if it wouldn’t be fatal (to my career) if it didn’t work out.”
The Sun made the playoffs in eight of their first 10 years, then let Thibault go after a loss in the conference finals in 2013. He went on to win the championship with Washington soon afterward, and he left The W as the winningest coach in its history, 379-289, though he has been passed by Cheryl Reeve. Now, as the Sun’s final season draws to a close, they will honor Mike Thibault during their second-to-last home game, the last name on the banner in the rafters of the arena noting those who were significant in the team’s history, a history both successful and yet oddly star-crossed.
“I was there 10 years and basically got fired in the midst of a good streak,” Thibault said, “and to be honored by the team, I don’t know that that usually happens in these situations. But I have such good memories of my time there. … The way the organization has handled a tough situation, with their “sunset season” theme, honoring former coaches and players, I think it’s very classy.”
Thibault, 75, now coaches Belgium’s national team, a commitment of 14-15 weeks per year, succeeding the final Sun coach, Rachid Meziane, in that position. Belgium finished fifth in the recent World Cup. Coaching in the WNBA in the summers gave Thibault a chance to settle in Connecticut and be around more for his son, Eric, now the coach of the Mystics, and his daughter, Carly Thibault-Dudonis, who is building an impressive legacy coaching Fairfield’s women. In The W, Mike Thibault was one of those who put a stamp on the league.
“Two teams folded that year, and one team moved to Connecticut,” he said. “But I knew the NBA’s commitment, and I knew David Stern’s commitment. so I didn’t worry about the WNBA not making it. Why not be a part of making something work? A lot of the coaches who came in at that time, Cheryl Reeve, Michael Cooper, Bill Laimbeer had a lasting impact. Before that, a lot of the coaches in the league were former college coaches and it was played more like the college game. The NBA influence brought a good blend, and it started to play more like a pro league.”
Today, he compares the league’s growth to the NBA in the 1980s, about 30 years into its history. “I think the game has gotten better, the talent is better, bigger, stronger, faster, better shooters, better athletes,” Thibault said. “It reminds me, I was in the NBA when it was about 30 years old and it started to take off during the 1980s with the talent level really high. The rules changes have allowed the game to be a little more free-flowing. It’s higher scoring, with the athlete taking over on the offensive side of the game. At times it gets physical, and it will be interesting to see how games are called during the playoffs. So TV is excited about it because it’s a more entertaining game.”
The Orlando franchise had been an underachiever, it was perceived. Thibault took over the roster in Connecticut and said his goal was to compete for the title, and he had Nykesha Sales and Rebecca Lobo for the chase.
“At my first press conference there were snickers when I said my first goal would be to play for a championship,” he said. “Everyone was like, ‘Dude!’ But you have to have that mindset going in. Then making the finals two years in a row. There were a lot of coulda, woulda, shoulda’s in both years. In 2006 I think we had our best team, but we were so injury-riddled and ground down when we got to the playoffs.”
In 2009, the Sun traded star Lindsay Whalen to the Lynx, a most painful moment for Thibault.
“I hated that I had to trade Lindsey Whalen,” Thibault said. “She was like a second daughter in my house. It was time because we couldn’t put enough players around her. But then we got Tina Charles and began the rebuild. We had the second youngest team in the league, the second lowest payroll, I was proud of that group. I got fired basically because I didn’t win a championship, even though we had committed two years earlier to the rebuild.”
Ultimately, Thibault jumped into a league struggling to survive and brought the credibility that helped stabilize a new franchise and the league — so in the larger picture he is more than just a “Sun Legend.” The Sun, purchased for $10 million in 2003, began making a profit in 2010, its location one of the reasons. Now it will go to Houston, having been sold for roughly $300 million.
The countdown is on for Sun’s final game in Connecticut is Sept. 24.
“I was sad,” Thibault said. “I understand it from a business standpoint, the league has changed, the money has changed. The salaries, the amenities you have to have, it’s hard to draw free agents, too. I felt bad for the fans more than anybody. … I thought Boston would have been a good compromise. The most disappointing thing was not winning a championship for our fans, the way they supported us. We gave it our best shot.”
More for your Sunday Read:
Filling iconic skates at UConn
Tia Chan was in goal for the UConn women’s hockey team for so long, playing at such a high level, one could almost call her an icon — rare for a college athlete. Now the Huskies, who reached the NCAA’s Elite Eight last year, have a strong cast of skaters led by high-scoring Claire Murdoch, but will be looking for the next goalie.
“We were worried when Elaine Chuli left (in 2016), we were worried when Morgan Fisher left (in 2020), we were worried when Annie Belanger left (2018),” coach Chris MacKenzie said. “I just think there is going to be someone who is going to step up. It’s happened enough over the 13 years we’ve been here, we’re going to need one of the three we have in there to step up.”
Senior Shannon Moran, freshman Ameilia Wilkinson and sophomore Taylor Belchetz are competing for the starting spot, and all three were expected to see action Saturday in the exhibition game vs. Quinnipiac, also an Elite Eight team, as was Yale.
Among the newcomers for MacKenzie are twin sisters Caileigh and Chelsea Tiller, who could have immediate impact as freshman. The UConn season begins at St. Cloud State Sept. 25.
Warnings from Wesleyan
Wesleyan football coach Dan DiCenso posted a video on social media this week in which he called out the New England Small School Athletic Conference for imposing roster limits on football.
“Football is the only sport in the NESAC with a mandated roster limit,” DiCenso begins. “If all the sports had a mandated roster limit and were making cuts, I would have no problem with it. So this week myself, and three or four schools in this situation, will cut kids from our team. This goes against all of Division III philosophy, all our NESCAC core values (to encourage participation in athletics).”
Wesleyan won the league title with no roster limits in 2024, and again when roster limits were put in for 2025, citing possible competitive advantages, capping at 84 players. DiCenso noted there are sports where there are large disparities between roster numbers.
“Common sense says, if there isn’t a roster limit in any other sport, why is there one in football?” he said. “… Do we want to talk about it? Or do we want to do something about it. I’m tired of having to meet with kids and not be able to give them a good reason why they can’t be on our team — just to practice and be there.”
Sunday short takes
*The Ivy League is moving its men’s basketball championship to Allentown, Pa., in 2028. Big mistake, I say. With the great, historic venues available in the league, most of which are easy for fans to reach, the Ivy’s four-team format was one of the most exciting and enjoyable of the conference tournaments. Messing with happy is never a good idea.
*Sports performance coaches should commission a study of the spotted lantern fly. Have you tried stepping on one? For a bug its size, it has to have the most explosive first step of any creature on earth.
*UConn men’s hockey coach Mike Cavanaugh filled out his staff with director of player development Ryan Shannon, Darien native, former Boston College and pro player and head coach at Taft School. Earlier, Sean Walsh, who also has pro playing experience, came from Alaska-Fairbanks to join Cavanaugh’s staff.
*Yard Goats manager Robinson Cancel will be a bench coach in the Mexican winter league with Tomateros de Culiacan. He will work with, and hopes to learn a lot from Lorenzo Bundy, a long-time MLB coach with a lot of pro managing experiencing.
*Jim Calhoun and his wife, Pat, will be honored by the University of Saint Joseph on Oct. 9 at the Connecticut Convention Center in Hartford. Tickets and details are available on USJ’s website at usj.edu/give/gala for: ‘A Legacy of Leadership. A Gala Honoring Pat and Jim Calhoun,’ the event to benefit the Calhoun Legacy Fund at USJ. Quite a few of Calhoun’s former players are expected.
*Art Shamsky, the 1969 Met, will be the guest at the Hartford World Series Club’s gathering on Sept. 23.
*Jackie Adams-Cheney, John Benoit, Dr. Kelly Harrigan, Robert Kalat, Sara Plourde-Zirkle, Tom Roberts, Don Sourcy and Jillian Sullivan are the Class of ’26 inductees for the Bristol Sports Hall of Fame. The induction ceremony will be Nov. 20 at the DoubleTree in Bristol, go to bshof.org for tickets and info.
*Dan Lauria, SCSU football player in the late 1960s, who turned to acting and gave us that quintessential 60s Dad on The Wonder Years, was inducted into the New Haven Gridiron Club Hall of Fame earlier this month.
Last word
*Cam Schlittler has been great for the Yankees, but any MVP talk is over the top. When starting pitchers threw complete games, they were viable candidates for both Cy Young and MVP, but it would be silly to give the MVP award to a five- or six-inning starter when there are sluggers like Yordan Alvarez flirting with the Triple Crown in Houston or Junior Caminero blowing past 40 homers for Tampa Bay.
