title: How Red Sox’ Tanner Houck fared in final game of rehab assignment
author: Gabrielle Starr
body:
As the Red Sox fell to the Rays 2-1 at Tropicana Field on Saturday evening, wasting an excellent start by homegrown right-hander Brayan Bello, a similar scenario played out between the division rivals’ Triple-A affiliates.
The WooSox lost their penultimate game of the season to the Durham Bulls 4-3 in 10 innings, despite 3 1/3 innings of solid relief work from fellow homegrown Red Sox righty Tanner Houck, who is nearing a return from Tommy John surgery in August 2025.
Houck faced 12 batters, and allowed one earned run and one unearned, on two hits, struck out two and did not issue a walk.
Bulls catcher Tatem Levins scored both runs, but his only true damage off Houck was a one-out 431-foot solo homer in the seventh. Houck’s unearned run came after Sam McWilliams relieved him with one out in the 10th; McWilliams gave up an RBI single to Homer Bush Jr., and Levins scored as the automatic runner.
The Red Sox have not determined next steps for Houck, but they are planning to use him in a relief role. He could be activated during their final homestand, which begins Tuesday versus the Cleveland Guardians.
Houck is the longest-tenured Red Sox major leaguer in the organization, having debuted Sept. 15, 2020. He owns a career 3.97 ERA over six big-league seasons, a mark inflated by his 8.04 ERA in nine starts before the season-ending surgery last year.

title: Crochet, Houck making good progress toward return for Red Sox
author: Ian Browne
body:
Crochet, Houck making good progress toward return for Red Sox
This browser does not support the video element.
ST. PETERSBURG -- While the Red Sox were engaged in a tough battle with the Rays on Saturday, losing 2-1, two of their rehabbing pitchers took steps forward.
Garrett Crochet, the lefty ace who is trying to make it back in time to serve as reliever in the postseason, threw another two-inning side session on Saturday, this one at Polar Park in Worcester, Mass.
If Crochet doesn’t have any ill effects coming out of that session, the Red Sox are hopeful they can have him face hitters at Fenway Park early next week, and perhaps multiple times in the team’s final homestand leading up to the postseason.
“I think it just depends on how he feels coming out of it, how much volume we give him,” said Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy. “So it's hard to say. I know it's not a great answer, but it's just really how it is. How does he feel after each step? So when he does that, how does he feel? And then determine from there. Do we give him more hitters or do we want to put him in a game? It’s hard to say until you know how he feels.”
Meanwhile, righty Tanner Houck made his final rehab appearance for Triple-A Worcester, allowing two hits and two runs (one earned) over 3 1/3 innings. Houck walked none and struck out two as he continued to make progress in his return from Tommy John surgery.
As is the case with Crochet, Houck doesn’t have time to build back up as a starter, but he could be a bullpen option for the Sox in October.
Perhaps Houck could make an appearance or two during the season-ending homestand against the Guardians and Cubs, which starts Tuesday.

title: Rays continue walk-off winning ways against Red Sox
author: Field Level Media
body:
Rays continue walk-off winning ways against Red Sox
(Photo credit: Kim Klement Neitzel)
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as the Tampa Bay Rays edged the Boston Red Sox 2-1 on Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into shallow right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays (94-60) hit their third walk-off winner during the nine-game homestand.
Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece as Tampa Bay improved to 7-1 on the homestand.
Bidding for a fifth consecutive win over five starts, Freddy Peralta received no decision after yielding just one run on four hits over 5 2/3 innings that took 97 pitches. He struck out six and walked two.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox (84-71), who lost for the first time in three games.
Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
The Rays got an out with the infield drawn in and appeared to escape trouble in the third. Then Roman Anthony, who homered and had three RBIs in Friday's 4-2 win in the opener, remained hot and made it 1-0 with a two-out double that scored Durbin.
Cedric Mullins laid down a bunt single and reached second on Durbin's throwing error to open the third, but he was picked off and caught trying to steal third on Jorge Mateo's failed sacrifice bunt.
In the fourth, Aranda tied it 1-all when he rocked his 22nd homer to left field as he took Bello's 97 m.p.h. four-seam fastball the opposite way.
With Bello still in the game in the seventh, Hicks led off with a single and Simpson dropped one into right with no outs. Following a groundout and a fielder's choice, Bello ended the threat by whiffing Mullins on a foul tip.
Durbin lined his second double with one out in the ninth, but Hicks tossed him out trying to steal third. Jarren Duran followed with his fifth triple, but Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to deep third to end the inning off Bryan Baker (4-2).
--Field Level Media

title: Caleb Durbin blows the game for Red Sox with brutal baserunning blunder
author: Darryn Albert
body:
Caleb Durbin managed to do exactly what you do not want to do as the go-ahead run.
The Boston Red Sox played Saturday against the division rival Tampa Bay Rays. In the top of the ninth inning at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. with the score tied 1-1, the Boston infielder Durbin hit a one-out double to represent the winning run.
In the middle of the next at-bat by teammate Jarren Duran however, Durbin committed an inexplicable blunder — he decided to make a break for third base. Durbin was then easily thrown out for the second out of the inning.
Caleb Durbin is caught trying to steal 3rd and Junior Caminero is FIRED UP 
We are still tied in the 9th!pic.twitter.com/wrriTXW1yj
Making matters even worse for Durbin was that Duran proceeded to smack a triple in his at-bat (but was stranded at third after Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to end the half-inning). While Duran’s triple would have allowed Durbin to waltz home if he had simply stayed put, the baserunning error left the game tied and opened the door for the Rays to win the game in the bottom of the ninth inning on a walkoff RBI single by Richie Palacios.
It is hard to tell exactly what Durbin was thinking there. He was already in scoring position and also had a left-handed batter up at the plate (meaning that the catcher had an obstructed throw to third base). Though Durbin has stolen 19 bases so far this season, that was simply a risk completely unnecessary for him to take in that situation.

title: Brayan Bello pitches eight solid innings but Red Sox lose to Rays on walkoff single - The Boston Globe
author: Peter Abraham
body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Brayan Bello, a pitcher who lost his spot in the rotation earlier in this season, did his best to pitch the Red Sox into the postseason on Saturday afternoon, allowing one run over eight innings against the Rays.
But it was not enough.
The Rays walked-off the Sox in the ninth inning with a 2-1 victory before a crowd of 27,402 at Tropicana Field as Richie Palacios had a two-out run-scoring single.
Bello gave up only five hits and struck out 11 — matching his career high — without a walk.
The loss left the Red Sox with a magic number of two.
In a tense game between two teams who could well meet in October, the Sox missed numerous chances to score. They were for 1 for 11 with runners in scoring position and left eight runners on base.
They left a runner on second in the eighth inning and another on third in the ninth.
Facing Garrett Whitlock (7-2) in the ninth inning, Junior Caminero led off with a single — after his potentially playable foul popup struck a catwalk and was ruled a dead ball.
Chandler Simpson singled with one out. A passed ball by Connor Wong moved the runners up. Palacios then won the game with a soft single to shallow right field.
The early innings were a duel between Bello and Rays starter Freddy Peralta.
Peralta retired the first six Red Sox in order, four by swinging strikeout. Caleb Durbin led off the third inning with a double to left field. Jarren Duran sacrificed Durbin to third before Roman Anthony delivered an RBI double to center field.
The Rays tied the game when Jonathan Aranda led off the bottom of the fourth inning with a home run to left field when Bello left a first-pitch fastball over the plate.
Peralta gave up four hits and walked two over 5⅔ innings and 97 pitches but allowed only the one run. The Sox were 1 for 7 with runners in scoring position against him.
Bello had only 68 pitches through six innings. Liam Hicks and Simpson singled on his first two pitches of the seventh inning. With Jonny DeLuca running for Hicks, the runners moved up when Victor Mesa Jr. grounded to second.
With the infield in, Palacios grounded to shortstop. Trevor Story snapped the ball up and fired to the plate to get DeLuca. Bello then struck out Cedric Mullins with a 96.8-mile-per-hour fastball.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

title: Boston's clinch will have to wait after Bello's 11-K gem is spoiled
author: Ian Browne
body:
A brilliant pitching performance by Brayan Bello -- his best of the season -- wasn’t enough. Instead, the Rays earned a hard-fought, 2-1 victory in walk off fashion in the bottom of the ninth on Saturday at Tropicana Field.
Richie Palacios ended it with a bloop single to right against Garrett Whitlock.
Bello was the story for Boston. The righty was dominant and efficient, firing eight innings and 93 pitches while allowing five hits, walking none and tying his career high with 11 strikeouts.
It was the continuation of a strong upward trend for Bello, whose rough first two months of the season landed him back in Triple-A for five weeks.
Roman Anthony continued his solid weekend in his home state by belting an RBI double in the top of the second to break the scoreless tie and stake the Sox to a 1-0 lead.
Jonathan Aranda answered for the Rays in the fourth with an equalizing solo homer to lead off the fourth.
Neither team scored again until Tampa Bay won it in the bottom of the ninth. MVP candidate Junior Caminero caught a break when his seemingly routine foul popup hit one of the catwalks, allowing him to extend the at-bat. He made the most of it, belting a leadoff single to left. Chandler Simpson kept it going with a one-out single.
Palacios did the rest.

title: Red Sox waste dazzling performance by Brayan Bello, get walked off by Rays
author: Gabrielle Starr
body:
Someone only tuning into their first Red Sox game of the season Saturday might not understand the significance of Brayan Bello’s dominant performance against the hosting Tampa Bay Rays.
Particularly as it will be forever marred by a Rays’ 2-1 walk-off victory that keeps Boston’s postseason ticket dangling out of reach for at least another night.
But before that frustrating ending, there was Bello’s hard-earned triumph. It has been a tumultuous year for the homegrown right-hander, who lost his spot in the Red Sox starting rotation at the beginning of May, and pitched his way into a Triple-A demotion the first week of June. Bello dominated in a bulk-relief role from his mid-July recall through early September before the Red Sox gave him another chance to start.
Making his second start of the month on Saturday, Bello turned in not only his best game of the season, but one of the best of his five-year career. He owned his team’s first-place division rivals for eight innings of one-run ball. He yielded just five hits, issued no walks and matched his career-high 11 strikeouts.
“That was exceptional,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters postgame. “By far and away his best outing of the year. As good as I’ve seen him. So, I don’t know what else to say. He was awesome, really awesome.”
Bello’s reward was a no-decision, as the Red Sox lineup went 1 for 11 with runners in scoring position, then lost on Rays second baseman Richie Palacios’ walk-off RBI single in the bottom of the ninth.
Palacios’ game-winning hit came moments after a base-running gamble by Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin that proved calamitous. A glimmer of hope flared when Durbin collected his second double of the day, off Bryan Baker with one out in the top of the ninth. But he was then caught trying to steal third, which proved costly almost instantaneously when Jarren Duran tripled on the very next pitch. Isiah Kiner-Falefa’s inning-ending groundout sent the tie game to the bottom of the ninth.
“I’m OK with it,” Tracy said of Durbin’s attempt to steal. “It’s one-to-one game the whole way, and close play.”
“Hindsight is 20/20,” Tracy continued. “It’s easy in baseball. He gets thrown out, and then Duran has a triple. But you don’t have the privilege of hindsight. So (Durbin) was working hard out there, seeing if he can get the bag, and they got him.”
“I thought I had a window, and probably wasn’t a big enough window,” Durbin told reporters. “I those situations, too, you want to be sure about it. So obviously on me. Not really any excuse other than I gotta be more sure.”
Roman Anthony gave the Red Sox an early lead for the second straight game, doubling off Rays starter Freddy Peralta with two outs in the third. Anthony’s third RBI base hit of the series scored Durbin, who led off the frame with his first double.
But that was all the Red Sox wrote. The home team peppered the middle innings with costly mistakes, but the visitors never took advantage.
Rays centerfielder Cedric Mullins reached safely on a bunt single and advanced to second on a throwing error by Durbin to begin the bottom of the third, but Boston’s third baseman immediately atoned for the miscue by completing a caught-stealing relay with catcher Adley Rutschman and shortstop Trevor Story.
Tampa Bay ran out of ABS challenges by the fourth inning. Shortstop Jorge Mateo burned one on a called Strike 3 from Bello (1.2” Edge Distance) for the second out of the bottom of the third. Peralta lost his team’s remaining bid trying to overturn a Ball 4 with a 2.8” Edge Distance, which put right-fielder Wilyer Abreu on with one out in the fourth.
The worm turned in the bottom of the fourth. Boston’s squandering of a one-out opportunity with Abreu and Nick Sogard (single) on first and second in the top of the inning proved costly immediately when Jonathan Aranda led off the bottom with a first-pitch, game-tying home run.
An undeterred Bello held fast to the knot inning after inning, and looked effortless doing so. Whereas Peralta exited after 5 2/3 innings that required 97 pitches (59 for strikes), Bello needed 55 pitches to complete the first five frames, and his count sat at 68 at the end of the sixth.
When the Rays finally threatened in the bottom of the seventh, the Sox starter was the picture of poise. Unruffled by the back-to-back singles by Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson, Bello retired the next three men in order. The game became his longest of the season as a starter or reliever when he recorded the first out of the seventh, and when he returned to the dugout after finishing the eighth inning, it marked his deepest outing since his complete game on July 8, 2025.
With closer Aroldis Chapman still unavailable due to lat tightness, it fell to righty Garrett Whitlock to pitch the game to extra innings. Whitlock was one strike away from stranding slugger Junior Caminero and Simpson when Palacios sent his 1-2 sinker to right field, where it plunked down in front of Abreu.
The loss means Sunday is the earliest the Red Sox can punch their ticket to October. The current playoff picture has the Red Sox and Yankees meeting in a rematch of last year’s best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium. If Boston gets beyond that, they could see Tampa Bay again.
Saturday’s intensity felt like a preview to the Red Sox. Durbin hopes they can turn the experience into an advantage.
“That was a hell of a baseball game,” Tracy said. “I don’t have really anything negative to say about that game, other than it was really well-played on both sides by both teams. Big moments, and people rose the occasion. It was just a heck of a baseball game, and they were able to beat us.”
“Even yesterday and tomorrow, like they got a little bit of a playoff feel,” Durbin said. “I feel like last year (with the Milwaukee Brewers), first couple playoff games … adrenaline’s way higher. So to get that feel before playoffs even start is super important, because it usually takes a couple games to really settle in. So if we could settle in by Game 1 or 2, that’ll be big for us.”

Rays centerfielder Cedric Mullins reached safely on a bunt single and advanced to second on a throwing error by Durbin to begin the bottom of the third, but Boston’s third baseman immediately atoned for the miscue by completing a caught-stealing relay with catcher Adley Rutschman and shortstop Trevor Story.
Tampa Bay ran out of ABS challenges by the fourth inning. Shortstop Jorge Mateo burned one on a called Strike 3 from Bello (1.2” Edge Distance) for the second out of the bottom of the third. Peralta lost his team’s remaining bid trying to overturn a Ball 4 with a 2.8” Edge Distance, which put right-fielder Wilyer Abreu on with one out in the fourth.
The worm turned in the bottom of the fourth. Boston’s squandering of a one-out opportunity with Abreu and Nick Sogard (single) on first and second in the top of the inning proved costly immediately when Jonathan Aranda led off the bottom with a first-pitch, game-tying home run.
An undeterred Bello held fast to the knot inning after inning, and looked effortless doing so. Whereas Peralta exited after 5 2/3 innings that required 97 pitches (59 for strikes), Bello needed 55 pitches to complete the first five frames, and his count sat at 68 at the end of the sixth.
When the Rays finally threatened in the bottom of the seventh, the Sox starter was the picture of poise. Unruffled by the back-to-back singles by Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson, Bello retired the next three men in order. The game became his longest of the season as a starter or reliever when he recorded the first out of the seventh, and when he returned to the dugout after finishing the eighth inning, it marked his deepest outing since his complete game on July 8, 2025.
With closer Aroldis Chapman still unavailable due to lat tightness, it fell to righty Garrett Whitlock to pitch the game to extra innings. Whitlock was one strike away from stranding slugger Junior Caminero and Simpson when Palacios sent his 1-2 sinker to right field, where it plunked down in front of Abreu.
The loss means Sunday is the earliest the Red Sox can punch their ticket to October. The current playoff picture has the Red Sox and Yankees meeting in a rematch of last year’s best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium. If Boston gets beyond that, they could see Tampa Bay again.
Saturday’s intensity felt like a preview to the Red Sox. Durbin hopes they can turn the experience into an advantage.
“That was a hell of a baseball game,” Tracy said. “I don’t have really anything negative to say about that game, other than it was really well-played on both sides by both teams. Big moments, and people rose the occasion. It was just a heck of a baseball game, and they were able to beat us.”
“Even yesterday and tomorrow, like they got a little bit of a playoff feel,” Durbin said. “I feel like last year (with the Milwaukee Brewers), first couple playoff games … adrenaline’s way higher. So to get that feel before playoffs even start is super important, because it usually takes a couple games to really settle in. So if we could settle in by Game 1 or 2, that’ll be big for us.”

title: Garrett Crochet isn't Red Sox's only looming bullpen savior after Justin Slaten injury
author: Anthony Ranaudo
body:
There's a version of this continuous Boston Red Sox news saga that could have sent fans into a real panic, and I get why. Justin Slaten had quietly turned into one of the more trustworthy arms in this bullpen, working to a 2.84 ERA over his final two months of availability before elbow trouble sidelined him in August.
Now we know the full picture: an evaluation revealed degenerative changes in the flexor mass of his right elbow, and rather than push for a return with the postseason approaching, the Red Sox are having him get a PRP injection and start planning for 2027 instead.
On the year, he had thirty-six appearances, a 4.60 ERA overall, but provided a real chunk of high-leverage relief work, which is now gone for the stretch run. That's a real hole, absolutely. It's also not the whole story right now, and it's worth taking a breath before assuming the bullpen just got worse.
Garrett Crochet was the AL Cy Young runner-up last season, an 18-5, 2.59 ERA workhorse who threw 205.1 innings and struck out 255 batters. What a lot of people forget is that before all of that, Crochet broke into pro ball as a reliever with the Chicago White Sox, sitting comfortably in the upper 90s and regularly touching triple digits in short bursts. That's exactly the version the Red Sox may get back down the stretch.
He hasn't pitched in a game since throwing six scoreless innings on April 25, and after months sidelined with a shoulder issue that turned into more of a lingering problem, he just threw his first bullpen sessions in nearly three months. There isn't time left to stretch him back out as a starter, but a Crochet who can air it out for one to three innings at a time is exactly the profile that's thrived in October before.
Pair that with a Payton Tolle start going five or six innings, Crochet bridging the seventh and eighth, and Aroldis Chapman closing it out, and that's a real, dangerous alignment behind Sonny Gray in a Game 1.
Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo are trending toward returns to Red Sox bullpen alongside Garrett Crochet
Crochet isn't walking through that door alone, either. Tanner Houck is further along than anyone, working back from UCL surgery and already up to three innings and 48 pitches in a rehab outing for Double-A Portland, allowing just one run with four strikeouts, before moving on to Triple-A Worcester to keep building and facing some better competition.
Johan Oviedo, who Boston acquired from the Pittsburgh Pirates over the winter, finally made his own rehab appearance with Worcester this week after missing more than five months with a flexor strain, which is a sign he could factor into the bullpen picture before the year is out. Kutter Crawford is the longer shot of the group, hasn't pitched for the big club since 2024, and there are only unconfirmed "rumblings" he could get a look at Worcester this week. Even if that goes nowhere in 2026, he's still under team control for two more seasons.
Losing Slaten hurts, and nobody should pretend otherwise. But between Crochet, Houck, and Oviedo all trending in the right direction at the same time, Boston may be walking into the stretch run with more usable, high-upside arms than it's had healthy at any single point all season.

title: Red Sox Wrap: Ninth-Inning Breakdown Wastes Brayan Bello Gem | NESN
author: Rodney Knuppel
body:
The Boston Red Sox could not have asked much more from Brayan Bello on Saturday. Unfortunately for Boston, nearly everything around him went wrong at the worst possible moments.
Bello delivered eight outstanding innings, but the Red Sox squandered several scoring opportunities before the Tampa Bay Rays walked off with a 2-1 victory at Tropicana Field. Richie Palacios ended the game with a two-out single off Garrett Whitlock, bringing Junior Caminero home from third base. The loss dropped Boston to 84-71 and evened the three-game series at one victory apiece.
Here are four takeaways from Saturday’s game:
Bello Brilliant In Tough-Luck Start
Bello did everything necessary to earn a victory. The right-hander allowed only one earned run on five hits over eight innings. He did not issue a walk, struck out 11 and threw 65 of his 93 pitches for strikes.
FINAL: Rays 2, #RedSox 1
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 19, 2026
Bello retired the first three batters he faced and struck out seven through his first five innings. Tampa Bay’s only run against him came when Jonathan Aranda opened the fourth inning with a 361-foot home run.
The Rays threatened again in the seventh after singles from Lathan Hicks and Chandler Simpson placed two runners aboard with nobody out. Bello escaped without allowing a run, getting Víctor Mesa Jr. on a groundout, Palacios on a fielder’s choice at the plate and Cedric Mullins on a strikeout.
Bello finished the eighth by retiring Tampa Bay in order. He set down 17 of the final 20 hitters he faced and ended the afternoon with a season-high 11 strikeouts.
Boston Offense Wastes Its Chances
The Red Sox collected eight hits but finished only 1-for-11 with runners in scoring position and stranded eight runners. Boston scored its only run in the third inning. Caleb Durbin opened the frame with a double, advanced to third on Jarren Duran’s sacrifice bunt and scored when Roman Anthony doubled to center field.
That was all the Red Sox produced against Freddy Peralta and four Tampa Bay relievers.
Boston placed two runners aboard in both the fourth and sixth innings without scoring. Adley Rutschman doubled with one out in the eighth, but Wilyer Abreu struck out and Nick Sogard lined out to end the threat.
The most frustrating missed opportunity arrived in the ninth.
Durbin doubled with one out but was caught trying to steal third. Duran then tripled to center field, a hit that almost certainly would have scored Durbin had he remained at second. Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to strand Duran and keep the game tied.
Ninth Inning Unravels On Whitlock
Whitlock entered for the bottom of the ninth after Bello’s terrific afternoon and immediately surrendered a single to Caminero. Whitlock retired Jonny DeLuca before Simpson added another single. A passed ball charged to Connor Wong moved both runners into scoring position, although Whitlock responded by striking out Mesa for the second out.
He could not escape the inning.
Palacios lined a 2-2 sinker into right field, allowing Caminero to score the winning run. The run was unearned because of Wong’s passed ball, but Whitlock took the loss after surrendering three hits in two-thirds of an inning.
MORE: How the Red Sox Can Clinch a Playoff Spot on Saturday
Series Finale Takes On Added Importance
Boston entered Saturday with a chance to take another significant step toward securing its postseason spot after winning Friday’s series opener. Instead, the Red Sox will need to regroup quickly following one of their most frustrating losses of the season.
The defeat dropped Boston to 84-71 and left the Red Sox 10 1/2 games behind the first-place Rays in the American League East. More importantly, it prevented Boston from building additional momentum in the wild-card race.
The Red Sox and Rays will decide the series Sunday at Tropicana Field. First pitch is scheduled for 3:10 p.m. ET.

title: Payton Tolle News: Pushed back to next week
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Payton Tolle News: Pushed back to next week
Tolle no longer appears in line for a start this weekend in Tampa Bay, as the Red Sox are listing Patrick Sandoval as their probable starter for Sunday's game.
As Rob Bradford of WEEI.com points out, Boston appears to be lining Tolle up to start Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. It's a tough blow for Tolle's fantasy managers, as they will take a zero from the lefty this week. He struck out seven over six scoreless innings against Kansas City in his last start Sept. 13, lowering his ERA to 3.02 over 143 innings this season.

title: Red Sox's Game 1 Playoff Starter May Not Be Who You Expect
author: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
body:
We're just over one week away from the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season coming to a close. Then, the entire focus around the league will turn to the playoffs. When it comes to the Boston Red Sox, they will be in the mix.
The Red Sox haven't officially clinched yet, although that could happen as soon as Saturday. As the playoffs have inched closer and closer, one topic that has lingered around Boston is the starting rotation. The rotation is loaded and it's a real question of how the club will sort it out ahead of a Wild Card round series, very likely against the New York Yankees. Sonny Gray has seemed like the likely choice, but that may not be the case.
Could Boston Turn To The Rookie?
Do you roll with the veteran in Game 1? He has been among the best pitchers in the league in general all season to this point. Ranger Suárez has been red-hot recently and was brought to town because of the fact that he has been electric in the playoffs throughout his career to this point. Also, of course, there's Payton Tolle, who is also red-hot right now. On Saturday, Rob Bradford of WEEI shared on X that Tolle actually has a "good shot" at nabbing the Game 1 spot.
"It sure looking like Tolle has a good shot at pitching Game 1 the way they are lining things up," Bradford wrote on X.
Gray has been among the best pitchers in baseball this season. He has a 2.82 ERA and a 146-to-45 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 163 innings pitched this season. Gray also is leading the league with 17 wins. He has been Boston's ace all season. Since Aug. 15, Gray has a 2.89 ERA and a 3-2 record. Since Sep. 4, Suárez has a 0.92 ERA and a 3-0 record. Since Aug. 13, Tolle has a 2.50 ERA and a 42-to-9 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 36 innings pitched across six starts.
Frankly, Boston would be in a good position with any of these three starting Game 1. But in a three-game series, there are even more reasons to get the decision right.
Tolle has made two starts against New York this season and has allowed one run in 13 innings pitched (0.69 ERA) with 18 strikeouts. Gray has made two starts against New York and has allowed three runs in 13 2/3 innings pitched (1.98 ERA) with 12 strikeouts.
Suárez has made three starts against New York and has allowed 11 runs in 16 1/3 innings pitched (5.94 ERA. Of the three, Tolle has fared the best against New York, so the fact that he has a "good shot" at starting Game 1 actually makes a lot of sense.
All three of these guys are red-hot at the moment. Slotting in Tolle for a Game 1, the righty Gray for a Game 2 and then back to a lefty in Suárez for Game 3 — if necessary — arguably is the best bet for a New York series.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

The Red Sox haven't officially clinched yet, although that could happen as soon as Saturday. As the playoffs have inched closer and closer, one topic that has lingered around Boston is the starting rotation. The rotation is loaded and it's a real question of how the club will sort it out ahead of a Wild Card round series, very likely against the New York Yankees. Sonny Gray has seemed like the likely choice, but that may not be the case.
Could Boston Turn To The Rookie?
Do you roll with the veteran in Game 1? He has been among the best pitchers in the league in general all season to this point. Ranger Suárez has been red-hot recently and was brought to town because of the fact that he has been electric in the playoffs throughout his career to this point. Also, of course, there's Payton Tolle, who is also red-hot right now. On Saturday, Rob Bradford of WEEI shared on X that Tolle actually has a "good shot" at nabbing the Game 1 spot.
"It sure looking like Tolle has a good shot at pitching Game 1 the way they are lining things up," Bradford wrote on X.
Gray has been among the best pitchers in baseball this season. He has a 2.82 ERA and a 146-to-45 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 163 innings pitched this season. Gray also is leading the league with 17 wins. He has been Boston's ace all season. Since Aug. 15, Gray has a 2.89 ERA and a 3-2 record. Since Sep. 4, Suárez has a 0.92 ERA and a 3-0 record. Since Aug. 13, Tolle has a 2.50 ERA and a 42-to-9 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 36 innings pitched across six starts.
Frankly, Boston would be in a good position with any of these three starting Game 1. But in a three-game series, there are even more reasons to get the decision right.
Tolle has made two starts against New York this season and has allowed one run in 13 innings pitched (0.69 ERA) with 18 strikeouts. Gray has made two starts against New York and has allowed three runs in 13 2/3 innings pitched (1.98 ERA) with 12 strikeouts.
Suárez has made three starts against New York and has allowed 11 runs in 16 1/3 innings pitched (5.94 ERA. Of the three, Tolle has fared the best against New York, so the fact that he has a "good shot" at starting Game 1 actually makes a lot of sense.
All three of these guys are red-hot at the moment. Slotting in Tolle for a Game 1, the righty Gray for a Game 2 and then back to a lefty in Suárez for Game 3 — if necessary — arguably is the best bet for a New York series.

title: Willson Contreras hopes to get back into Red Sox lineup before the regular season ends - The Boston Globe
author: Peter Abraham
body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Willson Contreras stood at his locker Saturday afternoon and showed reporters the spot where a pitch hit his right hand in Texas on Thursday.
It was on the knuckles between his pinky finger and ring finger, and there was still swelling and a yellow bruise. Contreras could flex his hand but can’t yet grip a bat well enough to hit.
If you didn’t know Contreras was a baseball player, you’d think he was a boxer based on his battered hands.
“When I got hit, I felt my hand going numb. I thought it was bad because that’s a sign of a fracture,” he said. “That’s why I came off the game.”
Contreras is hopeful of getting in a few games before the start of the postseason.
“Hand’s still really sore. Woke up feeling a little better,” he said. “I can squeeze a little better than [Friday], but it’s gonna take a few days.”
The initial X-rays were negative, and any further scans will wait until after the swelling goes down, but Contreras is confident there isn’t a fracture based on his experience.
“I can squeeze a lot better. I’ve had fractures before, and when I have fractures, I couldn’t squeeze,” he said.
Contreras is hoping he can take some swings on Sunday. But because the injury is to his top hand, he has to make sure he can absorb the impact of making contact.
“I’m going to take it day-to-day. Of course I want to come back and play with the guys and be there for them,” he said. “It’s a part of baseball.”
Contreras said he might try using a guard over his batting glove to protect his hand.
The Sox play the Rays on Sunday afternoon and are off on Monday. Contreras could possibly return on Tuesday against the Guardians.
“I’m going to do everything in my power to get back on the field before the playoffs,” he said.
Contreras has been hit 24 times this season, tied for third-most in the majors, and 47 times over last two seasons. It’s largely because he stands close to the plate. But Contreras suggested on Thursday that Sox pitchers should retaliate on his behalf.
“I see, and completely feel and understand Willson’s frustration,” interim manager Chad Tracy said. “He’s been hit close to 50 times the last couple of years so he’s frustrated. Whether he’s referring to the umpires doing something or the pitchers, it’s irrelevant.”
Tracy acknowledged that Contreras crowds the plate. “But there’s a lot of guys that are close to the plate that don’t get hit as much as he does,” he said.
Rafaela progressing
Ceddanne Rafaela, who has been on the injured list since Sept. 3 with a strained right quadriceps, worked out at Worcester on Saturday and faced live pitching for the first time since the injury.
“I felt comfortable,” he said. “My body is rested, and I feel ready to go.”
The last hurdle is to sprint at 100 percent effort, something he will try on Sunday. Rafaela hopes to play against the Guardians on Tuesday.
Crochet could face hitters
Tracy said the goal set for Garrett Crochet would be to face hitters early in the week. That would likely be at Fenway Park before a game. Whether one such session would be enough to merit inclusion on the postseason roster isn’t certain. “Hard to say. I know that’s not a great answer, but it just really is,” Tracy said. … Righthanded reliever Tyron Guerrero could be activated off the injured list as soon as Sunday. He has been out since Sept. 1 with a sore shoulder.
Globe staff writer Alex Speier contributed to this report from Worcester.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

title: Roman Anthony’s underwhelming return to Red Sox from injury shows unfortunate pattern
author: Stephen Parello
body:
It felt like Roman Anthony was an instant star for the Boston Red Sox upon his call-up last season, but the truth of the matter was that it took a while for the hot-shot youngster to truly get going. Over his first 15 major league games, Anthony hit just .114/.291/.272.
The end result was a .292/.396/.463 performance over 71 games. We weren't complaining. It looked like the Red Sox had a perennial All-Star on their hands. Yet, thinking back on those first few games, it might have been the start of a trend.
It's not uncommon for even the best prospects to initially struggle during the first few games of their big league debut, but what has gone on since makes it seem like there's more than meets the eye.
Anthony started 2026 in a miserable slump, hitting just .229/.354/.321 before his finger ligament injury. That almost doesn't tell the whole story, though. The 22-year-old began to turn it on once the calendar flipped to May, with five hits and two walks over 15 plate appearances before landing on the IL.
The Red Sox better hope that Roman Anthony is just a slow starter and that he'll get in gear in time for October
After missing nearly four months, it was as if the youngster was starting his season again from scratch. Initially, he hit the ground running going 10-for-22 over his first five games back. But then he hit a wall. Over his last 11 games, Anthony is hitting just .149/.216/.213. His eagle eye at the plate has disappeared with just a 7.8% walk rate during that span, compared to an alarming 35.3% K-rate.
The struggles have led to calls for him to be dropped lower in the lineup. That might be a temporary solution, but even more important is that he snaps out of his funk soon.
Plenty of players throughout baseball history have gotten off to slow starts only to rebound; some have even made slow starts a habit throughout their careers. Habitually starting off behind the eight ball isn't ideal, but in the grand scheme of things, it's not catastrophic, either.
2026 saw plenty of prominent players get off to ice cold starts. Fernando Tatis Jr. didn't hit until nearly June. Old friend Alex Bregman looked washed with the Chicago Cubs before turning on the jets in the second half. Caleb Durbin no longer looks like a tragic mistake (September struggles, notwithstanding).
Given how long Anthony was on the shelf, it's almost as if he has had two Opening Days. If he truly is a chronically slow starter, that explains away the issues we're currently seeing. He's certainly not worried about it.
“I’m right where I want to be… I came back with enough time to get a good number of plate appearances, and to fail like I am right now and to succeed like I did in the beginning, and then kind of meet in the middle… [The playoffs are] what you play for after such a long year… At the end of the day, those few weeks are the only thing that really matters,” Anthony said.
It almost sounds as if Anthony was planning on this being a process, with the goal of getting back on track for the playoffs. Now, he'll have to make sure that comes to fruition; otherwise, the Red Sox will be in rough shape once the postseason rolls around.

title: ¿Cy Young? Cam Schlittler apunta al MVP de la Liga Americana
author: Carlos Zúñiga
body:
El rol regular de la campaña 2026 de la MLB está por llegar a su final para darle paso a la postemporada, sin dejar de lado las atractivas distinciones individuales para los mejores peloteros del año.
Entre ellos, emerge la figura de Cam Schlittler, el estelar brazo de los New York Yankees que ha pasado de ser un novato en 2025, a ser el máximo candidato para el Cy Young de la Liga Americana este año, acorde con la herramienta de seguimiento de premios MLB de ESPN.
Sin embargo, Cam ahora apunta a una distinción de mayor categoría y los números lo están respaldando seriamente para meterse en la conversación por el MVP de la Liga Americana, y la herramienta de medición es ni más ni menos que Clayton Kershaw, el último pitcher, sea en el joven o en el viejo circuito, que ha obtenido el galardón en las Ligas Mayores.
Las cifras que acercan a Cam Schlittler al histórico MVP que ganó Clayton Kershaw
Este 2026, Cam Schlittler ha puesto números muy cercanos a los que le valieron a Kershaw para ser reconocido como el MVP de la Liga Nacional en 2014. Desde el zurdo que hizo historia con Los Ángeles Dodgers, ningún otro lanzador de tiempo completo ha obtenido el reconocimiento.
| Stat | Cam Schlittler 2026 | Clayton Kershaw 2014 | 
|---|---|---|
| bWAR | 7.0 | 7.7 | 
| ERA | 1.95 | 1.77 | 
| ERA+ | 215 | 197 | 
| K’s | 228 | 239 | 
Estas cifras están presentadas antes de la apertura de Cam Schlittler de este mismo sábado 19 de septiembre frente a los Arizona Diamondbacks, y considerando que a los Yankees aún les restan series ante los Tampa Bay Rays y los Baltimore Orioles, lo más probable es que el franela #31 de los ‘Mulos’ todavía tenga otra salida antes de la conclusión del rol regular de la campaña.
¿Puede realmente Schlittler ganar el MVP de la Liga Americana?
Aunque los números han sido espectaculares para el derecho de 25 años, la propia herramienta de seguimiento de premios MLB de ESPN indica que, en este momento, el favorito para ser reconocido como el jugador más valioso del joven circuito es, con buena diferencia, Yordan Álvarez.
Y no es para menos, el designado de los Houston Astros batea en este 2026 para .312, con un OPS de 1.031, ha pegado 40 palos de vuelta entera, habiendo anotado 98 carreras e impusaldo 99. Cifras hasta antes del segundo juego de la serie de los ‘Space Boys’ ante los Atlanta Braves de este sábado.
Un candidato muy sólido como para que Cam Schlittler aspire a ser reconocido con el MVP, considerando que en el listado de candidatos también aparece otro bate de peso como Junior Caminero, su rival divisional de los Tampa Bay Rays.
Pitchers que han ganado el MVP en MLB
- Clayton Kershaw - Los Ángeles Dodgers | 2014
- Justin Verlander - Detroit Tigres | 2011
- Dennis Eckersley - Oakland Athletics | 1992
- Roger Clemens - Boston Red Sox | 1986
- Willie Hernández - Detroit Tigers | 1984
- Rollie Fingers - Milwaukee Brewers | 1981
- Vida Blue - Oakland Athletics | 1971
- Denny McLain - Detroit Tigers | 1968
- Bob Gibson - St. Louis Cardinals | 1968
- Sandy Koufax - Los Ángeles Dodgers | 1963
- Don Newcombe - Brooklyn Dodgers | 1956

|---|---|---|
| bWAR | 7.0 | 7.7 | 
| ERA | 1.95 | 1.77 | 
| ERA+ | 215 | 197 | 
| K’s | 228 | 239 |

Aunque los números han sido espectaculares para el derecho de 25 años, la propia herramienta de seguimiento de premios MLB de ESPN indica que, en este momento, el favorito para ser reconocido como el jugador más valioso del joven circuito es, con buena diferencia, Yordan Álvarez.
Y no es para menos, el designado de los Houston Astros batea en este 2026 para .312, con un OPS de 1.031, ha pegado 40 palos de vuelta entera, habiendo anotado 98 carreras e impusaldo 99. Cifras hasta antes del segundo juego de la serie de los ‘Space Boys’ ante los Atlanta Braves de este sábado.
Un candidato muy sólido como para que Cam Schlittler aspire a ser reconocido con el MVP, considerando que en el listado de candidatos también aparece otro bate de peso como Junior Caminero, su rival divisional de los Tampa Bay Rays.

title: Red Sox get promising Willson Contreras injury update as postseason nears
author: Gabrielle Starr
body:
On the verge of clinching a postseason berth for the second straight year, the Boston Red Sox have reason to be cautiously optimistic about the health of one of their best hitters.
Though still “pretty sore” from taking a pitch to the right hand on Sept. 17, Willson Contreras no longer believes he suffered a fracture, because he woke up feeling better and had improved range of motion and grip.
“I’m not concerned about having a fracture, just because I can squeeze a lot better today,” the All-Star first baseman told reporters before the team’s Saturday afternoon game at the Tampa Bay Rays’ Tropicana Field. “I had a fracture in my right hand in 2024 by hit-by-pitch, and I couldn’t squeeze at all.”
“But it’s going to take days,” Contreras cautioned.
Contreras’ 24th hit-by-pitch of the season, a 92.3 mph sinker from Rangers’ Jakob Junis to his knuckle in the eighth inning, was a moment of extreme panic for him and the team. Contreras initially went to take his base, but was evidently in severe pain and interim manager Chad Tracy and athletic trainer Dave Herrera quickly removed him from the game.
Though initial imaging was negative, Contreras and Tracy both acknowledged the swelling could be obscurative, with the former telling reporters postgame, “It felt like a fracture.”
“When I got hit, I felt my hand going numb, and I thought it was bad, because that’s a sign of a fracture,” Contreras said on Saturday. “And it was like, tingling for like five minutes.”
Contreras will try to grip a bat on Sunday, and if so, try to do some cage work. He is champing at the bit to get back in games before the postseason begins. He has soared to new heights in his 11th big-league season and first with the Red Sox, putting up career-best marks in his .905 OPS, 59 walks, 81 RBI, and 27 home runs (129 games).
“I’m dying to go out and play with the guys and be there for them,” Contreras said. “It’s part of baseball; I’ll do everything in my power to get back on the field.”
“You don’t want to get to the playoffs without playing any games,” he said. “I want to do everything in my power to get back on the field before the playoffs. If it happens, it happens. If it doesn’t happen, we’ll see what happens.”
Contreras is one of several injured stars the Red Sox are eager to have back as they careen toward October baseball. Gold Glove centerfielder Ceddanne Rafaela last played Sept. 2 before going on the injured list with a right quad strain. Though it’s unlikely Rafaela will get into a Triple-A Worcester game before their season ends on Sunday, interim manager Chad Tracy described him as “moving quickly in the right direction,” and said the goal is for him to get “live BP-type at-bats of some kind, plus the Trajekt (pitching machine).”
All-Star closer Aroldis Chapman is not on the IL, but remains day-to-day due to the lat tightness he felt during a workout before Tuesday’s game in Texas. Though unavailable for this weekend’s series in Tampa, he told reporters there (through a team translator), “I’m not worried at all. … I feel very good. I was going to go out and throw, but the team wants to take it slow, and they want me to take my time.” Chapman plans to get back in games during the team’s final homestand, which begins Tuesday versus the Cleveland Guardians.

title: ‘Drug Kingpins Don’t Order Hits On Nobodies’ | Fans Call Out MLB Legend David Ortiz For Involvement With Predatory Dominican Moneylender Santo Caraballo
author: Devon POV Mason
body:
Baseball Hall of Famer and three-time World Series champion David “Big Papi” Ortiz is in some hot water with fans. The Boston Red Sox legend and ten-time MLB All-Star is being called out for his dealings with a Dominican lender.
Ortiz is tied to Dominican baseball high-interest lenders through multi-million-dollar investments with lender Santo Caraballo. The las prestamistas system in the Dominican Republica connects impoverished parents of talented young baseball prospects with lenders who will extend high-interest loans up front against the boys’ future baseball bonuses.
A new report from ProPublica shows “Big Papi,” as he’s affectionately known, has invested millions into lender Caraballo’s baseball business.
Ortiz In Pretty Deep With Carabello
According to other reports Ortiz co-founded Florida-based Big Papi Sports Group in 2021. Ortiz also reportedly opposed reforms targeting high-interest loans tied to young prospects. All of this while denying he knowingly exploited players, claiming loans targeted trainers, not kids. 
Nearly 80 percent of Dominican MLB bonuses have attached high-interest loans. In the legal landscape of it all the Dominican Republic repealed usury laws 24 years ago.
Ortiz Lawyer Releases Statement On His Behalf
In an attempt to clarify his relationship with Caraballo, Ortiz had his lawyer attempt to do damage control with a statement.
In a statement sent to Pro Publica through his lawyer, Ortiz said that his business relationship with Caraballo “began to come to an end” more than 18 months ago.” He added that he ended his personal relationship with Caraballo “a year and a half to two years ago” after “noticing conduct by Mr. Caraballo that I considered inappropriate. I started distancing myself from him personally and placed the relevant matters in the hands of my legal advisors.”
Fans Come For Big Papi
“This guy’s been dancing his fat ass through the raindrops for decades. Started with him being implicated on the positive HGH list with no consequences. Screw this criminal miscreant,” a fan said.
“David Ortiz has always been a cheating POS. Drug kingpins don’t order hits on nobodies,” another fan said.
“Great reporting on a mess that MLB needs to address. Praying on the poor and illiterate in trying to farm kids into players. Despicable,” a fan commented.
“Ortiz always seemed like an MLB Jester to me. Paraded on camera, approved by owners. It never seemed natural,” someone else said.
“Been telling my family for years this guy is a phony – never bought his act,” a person mentioned.
“Made it out and pulled the ladder up behind him instead of building a staircase for everyone else to walk up,” a fan quipped.
“Wow. This should be a bigger story,” another fan spewed.
How Will Ortiz Spin This In His Favor?
The legendary slugger will attempt to frame the ProPublica Investigation on Dominican youth baseball as grassroots survival rather than exploitation. The Red Sox playoff hero already leans on the real economic vacuum in the Dominican Republic — asking who feeds, clothes, and equips a 13-year-old if trainers don’t step up.
He will likely spin dismissing percentage-of-bonus agreements as standard high-risk risk-capital (“it’s a business deal”) rather than predatory lending. Ortiz will definitely lean on his massive philanthropic footprint (David Ortiz Children’s Fund) and cultural ambassador status to humanize his involvement.

title: Chicago Cubs Announce Sudden Alex Bregman Change Before Reds Game
author: Jose Esquer
body:
On Saturday night, the Chicago Cubs will continue their series against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park.
Most recently, the Cubs lost 6-4 on Friday.
Third baseman Alex Bregman went 0-for-5 in the loss.
Chicago Cubs Announce Alex Bregman Change
Ahead of Saturday’s game, the Chicago Cubs have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB posted on X: “Cubs 9/19 P. Crow-Armstrong CF A. Bregman 3B S. Suzuki DH T. Taylor LF N. Hoerner 2B M. Busch 1B C. Kelly C M. Shaw RF D. Swanson SS M. Boyd SP”
After batting cleanup in Friday’s loss, Alex Bregman has been moved up in the team’s lineup and will bat second against the Reds on Saturday.
It will mark the first time Bregman has been in the No. 2 spot over the past 59 games. During that span, Bregman has alternated between the third and fourth spot in the lineup.
Bregman has appeared in the No. 2 spot 41 times this season. Out of that spot, Bregman is batting .217 in 191 plate appearances.
Overall, the three-time All-Star is batting .262 with 156 hits, 32 doubles, 26 home runs, three triples, 88 runs, 88 RBIs and three stolen bases in 151 games.
Prior to the season, Alex Bregman signed a five-year, $175 million contract with the Chicago Cubs.
Cubs Right Now
After dropping the series opener, the Chicago Cubs are now tied with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres for the top Wild Card spot in the National League. Chicago owns the tiebreaker over both teams. The Cubs have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games.
Left-hander Matthew Boyd is set to make his 21st start of the season. He enters Saturday’s outing with an 8-5 record and a 4.16 ERA in 114.2 innings. Boyd took the loss in his last start as he allowed four runs against the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Reds Right Now
Meanwhile, the Cincinnati Reds have also announced their starting lineup forr the second game of the series.

Underdog MLB posted on X: “Reds 9/19 D. Myers CF E. De La Cruz SS S. Stewart 1B T. Stephenson C E. Suárez DH J. Brito RF J. Bleday LF M. McLain 2B K. Hayes 3B N. Lodolo SP”
At 72-82, the Cincinnati Reds have officially been eliminated from playoff contention. They have gone 3-7 over their last 10 games.

title: Yankees vs. Diamondbacks prediction, odds: Cam Schlittler to further Cy Young case
author: Dylan Svoboda
body:
Cam Schlittler will take the mound Saturday in Arizona against the Diamondbacks as he looks to put the finishing touches on a Cy Young-caliber 2026 campaign.
The Yankees’ star has been nearly unhittable all season, but he has been even more dominant of late, keeping hitters at bay as he builds momentum heading into October.
Batters are hitting just .185 against Schlittler this season, which is second-best in the American League, but he’s holding them to an even more ridiculous rate over the past month-plus.
Schlittler has allowed just 21 hits over 45 innings over his last seven starts, helping him post a sparkling 1.00 ERA over that stretch and all but locking up the Cy Young award in the junior circuit, while also vaulting him into the MVP conversation (14-6, 1.95 ERA, 215 strikeouts).
In his last start, he allowed just one hit over six innings against a Mets lineup that has shown some life lately.
Over two starts before that outing, Schlittler allowed just five total hits over 15 innings against the Angels and Rockies.
The D-backs provide a tougher task than his recent opponents, having been an above-average offensive team all season, but Schlittler will at least have the advantage of unfamiliarity.
Learn all you need to know about MLB Betting
- Read about the Best Baseball Betting Sites
- Learn all about How to Bet on Baseball
Only one batter on Arizona’s roster has ever faced Schlittler in a big league game – Jesus Sanchez, who just joined the Diamondbacks this week and may not even see the field Saturday.
That should only make things more difficult for the snakes against one of baseball’s toughest pitchers to square up right now.
The play: Cam Schlittler Under 4.5 hits allowed (-168, DraftKings)

title: Boston Red Sox Drop Nick Sogard During Rays Series
author: Cole Shelton
body:
The Boston Red Sox dropped Nick Sogard in the lineup in the second game of a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Boston is coming off a 4-2 win over the Rays in the series opener, in a game where Sogard went 0-for-5 while hitting second.
The Red Sox are 84-70.
Boston Red Sox Drop Nick Sogard
Ahead of the second game of the series, Boston dropped Sogard in the lineup after his 0-for-5 night.
Sogard is playing first base as Willson Contreras remains out. Yet, his spot in the order is different, as he is now hitting fifth.
The Red Sox lineup on Saturday against the Rays is as follows:
- R. Anthony LF
- M. Gasper DH
- A. Rutschman C
- W. Abreu RF
- N. Sogard 1B
- T. Story SS
- C. Durbin 3B
- J. Duran CF
- I. Kiner-Falefa 2B
Sogard has struggled at the plate as of late, as he's now been dropped to fifth in the order. He's hitting .255 with 5 home runs and 19 RBIs. However, in his last 7 games, he's hitting .167 with 1 home run and 3 RBIs, while striking out 5 times.
First pitch on Saturday is set for 4:10 p.m. ET.
Boston Right Now
Boston is firmly in the second Wild Card spot in the American League.
The Red Sox are closing in on a playoff berth, and it could happen on Saturday depending on some outcomes.
"I think everybody does, for sure," said interim manager Chad Tracy. "We came out and looked really good offensively in the first part of that game, and there was a lot of energy in the dugout. And I think guys feel it. We're not done yet, but I definitely think they sniff it, and we're wanting to get there for sure."
Although Boston is likely to make the postseason, the Red Sox haven't clinched, so they aren't talking about anything yet.
"When we clinch, I want to be able to [celebrate]," said Ranger Suarez. "But mathematically, we're not there yet, so I'm not thinking about that yet."
Boston will likely face the New York Yankees in the Wild Card round for the second straight year.

title: How Should Boston Red Sox Set Playoff Rotation?
author: Zach Coe
body:
Sonny Gray? Ranger Suarez? Payton Tolle? Who should get the ball in game one in the Bronx for the Red Sox?
To manage the starting rotation workload and line up the rotation for the playoffs, the Boston Red Sox are turning to Brayan Bello to start Saturday's game against the Tampa Bay Rays. Whether the Red Sox go with Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, or Payton Tolle, the team will feel very good about its chances of winning. However, if the team gets swept, it risks leaving an incredible arm on the bench.
Let's take a look at the argument for each of the trio to get the ball in game one:
Gray
The 36-year-old veteran has inarguably been the Red Sox' best starter in 2026. After entering the season with questions about how effective he could be late in his career, Gray has passed every test with flying colors. In 28 starts, Gray has posted a 2.82 ERA, the eighth-lowest mark in the league, while the Red Sox have gone 20-8 on his start days.
Most importantly, even when he doesn't have his best stuff, he has done well to limit damage; of his 28 starts, he has allowed more than three runs on four occasions. In two starts against the New York Yankees in 2026, Gray has allowed only three earned runs on nine hits, while striking out 12 and walking only four. In his career, Gray has a solid record of playoff success, posting a 3.26 ERA in 30.1 innings.
However, when it comes to elite strikeout stuff that can completely shut down a lineup, Gray lacks that, posting a rather pedestrian strikeouts per nine innings of 8.06, which ranks 30th out of 48 qualified starters.
Still though, Gray appears to be the most obvious choice to get the start in game one.
Suarez
The Red Sox' most difficult decision with their postseason rotation may be the one they have to make with Suarez. The 30-year-old All-Star signed a five-year, $130-million deal with the Red Sox in the offseason, in part because he posted an impressive 1.48 ERA over 42.2 innings with the Philadelphia Phillies.
However, of the trio in consideration, Suarez has been the shakiest since the All-Star break, posting a 3.46 ERA in his last 10 starts. However, the three-time All-Star has been better lately, allowing only two earned runs in 19.2 innings across three starts. Suarez has struggled against the Yankees in three starts in 2026, allowing 11 runs on 20 hits for a 6.06 ERA.
Still, it seems unlikely the team would risk leaving its $130 million investment on the sidelines for a playoff series.
Tolle
The 23-year-old rookie has been Boston's best starter since the All-Star break. In his last 10 starts, Tolle has posted a 2.90 ERA while striking out 12.05 batters per nine innings, the fifth-highest mark among 93 pitchers with at least 50 innings pitched.
Tolle has also performed incredibly well against the Yankees, allowing only one earned run on four hits while striking out 18 and walking only four. Tolle is also the only pitcher on the Boston staff with the electric stuff that could match New York ace Cam Schlittler in shutting down the lineup.
While it certainly may seem risky to some to give a 23-year-old rookie the ball in game one in Yankee Stadium, how can you risk not throwing him at all?
Up next for the Sox
With their magic number down to two, the Red Sox will look to win a series against the likely American League East champion Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday afternoon. Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.74 ERA) will get the start for Boston opposite Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA) will start for Tampa. First pitch from Tropicana Field is set for 4:10 p.m. ET.

title: Red Sox Have New Reason to Be Hopeful on Willson Contreras' Hand
author: Jackson Roberts; Unknown
body:
The Boston Red Sox could punch their ticket to the playoffs on Saturday, but health remains a bigger story with this club than the mechanics of a clinching scenario.
Ironically, as the Red Sox look to be locked into a first-round matchup against the New York Yankees, both archrivals are missing their best hitters. The Yankees placed Aaron Judge on the 10-day injured list with a calf strain on Friday, but the Red Sox are still waiting for clarity about Willson Contreras.
On Saturday, we learned that Contreras is at least somewhat on the mend after wearing a pitch to the left hand during Thursday night's game with the Texas Rangers. That's no guarantee of any time frame for a comeback, but it's definitely something positive to take from the day.
Latest update on Contreras sounds promising
According to Red Sox insider Ian Browne of MLB.com, Contreras saw an improvement in his condition from Friday to Saturday. That wasn't a guarantee that his hand avoided a fracture on the hit-by-pitch during Thursday's eighth inning, but Contreras sent a positive indication in that regard as well.

title: Red Sox believe Sonny Gray could retire after this season — and Yankees could be final game
author: Dylan Svoboda
body:
The 2026 season could end up being Sonny Gray’s last.
The veteran right-hander, who turns 37 in November, has not committed to pitching in 2027 and recently told The Boston Globe he would retire “in a heartbeat” if his family wanted him to do so.
Boston reportedly is taking the possibility seriously, according to the outlet, with some in the organization believing retirement is on the table despite Gray’s strong season.
Asked recently about the possibility of retirement, Gray declined to say much.
“We can get into that at another time but not right now,” he said, per the Globe.
If 2026 is, indeed, his final big league season, Gray’s final start could come in the increasingly likely matchup against the rival Yankees during the wild-card round of the postseason.
Gray spent a season and a half in pinstripes after coming over before the 2017 trade deadline, and it didn’t go exactly as planned for either him or the team.
The three-time All-Star posted a 4.51 ERA across 41 games (34 starts) with the Yankees before being traded to Cincinnati before the 2019 season, during which he posted a Cy Young-caliber season with the Reds.
Gray ripped the Yankees during his introductory press conference with the Red Sox over the winter.
“It feels good to me to go to a place where it’s easy to hate the Yankees,” Gray said.
“I never wanted to go there in the first place.”
Gray is enjoying one of the best seasons of his 14-year MLB career in Beantown, posting a 2.82 ERA in 163 innings.
“I’ve very, very much so enjoyed Boston. Enjoyed the guys. Fenway has been, and is, a very special place,” Gray said.

title: Red Sox ace Crochet throws side session at Polar Park before WooSox game
author: Tommy Cassell
body:
Red Sox ace Crochet throws side session at Polar Park before WooSox game
WORCESTER — Garrett Crochet threw a baseball at Polar Park Saturday.
Four hours before the WooSox hosted the Durham Bulls (Tampa Bay Rays AAA club), the Red Sox star left-handed pitcher threw a side session as he continues his rehab from a left shoulder injury.
Crochet, dressed in a full white Red Sox uniform, tossed roughly 20 pitches and sat in the 91 to 92 mph range.
“He looks great,” WooSox pitching coach Dan DeLucia said. “It was pretty much what we expected. Like, that was the expectation, go out there and kind of make it an in-between side start. No, actually probably a tick above what I think the expectations were, but for the most part, as expected the fine-tuning things, getting on the mound again.
“(We had) one of the coaches stand in (in the batter’s box) and he still just needs to fine-tune things, and that takes some time, but the outputs look pretty good. Like, how the body’s moving and all that looks pretty good.”
Crochet (3-3, 6.30 ERA with 37 strikeouts in 30 IP) last pitched for the Red Sox on April 25 in a game against the Baltimore Orioles. He was placed on the 15-day injured list four days later (retroactive to April 26) and transferred to the 60-day IL on June 5.
While meeting with media members in St. Petersburg, Fla. Friday, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy wasn’t clear on the next steps for Crochet moving forward as the Red Sox wrap up their regular season a week from Sunday.
Crochet is attempting to come back to help Boston out of the bullpen for their likely upcoming playoff series against the New York Yankees.
“It’s hard to say. If everything goes well Saturday, then you kind of determine what that looks like at the beginning part of next week,” said Tracy, according to Sean McAdam of MassLive. “I’d say we’re at a point where these next five days are going to be pretty telling. How does the side go and what can we do with him at the start of next week? That will give us a better idea.”
With fellow Red Sox pitcher Tanner Houck scheduled to pitch for Triple-A Worcester later in the day in a rehab assignment, both Crochet and Houck — and starting center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who hit living pitching at Polar Park pregame Saturday as he continues his recovery from a right quadriceps strain — present possible reinforcements for the Red Sox as they look to make a run in the playoffs.

title: Game 155: Red Sox at Rays lineups and notes - The Boston Globe
author: Matty Wasserman
body:
The Red Sox enter Saturday with the opportunity to clinch a postseason berth.
In Friday’s series opener, Roman Anthony hit the longest home run of his career en route to a 4-2 victory, which snapped Tampa Bay’s six-game winning streak.
The Sox’ magic number is down to two following the win. Two scenarios would secure a postseason berth for Boston on Saturday: A Sox victory and Blue Jays victory over the Rangers, or a Sox victory, Blue Jays loss, and Braves win over the Astros.
The Sox will turn to righthander Brayan Bello, who pitched 1 ⅔ scoreless innings out of the bullpen in his last appearance against Texas on Tuesday.
Righthander Freddy Peralta will take the mound for the Rays. He faced the Sox on July 11 while a member of the Mets, allowing two runs on three hits in 4 ⅓ innings.
Here’s a preview.
RED SOX (84-70): Anthony LF, Gasper DH, Rutschman C, Wilyer Abreu RF, Sogard 1B, Story SS, Durbin 3B, Duran CF, Kiner-Falefa 2B
Pitching: RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.74 ERA)
RAYS (93-60): Diaz DH, Aranda 1B, Caminero 3B, Hicks C, Simpson LF, Mesa Jr. RF, Palacios 2B, Mullins CF, Mateo SS
Pitching: RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA)
Time: 4:10 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Red Sox vs. Peralta: Wilyer Abreu 0-5, Willson Contreras 7-26, Jarren Duran 3-7, Caleb Durbin 1-1, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 4-9, Andruw Monasterio 1-1, Adley Rutschman 0-3, Nick Sogard 0-2, Trevor Story 1-9, Connor Wong 1-2
Rays vs. Bello: Jonathan Aranda 6-19, Junior Caminero 1-9, Jonny DeLuca 0-2, Yandy Diaz 8-21, Jake Fraley 3-5, Nick Fortes 1-5, Liam Hicks 0-3, Richie Palacios 0-2, Jorge Mateo 2-7, Cedric Mullins 4-16, Chandler Simpson 1-3, Taylor Walls 2-17
Stat of the day: Opponents were batting .280 off Peralta’s changeup with the Mets, but they’ve hit .097 off it over the last month.
Notes: Peralta posted a 4.99 ERA in 22 starts with the Mets, but since being acquired by Tampa Bay on Aug. 2, he’s posted a 3.86 ERA in eight starts. Over his past four outings, he’s allowed just two runs on 10 hits, with 17 strikeouts and a 0.78 ERA … Willson Contreras remains day-to-day after getting hit on the right hand in Thursday night’s victory at Texas, and the Sox are confident he dodged a serious injury. Tracy said Friday he would not rule out Contreras playing this weekend …. The Sox enter Saturday 5½ games behind the Yankees for the first wild card spot. The Yankees trail Tampa Bay by 4 games for the AL East division lead.

title: What do the Red Sox need vs Rays to seal a 2026 MLB playoff berth today, Sep. 19?
author: Matías Persuh
body:
The Boston Red Sox have been one of the major storylines in the AL East right up until the final stretch of the season. Behind the Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees, the team managed by interim manager Chad Tracy needs a series of results to secure a Wild Card berth and keep its postseason hopes alive.
Beating the Rays on the road at Tropicana Field is a must. On top of that, the Red Sox need either the Texas Rangers or the Houston Astros to lose their game in order to finally punch their ticket to the postseason.
Both the Rangers and the Astros will play at home in the evening. Texas will host the Toronto Blue Jays at Globe Life Field, while Jose Espada’s team will welcome the Atlanta Braves to Daikin Park.
Boston wants to return to the World Series
The Boston Red Sox are itching to make a serious Fall Classic run, aiming to bring the Commissioner’s Trophy back to Fenway for the first time since their dominant 2018 championship. Sitting at an impressive 84-70 record late into the campaign, the club has completely revitalized its season under manager Chad Tracy, who took the helm and turned things around after a rough start.
Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox.
With the squad clicking at the right time and buying into Tracy’s energetic leadership, Boston looks ready to cause standard postseason chaos and prove they belong back on baseball’s biggest stage.
More chances to clinch a postseason spot
If the Red Sox can’t lock up their Wild Card spot today against Tampa Bay, they still have plenty of chances left on the schedule to seal the deal. They’ll wrap up their road trip at Tropicana Field on Sunday against the Rays before returning home for a critical six-game homestand to close out the regular season.
BoSox will host a three-game series against the Cleveland Guardians mid-week, followed by a final three-game Interleague matchup against the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park from September 25-27. With those remaining games right in front of their home crowd, the Red Sox hold their postseason destiny firmly in their own hands.
original_title: What do the Red Sox need vs Rays to seal a 2026 MLB playoff berth today, Sep. 19?
original_body:
The Boston Red Sox have been one of the major storylines in the AL East right up until the final stretch of the season. Behind the Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees, the team managed by interim manager Chad Tracy needs a series of results to secure a Wild Card berth and keep its postseason hopes alive.
Beating the Rays on the road at Tropicana Field is a must. On top of that, the Red Sox need either the Texas Rangers or the Houston Astros to lose their game in order to finally punch their ticket to the postseason.
Both the Rangers and the Astros will play at home in the evening. Texas will host the Toronto Blue Jays at Globe Life Field, while Jose Espada’s team will welcome the Atlanta Braves to Daikin Park.
Boston wants to return to the World Series
The Boston Red Sox are itching to make a serious Fall Classic run, aiming to bring the Commissioner’s Trophy back to Fenway for the first time since their dominant 2018 championship. Sitting at an impressive 84-70 record late into the campaign, the club has completely revitalized its season under manager Chad Tracy, who took the helm and turned things around after a rough start.
Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox.
With the squad clicking at the right time and buying into Tracy’s energetic leadership, Boston looks ready to cause standard postseason chaos and prove they belong back on baseball’s biggest stage.
More chances to clinch a postseason spot
If the Red Sox can’t lock up their Wild Card spot today against Tampa Bay, they still have plenty of chances left on the schedule to seal the deal. They’ll wrap up their road trip at Tropicana Field on Sunday against the Rays before returning home for a critical six-game homestand to close out the regular season.
BoSox will host a three-game series against the Cleveland Guardians mid-week, followed by a final three-game Interleague matchup against the Chicago Cubs at Fenway Park from September 25-27. With those remaining games right in front of their home crowd, the Red Sox hold their postseason destiny firmly in their own hands.
