title: The Red Sox took great pains to build depth in the offseason, and the results are paying off - The Boston Globe
author: Alex Speier
body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — For the Red Sox, the vision of contention in 2026 seemed straightforward.
The team’s championship window had been pried open by the presence of a pair of cornerstones, with Garrett Crochet anchoring the rotation and Roman Anthony representing a lineup anchor not only for this year but several seasons to come.
But while the Sox are amid a magic-number countdown to a playoff berth, they’ve done so without Anthony and Crochet for most of the year. Their season has been saved in no small part by players who have emerged from obscurity to play critical roles — with essential contributions coming from Andruw Monasterio, Anthony Seigler, Mickey Gasper, Tsung-Che Cheng, Jahmai Jones, Tyron Guerrero, and more.
“I don’t think anybody had that on the drawing board,” said interim manager Chad Tracy with a chuckle. “They were asked to play a lot, and they produced. And if they didn’t, we were in trouble. It’s a huge piece of the 2026 season, no question.”
Of course, while no one expected the outsized impact of players who began the year as big league backups or in Triple-A, the Sox also took considerable pains to build organizational depth through a variety of transactions.
Whether it was an expanded version of the trade that brought Caleb Durbin from Milwaukee to include Monasterio and Seigler, or waiver claims of Cheng and Gasper, or a minor league deal for Guerrero, the season has been a case study in the notion that perceived little moves can have a huge impact.
“Every move and every decision matters,” said assistant general manager Mike Groopman, who oversees the team’s acquisitions group. “The big ones, whether it’s a larger free agent deal, [or] a larger, more high-profile trade, is naturally going to get a lot of attention.
“I don’t think this is unique to the Red Sox. There are 29 other teams that try to and do a very good job about caring about the ‘little’ things. But I think what we really try to reinforce is … that year over year, around the game, you see things that seem ‘little’ that end up being really impactful and big. [Deals that] seemed like small moves at the outset end up having a much, much larger impact commensurate with what would have been perceived at the time as a ‘larger’ move.”
Players who evolve from theoretical depth to become big league contributors excite numerous corners of an organization. The primary credit for those contributions, of course, belongs with a player, but they still often represent the combined efforts of personnel in scouting who identify the player’s potential contributions, player development personnel who help the player build on preexisting strengths and abilities in the minors, and big league staffers who help the players to perform at the game’s highest level.
Take Guerrero. After brief stints in the big leagues in 2018 and 2019, he’d become a journeyman, shuffling between organizations — and countries — but unable to forge a way back to the big leagues despite elite velocity.
But the Sox — who’d been interested in signing Guerrero before he pitched in the NPB in Japan in 2025 — remained intrigued, thanks in part to strong scouting recommendations from Kento Matsumoto in Japan and Manny Nanita in the Dominican Winter League. After they signed Guerrero to a minor league deal in the offseason, player development officials worked with him on some minor grip changes that unlocked significantly improved command with a sinker that regularly reached triple digits.
Guerrero’s dominance this year in Triple-A (0.92 ERA) essentially forced the Sox to call him up, and the 35-year-old emerged as a late-innings force from late June to late August (before shoulder fatigue led to a bad outing followed by a trip to the injured list), posting a 2.13 ERA over a 23-appearance stretch.
Again, the lion’s share of the credit goes to Guerrero for the work he did to fight his way back to the big leagues. But his emergence embodies the sort of under-the-radar acquisition that helped save the Sox’ season.
“The connection and integration between acquisition and development is really important,” said Groopman. “Guerrero and our [player development] group put a lot of time into [those changes] in the spring and the early season, to get him to a point where he was able to lock in some of these changes and unlock what was super obvious arm talent into something that was translating more consistently onto the major league mound.”
Of course, talent alone doesn’t dictate success once a depth player gets to the big leagues. They must also have the opportunity to contribute — and, in many cases, the freedom to fail while getting their bearings.
Tracy, who spent time with nearly all of this year’s depth contributors in Triple-A at the beginning of the year, has been mindful of creating an environment in which call-ups can contribute.
“I’m in the same boat [as them]. I want the freedom to go manage the game [as a first-time big league manager],” said Tracy. “I need to manage a game and feel like if I do something that doesn’t go right, it’s not the end of the world. If I feel that way, then I want the player to feel like, ‘Hey, if you go out there and play second base today and you make an error, move on to the next play.’
“If the culture becomes, ‘If I make a mistake, then all of a sudden I clam up and I get really tight,’ we’re going to have a problem. So you look at them and say, ‘You’re here for a reason: To go play your game. Don’t worry about making a mistake. Move on to the next pitch, next play.’ And they did that, and they were awesome.”

title: It's good news, bad news for Red Sox pitching staff
author: Ty Anderson
body:
BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS – APRIL 08: Garrett Crochet #35 of the Boston Red Sox pitches against the Toronto Blue Jays during the first inning at Fenway Park on April 08, 2025 in Boston, Massachusetts.
Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images
Chad Tracy and the Red Sox know some reinforcements on the mound are coming.
And speaking ahead of Tuesday's loss to the Rangers, Tracy provided the masses with a mixed bag sort of update on those rehabbing arms trying to work their way back to Boston in time for the final push of the regular season and the playoffs.
Beginning with Garrett Crochet, Boston's ace who has been sidelined since late April, things continue to trend in the right direction, according to Tracy.
"Crochet threw today [and] that went well," Tracy said. "Everything went well. We’ll wait and see on the next steps, [but] that was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see over the next couple of days how he feels and then we’ll go from there.”
Crochet and the Red Sox have outright said that any return to action this season would by all means have to come in a reliever role. Crochet, meanwhile, has even suggested that he could make his return to the roster in the postseason.
Elsewhere on the rehab front, Tanner Houck took his best step yet in what's been an improbable run back into the picture as a legitimate option for the Red Sox.
On the hill for the Woo Sox in what was his third rehab outing (but first in Triple A), Houck allowed one walk and struck out three batters in one inning out of the bullpen. Houck is now up to seven strikeouts and has surrendered just one hit (but four walks) over 4.2 innings of work through three games between Portland and Worcester.
The hard-throwing Tyron Guerrero, meanwhile, is eligible to return from the injured list on Wednesday. Guerrero has been on the injured list since Sept. 1 with right shoulder inflammation, and could be a hugely important piece of the puzzle for Boston down the stretch given his dominant stretches earlier in the year.
But Tracy's seemingly endless parade of updates also came with some bad news, as he revealed that the club will be without Justin Slaten for the rest of the season.
Justin Slaten #63 of the Boston Red Sox pitches against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park.
"There was some degenerative changes in the flexor mass, so he's going to be [shut] down," Tracy said of Slaten, who met with Dr. Keith Meister, and his status moving forward. "He's going to get a PRP injection and likely going to end his season."
Slaten, who has not pitched since has not pitched since the club's Aug. 12 loss to Toronto, had recently started throwing from 90 feet before the shutdown. Slaten had really turned it on over his last 14 appearances prior to landing on the shelf, too, with 14 strikeouts and a 2.19 ERA in 12.1 innings of work before his season ended.
Fresh off a 4-2 loss to the Rangers on Tuesday but firmly in control of the second wild card in the American League, the Red Sox have another 11 games to get Crochet, Houck, Guerrero, and whoever else up to speed before the postseason begins.

title: Red Sox loss includes near go-ahead grand slam, different bullpen strategy, poor start
author: Chris Cotillo; Chriscotillo; Ccotillo Com
body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Red Sox didn’t have many big swings Tuesday night against Jacob deGrom and the Rangers, but one from a late-game pinch-hitter nearly flipped the script on the whole night.
Pinch-hitting for Jarren Duran against All-Star closer Jacob Latz in the eighth inning with Boston trailing by two, Andruw Monasterio got a 3-2 fastball just below the zone and smoked it — just foul. Monasterio sent a screaming line drive down the left field line, but it landed in the seats in foul territory, 369 feet away from home plate. If the ball had landed a few feet to its right, the Red Sox would have led 6-4 heading into the ninth.
For a second, the Red Sox dugout (on the third base side) thought Monasterio was a hero.
“It’s hard to tell from the dugout, from our angle,” said interim manager Chad Tracy. “When it came off the bat, it looked like, ‘Is that gonna hit the foul pole?’ But for about halfway on the ball flight, it was like, ‘I think that might hit the foul pole, I think it might be close.’”
Instead, Monasterio’s at-bat continued and Latz blew a 97 mph fastball by him to escape the threat. It was the second bases-loaded escape for the Rangers, who also didn’t allow a run in a similar situation in the fifth. In all, the Red Sox were hitless in four at-bats with runners in scoring position and left nine on base.
“We gave ourselves a couple of opportunities to maybe hit a single and tie the game up,” Tracy said. “We just couldn’t do it tonight.”
The pressure-filled situation marked just Monasterio’s 12th plate appearance in 15 games since Trevor Story and Roman Anthony were both activated from the injured list August 30.
Sandoval struggles
When starter Patrick Sandoval struck out the first four batters of his outing, it looked like he was about to go toe-to-toe with deGrom, the five-time All-Star on the other side. But that illusion quickly collapsed in a brutal second inning in which Sandoval allowed four runs and threw 44 pitches.
Sandoval allowed two separate rallies as the Rangers scored four times with two outs. With two men on after both singled, Elias Díaz opened the scoring with a two-run double to left. Sandoval then walked two batters in a row before Corey Seager plated two runs with a bloop single to left-center.
“Just got to pitch better,” said Sandoval, who has a 4.99 ERA. “Got to do better for this team. Can’t be doing this.”

title: Patrick Sandoval unravels as Red Sox strand chances in 4-2 loss to Rangers
author: Chris Henrique
body:
One miserable inning was enough to put the Red Sox in a hole. A pair of missed opportunities prevented them from climbing out of it.
Patrick Sandoval endured a brutal 44-pitch second inning in which the Rangers scored four times, and the Red Sox repeatedly came up empty with runners on base in a 4-2 loss Tuesday night at Globe Life Field.
Boston (82-69) opened its final road trip of the regular season with a loss and fell to 7-6 in September. The Red Sox did, however, move another step closer to securing a postseason berth after Toronto was routed by Detroit, reducing Boston’s magic number to five.
Any potential celebration will have to wait until after the Red Sox leave Texas. Even if Boston wins the final two games of the series, Toronto is off Thursday and would remain mathematically alive entering Friday.
Sandoval’s night began when he struck out the first four Rangers he faced before everything unraveled in a second inning that seemed as though it might never end.
With two outs, Brandon Nimmo and Ezequiel Duran delivered hard-hit singles at 106.3 mph and 105.3 mph, respectively. Elias Díaz followed by pulling a two-run double into left field to give Texas a 2-0 lead.
Sandoval never recovered walking former Sox catcher Danny Jansen and Justin Foscue before Corey Seager dropped a bloop single into shallow left, just beyond the reach of Trevor Story, allowing two more runs to score. By the time Sandoval finally escaped, he had thrown 44 pitches in the inning and Boston trailed 4-0.
Sandoval lasted just 2 2/3 innings and saw his ERA climb to 4.99.
“They drug at bats out on him,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters postgame. “It looked like he was going to get out of there with Diaz, that was a long at bat, I think one of those pitches was close and then he hits the double in the corner and it was just a struggle, we just couldn’t get out of the inning.”
The left-hander’s return from injury provided Boston with some needed innings after he was activated July 9, and he delivered several quality outings along the way. But with the postseason approaching, his place on the October roster has become increasingly uncertain.
Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle and Jake Bennett are ahead of him in the rotation picture, while Brayan Bello has found success in a bulk role. Garrett Crochet and Tanner Houck are also attempting to return before the postseason.
Patrick Sandoval strikes out the side in the 1st.
Justin Foscue made him throw 9 pitches to start the game. Needed 19 total to finish the inning. pic.twitter.com/qpUpDLA5Rc
Sandoval will have time to try and clean things up, but it’s looking as if the Red Sox are better suited with the lefty as a spectator when they inevitably travel to the Bronx.
Boston’s offense quickly cut the deficit in half against Jacob deGrom.
Nick Sogard jumped on a pitch in the third and sent it down the right-field line for a two-run homer, pulling the Red Sox within 4-2.
Sogard didn’t hit his first major league homer until his 322nd plate appearance Aug. 19. He has now hit five in his last 99 plate appearances, all coming over a 24-game span.
The versatile infielder contributed in other ways, too. Sogard perfectly executed a sacrifice bunt in the fifth to move two runners into scoring position and later made an athletic play to complete a 1-4-3 double play.
But the Red Sox couldn’t capitalize on their opportunities against deGrom. The Texas right-hander held Boston to three hits and struck out eight over five innings while maintaining a fastball around 97 mph.

title: Patrick Sandoval allows four runs in second, Red Sox lose opener to Rangers
author: Mac Cerullo
body:
Patrick Sandoval has had a rocky month. Entering Tuesday, the Red Sox left-hander had allowed a 6.12 ERA over his last five starts, but coming out of the gate Sandoval looked like he’d finally figured things out.
But after striking out the first four batters he faced, the wheels came off in the bottom of the second.
Sandoval allowed four runs over an interminable 44-pitch second inning and ultimately got the hook after recording just eight outs in Boston’s 4-2 loss to the Texas Rangers.
Nick Sogard hit a two-run home run to help get the Red Sox back into the game, but the offense otherwise couldn’t get anything going against Jacob deGrom and the Rangers bullpen, squandering bases loaded opportunities in the fifth and eighth innings.
Sandoval started strong by striking out the side in the first inning, but after sending down Jake Burger to start the second everything ground to a screeching halt. The right-hander allowed a pair of singles, served up a two-run double to Elias Diaz, and then walked back-to-back batters to load the bases for five-time All-Star Corey Seager.
It appeared for a moment like Sandoval might minimize the damage when he drew a pop fly to shallow left, but the ball drifted into no-man’s land and Trevor Story couldn’t make the catch, allowing two more runs to score and putting the Rangers up 4-0.
Sandoval ultimately needed 44 pitches to get through the second, blowing up his pitch count and ensuring a long evening for the Red Sox bullpen. He recorded two outs in the third and was lifted for Brayan Bello after allowing four runs over 2 2/3 innings.
“They drug at bats out on him,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters in Arlington postgame. “It looked like he was going to get out of there with Diaz, that was a long at bat, I think one of those pitches was close and then he hits the double in the corner and it was just a struggle, we just couldn’t get out of the inning.”
Four runs matches the largest deficit the Red Sox have overcome in a win this season, but the club didn’t need long to cut it in half. After Caleb Durbin reached on a one-out single in the top of the third, Sogard ripped a line drive off deGrom that cleared the right field fence for a two-run home run.
It was the fifth home run of the season for Sogard, all of which have come since Aug. 19. Prior to that the 29-year-old had never hit a homer over his first three seasons as a big leaguer.
That wound up being as close as Boston got.
The Red Sox could have tied the score or taken the lead with one swing in the fifth inning, but despite loading the bases without recording a hit the club couldn’t get a run across. Jarren Duran was hit by a pitch, Durbin reached on catcher’s interference and Mickey Gasper walked to bring up Adley Rutschman with two outs, but the catcher grounded out to short to keep it a 4-2 game.
Boston’s bullpen did its part to keep the Red Sox in the game. Bello tossed 1 2/3 perfect innings, Alec Gamboa threw one scoreless aided in large part by a brilliant double play turned by Sogard to end the fifth, and Wyatt Olds worked his way out of a runners-at-the-corners, two-out jam to escape the sixth. Jovani Moran entered with a man on in the seventh and got three quick outs, setting the table for one last Red Sox push in the eighth.
Jahmai Jones sparked the rally with a leadoff single, Willson Contreras drew a one-out walk, and after Wilyer Abreu grounded out to move the two runners into scoring position Story was intentionally walked to load the bases again.
Rather than have Duran face the left-hander Jacob Latz, Tracy pinch hit Andruw Monasterio, but the move didn’t pay off. Monasterio worked a full count and nearly went deep on a hard hit liner that landed just foul before striking out to leave them loaded again.
Boston went quietly in the top of the ninth, finishing the game 0 for 4 with runners in scoring position while stranding nine men on base.
“We gave ourselves a couple of opportunities to maybe hit a single and tie the game up and we couldn’t do it tonight,” Tracy said.
Magic number still 5
In addition to keeping pace in the AL West race, the Rangers also jumped the Toronto Blue Jays to become the first team below the AL Wild Card cutline. As a result the Red Sox’s magic number remains five despite the Blue Jays’ 10-1 loss earlier in the night.
Boston (82-69) can clinch a playoff berth as early as Friday, and depending on how things play out in the AL Central the Red Sox could lock down the second Wild Card spot as soon as this weekend.
Houck scoreless with WooSox
Tanner Houck (Tommy John surgery rehab) tossed a scoreless inning of relief in his latest rehab appearance with the WooSox on Tuesday. The right-hander entered the game in the seventh inning and allowed one walk, no hits and struck out three over 22 pitches.

Jovani Moran entered with a man on in the seventh and got three quick outs, setting the table for one last Red Sox push in the eighth.
Jahmai Jones sparked the rally with a leadoff single, Willson Contreras drew a one-out walk, and after Wilyer Abreu grounded out to move the two runners into scoring position Story was intentionally walked to load the bases again.
Rather than have Duran face the left-hander Jacob Latz, Tracy pinch hit Andruw Monasterio, but the move didn’t pay off. Monasterio worked a full count and nearly went deep on a hard hit liner that landed just foul before striking out to leave them loaded again.

Boston (82-69) can clinch a playoff berth as early as Friday, and depending on how things play out in the AL Central the Red Sox could lock down the second Wild Card spot as soon as this weekend.

Tanner Houck (Tommy John surgery rehab) tossed a scoreless inning of relief in his latest rehab appearance with the WooSox on Tuesday. The right-hander entered the game in the seventh inning and allowed one walk, no hits and struck out three over 22 pitches.
rss_title: Patrick Sandoval allows four runs in second, Red Sox lose opener to Rangers
rss_body:
Patrick Sandoval has had a rocky month. Entering Tuesday, the Red Sox left-hander had allowed a 6.12 ERA over his last five starts, but coming out of the gate Sandoval looked like he’d finally figured things out.
But after striking out the first four batters he faced, the wheels came off in the bottom of the second.
Sandoval allowed four runs over an interminable 44-pitch second inning and ultimately got the hook after recording just eight outs in Boston’s 4-2 loss to the Texas Rangers.
Nick Sogard hit a two-run home run to help get the Red Sox back into the game, but the offense otherwise couldn’t get anything going against Jacob deGrom and the Rangers bullpen, squandering bases loaded opportunities in the fifth and eighth innings.

title: 4 big questions surround Crochet's possible return, impact down the stretch
author: Ian Browne
body:
The 2026 season has been, for the most part, an injury-plagued loss for Crochet, who made his first six starts before getting shut down with left shoulder inflammation that regressed when he made his first attempted comeback in late May.
But the beauty of all this is that Crochet can wash away the sour taste of missing most of the season by getting back as a reliever in time for the most important games.
After that setback at the end of May, it took Crochet three months just to be cleared to throw off the mound again.
Now that he’s been able to do so three times, and is scheduled for a fourth bullpen session at Fenway Park on Tuesday, there is legitimate hope he can be on the roster when the Red Sox open their postseason on Sept. 29 -- likely at Yankee Stadium.
This time, assuming he makes it back, Crochet will be cast in a much different role, but one that can still be impactful.
Figuring you have questions about how and when Crochet fits in, here are some answers.
Can Crochet make it back before the regular season ends?
It’s not impossible. His next key step after graduating from bullpen sessions will be to face hitters. That could happen as soon as this weekend, depending on what the club decides after Tuesday’s session.
Ideally, when it comes to Crochet’s situation, the Triple-A season would go a little longer. But, alas, it ends on Sunday.
It seems more likely Crochet will throw live batting practice and/or some type of simulated game rather than getting into a Minor League game, perhaps doing so multiple times.
Would this leave time for one tune-up before the regular season ends on Sept. 27? Perhaps, but not necessarily.
Would Crochet be thrown right into the fire of the playoffs?
What if there isn’t time for Crochet to pitch in any type of game setting before the Wild Card Series starts? Would the Red Sox still put him on the roster?
Well, if he’s throwing up to his capabilities, the answer is absolutely yes.
“It's Garrett Crochet,” said Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy. “If Garrett Crochet looks like Garrett Crochet and he's healthy and able to go out there and pitch, and it looks like him? Yeah, that helps any team.”
What would Boston’s bullpen cast look like with Crochet in the mix?
In a word, dominant. Through their first 150 games of the season entering Tuesday, Boston’s bullpen has a 3.11 ERA, best in the Majors. That’s without Crochet.
Now, add Crochet and possibly 2024 Tanner Houck, who is on a Minor League rehab assignment in his return from Tommy John surgery, and Tracy’s relief crew could have a succession of pitchers with nasty stuff.
At 38 years old, lefty Aroldis Chapman continues to be a force. He has one of the best eighth-inning setup men in the game in front of him in righty Garrett Whitlock. Tyron Guerrero, the righty with triple-digit heat, is due back in the next couple of days after missing the last couple of weeks with right shoulder inflammation. Power lefty Erik Miller has been tremendous since he was acquired at the Aug. 3 Trade Deadline.
Brayan Bello, who hasn’t had much success has a starter this season but has been largely stellar in relief, is another weapon. Add Crochet and Houck to those five pitchers and the Sox would have bullpen depth that would be the envy of most teams.
How would the Sox use Crochet?
The beauty of Crochet is that he could work out of a hybrid role, meaning he could be available for whichever part of the game Tracy needs him most.
Keep in mind that Crochet was a relief pitcher not just in college at Tennessee, but also for the White Sox before being converted to a starting role in ‘24. He has experience working in the early, middle and late part of games.
Thinking outside the box, the Sox could even deploy Crochet as an opener if the occasion called for it, given his experience starting games.
“He'd have plenty of comfort opening if you wanted to go that route," Tracy said. "He pitched out of the 'pen. So if you need him to come in the middle innings of a game, a two-inning pocket, I'm sure he'd have comfort doing that, too."

title: Kristian Campbell’s Season Takes Another Bad Turn for Red Sox
author: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
body:
Boston Red Sox fans will not be seeing former top prospect Kristian Campbell in the big leagues at all this season, unfortunately.
On Tuesday, Tommy Cassell of the Worcester T&G Sports reported that Campbell's season is over. Campbell was placed on the seven-day Injured List due to a left foot contusion on Sep. 10. Cassell reported that Campbell will not be able to return before Triple-A Worcester's season ends on Sep. 20.
"Some injury updates today in AAA Worcester: Tanner Houck is scheduled to pitch one inning (20-25 pitches) in relief," Cassell wrote. "Romy Gonzalez is in at DH despite being a bit banged up. Iggy Suarez mentioned he's "an option" to contribute with the Red Sox moving forward. Kristian Campbell is out for the rest of the WooSox season. 'He was a big part of what we've been doing,' Suarez said. 'So, it's definitely a downer for that.'"
Kristian Campbell Is Done For The Year
That's some really unfortunate news for one of the most intriguing players in the Red Sox's system. Campbell made the big league club out of Spring Training in 2025 as the first member of the "Big 3," including him, Roman Anthony and Marcelo Mayer. He was red-hot out of the gate to the point that Boston handed him an eight-year, $60 million deal. But things took a turn afterward. Campbell was demoted to Triple-A in June, 2025. He hasn't been in the majors since.
Campbell played in 73 down in Triple-A last season and then didn't make the Red Sox's big league club out of camp. He has been down in the minors all season this year trying to work his way back.
The 24-year-old spent the season in the outfield as Boston tried to slow things down after moving him around all over the place last year. For Boston, it is loaded in the outfield to the point that there was a logjam early on in the season. Then, despite the Red Sox losing Roman Anthony to the Injured List for a while, there still wasn't space for Campbell in the majors.
Overall, Campbell wrapped up his season after playing in 109 games for Triple-A and slashing .256/.383/.380 with a .763 OPS, eight homers and 51 RBIs. Hopefully, he's able to get back on track and get back into the mix by the time Spring Training rolls around. Who could've seen this coming back in 2025? Campbell looked like a franchise cornerstone piece. Unfortunately, he hasn't been in the majors in over a year and now that won't be happening this year.

title: Chicago Cubs Make Alex Bregman Announcement During Braves Series
author: TJ French
body:
The Chicago Cubs are currently taking on the Atlanta Braves in a 3-game series this week with NL-seeding implications.
Chicago took the series opener on Monday by a score of 7-3, and will look to win the series on Tuesday evening with Kevin Gausman on the mound (9-12, 4.60 ERA, 171 SO). The Cubbies will be trying to muster up offense against Martin Perez.
Due to the lefty going for the Braves, manager Craig Counsell has announced a new rendition of the Cubs lineup, which features a slight Alex Bregman tweak.
More MLB on Heavy: Bobby Miller Makes Honest Statement Before Dodgers-Reds Game
Alex Bregman Slotted in 3-Hole For Braves Game on Tuesday
After batting cleanup on Monday evening, Alex Bregman will bat third on Tuesday against the southpaw Perez.
It's a lineup for Craig Counsell that features many changes.
Per @UnderdogMLB, here is the full batting order for Chicago on 9/15:
Cubs 9/15: "P. Crow-Armstrong CF S. Suzuki RF A. Bregman 3B T. Taylor LF N. Hoerner SS M. Busch 1B M. Shaw DH P. Ramírez 2B M. Amaya C K. Gausman SP"
Other changes include Tyrone Taylor batting cleanup, Nico Hoerner in the five-spot, and Ian Happ not being included in today's order. Matt Shaw gets the start at DH.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Announce Injury News on 9-Year MLB Player

title: 2026시즌 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 결과 발표…캠 슐리틀러와 제이콥 미시오로스키 만장일치 1위 등극
author: MLB Korea 기자
body:
2026 정규시즌이 단 2주만을 남겨둔 가운데, 아메리칸리그와 내셔널리그 사이영상 수상 레이스가 사실상 막을 내린 것처럼 보입니다.
이는 양 리그 모두 쟁쟁한 후보들이 포진해 있는 다른 후보군 때문이라기보다는 독보적인 선두 주자들 때문입니다. 뉴욕 양키스의 캠 슐리틀러와 밀워키 브루어스의 제이콥 미시오로스키가 확실하게 쐐기를 박았습니다. 올해 마지막 사이영상 모의 투표에 참여한 MLB.com 투표인단 32명은 두 명의 강력한 강속구 투수를 각 리그의 만장일치 1위로 선정했습니다.
전문가들은 지금까지의 결과뿐만 아니라 남은 2주 동안의 판도가 어떻게 전개될지 예상하여 트로피를 거머쥘 주인공에게 투표했습니다. 투표인단은 각 리그에서 상위 5명의 선수를 선정하도록 요청받았으며, 투수들은 5-4-3-2-1 점수 스케일(1위 표 5점, 2위 표 4점 등)에 따라 점수를 획득했습니다.
별도 표기가 없는 한 모든 기록은 13일(미국 현지시간) 경기 기준이었습니다.
아메리칸리그
1. 캠 슐리틀러, 뉴욕 양키스 (총 160점; 1위 표 32장)
슐리틀러는 13일 서브웨이 시리즈 최종전에서 뉴욕 메츠 타선을 상대로 6이닝 동안 무실점 피칭을 선보이며 시즌 평균자책점을 1.95로 낮췄습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그에서 가장 뛰어난 기록일 뿐만 아니라, 메이저리그 규정 이닝 충족 투수 중 미시오로스키와 공동으로 가장 낮은 기록이기도 합니다. 슐리틀러는 최근 7경기 연속으로 1실점 이하 경기만을 기록하며 자신의 메이저리그 첫 풀타임 시즌을 화려하게 마무리하고 있습니다. 그는 지난 포스트시즌 아메리칸리그 와일드카드 시리즈에서 센세이션을 일으켰던 바로 그 공식인 '삼진아웃을 유도하는 세 가지 패스트볼 조합'으로 타자들을 계속해서 압도하고 있습니다. 10월 가을야구가 다가오는 가운데, 그의 화려한 앙코르 무대가 코앞으로 다가왔습니다.
2. 딜런 시즈, 토론토 블루제이스 (126점)
시즈는 지난해 11월 토론토 블루제이스와 체결한 7년 계약의 첫해부터 완벽 그 자체인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 그는 가장 최근 경기인 13일 볼티모어 오리올스전에서 9개의 삼진을 솎아내며, 올 시즌 9개 이상의 탈삼진을 기록한 경기를 13차례로 늘렸습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그 어떤 투수보다도 많은 기록입니다. 시즈의 통산 236개의 탈삼진은 개인 단일시즌 최다 기록 경신이자 메이저리그 전체에서 미시오로스키와 함께 공동 1위에 해당합니다. 올해 시즈는 치명적인 포심 패스트볼/슬라이더 조합에 더 균형 잡힌 구종 배합을 더해 상대 타선을 공략하는 다양한 방식을 구사하고 있습니다. 이것이 바로 시즈의 피안타율(.177)이 아메리칸리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 가장 낮은 이유 중 일부입니다.
3. 파커 메식, 클리블랜드 가디언스 (77점)
슐리틀러나 시즈와 같은 반열은 아닐지 몰라도, 메식은 루키 시즌에 부정할 수 없는 환상적인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 개성 있는 폼을 지닌 이 좌완 투수는 11일 미네소타 트윈스를 상대로 한 직전 등판에서 5.1이닝 동안 단 1실점만을 허용했으며, 치열한 페넌트레이스 혈전 속에서도 그것이 바로 메식이 해내는 방식입니다. 이번 시즌 5이닝 이상을 소화하면서 1실점 이하만 내준 경기가 슐리틀러와 시즈보다 많은 아메리칸리그 투수는 단 두 명뿐입니다. 메식의 2.51의 평균자책점은 메이저리그 전체 5위에 해당하는 기록입니다. 그의 성공 비결은 바로 포심 패스트볼입니다. 메식은 구속이 시속 94.3마일(약 151.8km)로 아주 빠르지는 않지만, 스타캐스트의 득점 가치(run value) 지표에 따르면 그의 포심은 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 개별 구종 중 하나로 꼽힙니다.
4. 드류 라스무센, 탬파베이 레이스 (52점)
금요일, 탬파베이는 주니어 카미네로의 극적인 끝내기 홈런에 힘입어 올 시즌 구단 중 가장 먼저 포스트시즌 진출을 확정 지었습니다. 잊지 말아야 할 점은 라스무센이 그날 탬파베이의 선발 투수로 등판해 1실점 투구로 7이닝을 가볍게 책임졌다는 사실입니다. 탬파베이가 승리한 것은 놀라운 일이 아닙니다. 그것이 바로 라스무센이 마운드에 올랐을 때 그들이 보여주는 방식이기 때문입니다. 탬파베이는 올스타 브레이크 이전부터 거슬러 올라가 그의 최근 선발 등판 10경기를 모두 승리로 장식했습니다. 31세의 우완 투수인 그는 세 가지 형태의 패스트볼 구종과 완벽한 제구력을 바탕으로 아메리칸리그 평균자책점(2.81), WHIP(0.92), 피안타율(.203) 부문에서 모두 상위 5위 이내에 이름을 올리고 있습니다.
5. 소니 그레이, 보스턴 레드삭스 (37점)
보스턴은 야구계 최고 수준의 투수진을 앞세워 포스트시즌 진출을 향해 순항하고 있습니다. 이 문장은 개막전 당시였다면 당연히 이해되었겠지만, 좌완 투수 개럿 크로셰가 4월 말 이후 부상으로 전력에서 이탈했다는 사실을 안다면 이야기가 다릅니다. 크로셰의 공백 속에서 그레이가 에이스 역할을 톡톡히 해냈습니다. 그는 27경기에 선발 등판해 17승 5패 평균자책점 2.76을 기록 중이며, 투수 승리 기록이 전부를 말해주는 것은 아니지만 아메리칸리그에서 그레이보다 더 많은 승리를 거둔 투수가 없다는 점은 주목할 만합니다. 그는 통산 세 번째 아메리칸리그 사이영상 투표 상위 5위 진입을 노리고 있습니다. 2023년 미네소타 소속으로 투표 2위를 차지했으며, 2015년에는 오클랜드 소속으로 3위에 오른 바 있습니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 리드 데트머스(LA 에인절스), 개빈 윌리엄스(클리블랜드 가디언스), 닉 마르티네즈(탬파베이 레이스), 마이클 와카(캔자스시티 로열스)
내셔널리그
1. 제이콥 미시오로스키, 밀워키 브루어스 (총 160점, 1위 표 32장)
'더 미즈'는 지난 8일 시카고 컵스를 상대로 6.1이닝 동안 탈삼진 9개를 솎아내며 단 1실점만 내주는 센세이션한 투구로 보기 드문 부진을 말끔히 씻어냈습니다. 압도적인 구위를 자랑하는 이 우완 투수는 평균자책점(1.95), 피안타율(.155), 탈삼진(236개)을 포함하여 거의 모든 주요 투수 통계 부문에서 내셔널리그 선두를 달리고 있습니다. 161.1이닝을 소화한 지금까지도 미시오로스키는 여전히 강력한 불을 뿜어내고 있습니다. 그는 이번 시즌 시속 100마일 이상의 공을 무려 1,010개나 던졌으며, 이는 이 부문 2위인 투수(메이슨 밀러, 468개)의 두 배를 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 수치입니다.
2. 크리스 세일, 애틀랜타 브레이브스 (106점)
나이를 가늠할 수 없는 이 불세출의 투수는 시즌 막판 내셔널리그 사이영상 레이스의 격차를 좁히기 위해 최선의 노력을 다하고 있습니다. 세일의 평균자책점 2.18은 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 좋은 기록이자, 37세의 이 베테랑이 2018년 이후 단일 시즌 기준 기록한 가장 낮은 수치입니다. 그는 최근 23경기 연속으로 3실점 이하 경기만을 치르며 놀라울 정도로 꾸준한 모습을 보여주었습니다. 이번 시즌 16경기 이상 연속으로 3실점 이하를 기록한 선발 투수는 그 외에 단 한 명도 없습니다. 세일은 향상된 구속 덕분에 세월을 역행하고 있으며, 선발 투수로 활약한 통산 그 어느 때보다 더 빠른 공을 뿌리고 있습니다.
3. 크리스토퍼 산체스, 필라델피아 필리스 (99점)
산체스는 최근 두 경기에서 총 9실점을 허용하며 이전 모의 투표보다 한 계단 내려앉았습니다. 하지만 이 마른 좌완 투수는 여전히 사이영상 후보로 손색이 없는 시즌을 만들어가고 있습니다. 산체스는 메이저리그 전체에서 두 번째로 많은 이닝(187.1이닝)을 소화했으며, 내셔널리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 5번째로 좋은 평균자책점(2.79)과 3번째로 좋은 FIP(수비 무관 평균자책점, 2.72)를 기록 중입니다. 야구 통계 전문 사이트 베이스볼레퍼런스(Baseball Reference) 기준 WAR에 따르면, 산체스는 7.6의 WAR을 기록하며 2026년 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 투수로 자리매김했습니다.
4. 헤수스 루자르도, 필라델피아 필리스 (52점)
루자르도는 노동절에 내셔널리그 동부지구 선두인 애틀랜타를 상대로 거둔 눈부신 완봉승에 힘입어 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 명단에 이름을 올렸습니다. 이 좌완 투수가 마땅히 받아야 할 찬사를 받는 시점은 이미 한참 지났습니다. 루자르도는 최근 12경기에서 8승 1패 평균자책점 1.66을 기록하며, 7월 1일 이후 메이저리그 전체에서 가장 낮은 평균자책점을 마크했고 8월 내셔널리그 이달의 투수로 선정되었습니다. 지난 시즌 연마한 치명적인 스위퍼를 무기로 장착한 루자르도는 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 높은 탈삼진율(30.4%)을 기록하고 있습니다. 필리스 팬들은 루자르도가 어깨 통증으로 인해 직전 등판을 건너뛰어 가슴을 졸였으나, MRI 검사 후 본인은 "걱정하지 않는다"고 안심시켰습니다.
5. 야마모토 요시노부, LA 다저스 (43점)
우리는 이제 야마모토에게 너무나 많은 것을 기대한 나머지, 지난 9일 레즈전에서 보여준 7이닝 10탈삼진 역투 같은 최고의 피칭조차 당연하게 느껴질 정도입니다. 그는 여전히 할리우드(LA)에 어울리는 화려한 스타 군단 선발진의 에이스로서 26경기에 등판해 평균자책점 2.62를 기록하고 있습니다. 미시오로스키에 이어 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 낮은 0.88의 WHIP과 .184의 피안타율을 기록 중인 야마모토만큼 주자 출루를 철저히 억제하는 투수는 드뭅니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 체이스 번스(신시내티 레즈), 에두아르도 로드리게스(애리조나 다이아몬드백스), 메이슨 밀러(샌디에이고 파드리스), 잭 휠러(필라델피아 필리스)

아메리칸리그
1. 캠 슐리틀러, 뉴욕 양키스 (총 160점; 1위 표 32장)
슐리틀러는 13일 서브웨이 시리즈 최종전에서 뉴욕 메츠 타선을 상대로 6이닝 동안 무실점 피칭을 선보이며 시즌 평균자책점을 1.95로 낮췄습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그에서 가장 뛰어난 기록일 뿐만 아니라, 메이저리그 규정 이닝 충족 투수 중 미시오로스키와 공동으로 가장 낮은 기록이기도 합니다. 슐리틀러는 최근 7경기 연속으로 1실점 이하 경기만을 기록하며 자신의 메이저리그 첫 풀타임 시즌을 화려하게 마무리하고 있습니다. 그는 지난 포스트시즌 아메리칸리그 와일드카드 시리즈에서 센세이션을 일으켰던 바로 그 공식인 '삼진아웃을 유도하는 세 가지 패스트볼 조합'으로 타자들을 계속해서 압도하고 있습니다. 10월 가을야구가 다가오는 가운데, 그의 화려한 앙코르 무대가 코앞으로 다가왔습니다.
2. 딜런 시즈, 토론토 블루제이스 (126점)
시즈는 지난해 11월 토론토 블루제이스와 체결한 7년 계약의 첫해부터 완벽 그 자체인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 그는 가장 최근 경기인 13일 볼티모어 오리올스전에서 9개의 삼진을 솎아내며, 올 시즌 9개 이상의 탈삼진을 기록한 경기를 13차례로 늘렸습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그 어떤 투수보다도 많은 기록입니다. 시즈의 통산 236개의 탈삼진은 개인 단일시즌 최다 기록 경신이자 메이저리그 전체에서 미시오로스키와 함께 공동 1위에 해당합니다. 올해 시즈는 치명적인 포심 패스트볼/슬라이더 조합에 더 균형 잡힌 구종 배합을 더해 상대 타선을 공략하는 다양한 방식을 구사하고 있습니다. 이것이 바로 시즈의 피안타율(.177)이 아메리칸리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 가장 낮은 이유 중 일부입니다.
3. 파커 메식, 클리블랜드 가디언스 (77점)
슐리틀러나 시즈와 같은 반열은 아닐지 몰라도, 메식은 루키 시즌에 부정할 수 없는 환상적인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 개성 있는 폼을 지닌 이 좌완 투수는 11일 미네소타 트윈스를 상대로 한 직전 등판에서 5.1이닝 동안 단 1실점만을 허용했으며, 치열한 페넌트레이스 혈전 속에서도 그것이 바로 메식이 해내는 방식입니다. 이번 시즌 5이닝 이상을 소화하면서 1실점 이하만 내준 경기가 슐리틀러와 시즈보다 많은 아메리칸리그 투수는 단 두 명뿐입니다. 메식의 2.51의 평균자책점은 메이저리그 전체 5위에 해당하는 기록입니다. 그의 성공 비결은 바로 포심 패스트볼입니다. 메식은 구속이 시속 94.3마일(약 151.8km)로 아주 빠르지는 않지만, 스타캐스트의 득점 가치(run value) 지표에 따르면 그의 포심은 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 개별 구종 중 하나로 꼽힙니다.
4. 드류 라스무센, 탬파베이 레이스 (52점)
금요일, 탬파베이는 주니어 카미네로의 극적인 끝내기 홈런에 힘입어 올 시즌 구단 중 가장 먼저 포스트시즌 진출을 확정 지었습니다. 잊지 말아야 할 점은 라스무센이 그날 탬파베이의 선발 투수로 등판해 1실점 투구로 7이닝을 가볍게 책임졌다는 사실입니다. 탬파베이가 승리한 것은 놀라운 일이 아닙니다. 그것이 바로 라스무센이 마운드에 올랐을 때 그들이 보여주는 방식이기 때문입니다. 탬파베이는 올스타 브레이크 이전부터 거슬러 올라가 그의 최근 선발 등판 10경기를 모두 승리로 장식했습니다. 31세의 우완 투수인 그는 세 가지 형태의 패스트볼 구종과 완벽한 제구력을 바탕으로 아메리칸리그 평균자책점(2.81), WHIP(0.92), 피안타율(.203) 부문에서 모두 상위 5위 이내에 이름을 올리고 있습니다.
5. 소니 그레이, 보스턴 레드삭스 (37점)
보스턴은 야구계 최고 수준의 투수진을 앞세워 포스트시즌 진출을 향해 순항하고 있습니다. 이 문장은 개막전 당시였다면 당연히 이해되었겠지만, 좌완 투수 개럿 크로셰가 4월 말 이후 부상으로 전력에서 이탈했다는 사실을 안다면 이야기가 다릅니다. 크로셰의 공백 속에서 그레이가 에이스 역할을 톡톡히 해냈습니다. 그는 27경기에 선발 등판해 17승 5패 평균자책점 2.76을 기록 중이며, 투수 승리 기록이 전부를 말해주는 것은 아니지만 아메리칸리그에서 그레이보다 더 많은 승리를 거둔 투수가 없다는 점은 주목할 만합니다. 그는 통산 세 번째 아메리칸리그 사이영상 투표 상위 5위 진입을 노리고 있습니다. 2023년 미네소타 소속으로 투표 2위를 차지했으며, 2015년에는 오클랜드 소속으로 3위에 오른 바 있습니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 리드 데트머스(LA 에인절스), 개빈 윌리엄스(클리블랜드 가디언스), 닉 마르티네즈(탬파베이 레이스), 마이클 와카(캔자스시티 로열스)
내셔널리그
1. 제이콥 미시오로스키, 밀워키 브루어스 (총 160점, 1위 표 32장)
'더 미즈'는 지난 8일 시카고 컵스를 상대로 6.1이닝 동안 탈삼진 9개를 솎아내며 단 1실점만 내주는 센세이션한 투구로 보기 드문 부진을 말끔히 씻어냈습니다. 압도적인 구위를 자랑하는 이 우완 투수는 평균자책점(1.95), 피안타율(.155), 탈삼진(236개)을 포함하여 거의 모든 주요 투수 통계 부문에서 내셔널리그 선두를 달리고 있습니다. 161.1이닝을 소화한 지금까지도 미시오로스키는 여전히 강력한 불을 뿜어내고 있습니다. 그는 이번 시즌 시속 100마일 이상의 공을 무려 1,010개나 던졌으며, 이는 이 부문 2위인 투수(메이슨 밀러, 468개)의 두 배를 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 수치입니다.
2. 크리스 세일, 애틀랜타 브레이브스 (106점)
나이를 가늠할 수 없는 이 불세출의 투수는 시즌 막판 내셔널리그 사이영상 레이스의 격차를 좁히기 위해 최선의 노력을 다하고 있습니다. 세일의 평균자책점 2.18은 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 좋은 기록이자, 37세의 이 베테랑이 2018년 이후 단일 시즌 기준 기록한 가장 낮은 수치입니다. 그는 최근 23경기 연속으로 3실점 이하 경기만을 치르며 놀라울 정도로 꾸준한 모습을 보여주었습니다. 이번 시즌 16경기 이상 연속으로 3실점 이하를 기록한 선발 투수는 그 외에 단 한 명도 없습니다. 세일은 향상된 구속 덕분에 세월을 역행하고 있으며, 선발 투수로 활약한 통산 그 어느 때보다 더 빠른 공을 뿌리고 있습니다.
3. 크리스토퍼 산체스, 필라델피아 필리스 (99점)
산체스는 최근 두 경기에서 총 9실점을 허용하며 이전 모의 투표보다 한 계단 내려앉았습니다. 하지만 이 마른 좌완 투수는 여전히 사이영상 후보로 손색이 없는 시즌을 만들어가고 있습니다. 산체스는 메이저리그 전체에서 두 번째로 많은 이닝(187.1이닝)을 소화했으며, 내셔널리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 5번째로 좋은 평균자책점(2.79)과 3번째로 좋은 FIP(수비 무관 평균자책점, 2.72)를 기록 중입니다. 야구 통계 전문 사이트 베이스볼레퍼런스(Baseball Reference) 기준 WAR에 따르면, 산체스는 7.6의 WAR을 기록하며 2026년 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 투수로 자리매김했습니다.
4. 헤수스 루자르도, 필라델피아 필리스 (52점)
루자르도는 노동절에 내셔널리그 동부지구 선두인 애틀랜타를 상대로 거둔 눈부신 완봉승에 힘입어 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 명단에 이름을 올렸습니다. 이 좌완 투수가 마땅히 받아야 할 찬사를 받는 시점은 이미 한참 지났습니다. 루자르도는 최근 12경기에서 8승 1패 평균자책점 1.66을 기록하며, 7월 1일 이후 메이저리그 전체에서 가장 낮은 평균자책점을 마크했고 8월 내셔널리그 이달의 투수로 선정되었습니다. 지난 시즌 연마한 치명적인 스위퍼를 무기로 장착한 루자르도는 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 높은 탈삼진율(30.4%)을 기록하고 있습니다. 필리스 팬들은 루자르도가 어깨 통증으로 인해 직전 등판을 건너뛰어 가슴을 졸였으나, MRI 검사 후 본인은 "걱정하지 않는다"고 안심시켰습니다.
5. 야마모토 요시노부, LA 다저스 (43점)
우리는 이제 야마모토에게 너무나 많은 것을 기대한 나머지, 지난 9일 레즈전에서 보여준 7이닝 10탈삼진 역투 같은 최고의 피칭조차 당연하게 느껴질 정도입니다. 그는 여전히 할리우드(LA)에 어울리는 화려한 스타 군단 선발진의 에이스로서 26경기에 등판해 평균자책점 2.62를 기록하고 있습니다. 미시오로스키에 이어 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 낮은 0.88의 WHIP과 .184의 피안타율을 기록 중인 야마모토만큼 주자 출루를 철저히 억제하는 투수는 드뭅니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 체이스 번스(신시내티 레즈), 에두아르도 로드리게스(애리조나 다이아몬드백스), 메이슨 밀러(샌디에이고 파드리스), 잭 휠러(필라델피아 필리스)

rss_title: 2026시즌 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 결과 발표…캠 슐리틀러와 제이콥 미시오로스키 만장일치 1위 등극
rss_body:
2026 정규시즌이 단 2주만을 남겨둔 가운데, 아메리칸리그와 내셔널리그 사이영상 수상 레이스가 사실상 막을 내린 것처럼 보입니다.
이는 양 리그 모두 쟁쟁한 후보들이 포진해 있는 다른 후보군 때문이라기보다는 독보적인 선두 주자들 때문입니다. 뉴욕 양키스의 캠 슐리틀러와 밀워키 브루어스의 제이콥 미시오로스키가 확실하게 쐐기를 박았습니다. 올해 마지막 사이영상 모의 투표에 참여한 MLB.com 투표인단 32명은 두 명의 강력한 강속구 투수를 각 리그의 만장일치 1위로 선정했습니다.
전문가들은 지금까지의 결과뿐만 아니라 남은 2주 동안의 판도가 어떻게 전개될지 예상하여 트로피를 거머쥘 주인공에게 투표했습니다. 투표인단은 각 리그에서 상위 5명의 선수를 선정하도록 요청받았으며, 투수들은 5-4-3-2-1 점수 스케일(1위 표 5점, 2위 표 4점 등)에 따라 점수를 획득했습니다.
별도 표기가 없는 한 모든 기록은 13일(미국 현지시간) 경기 기준이었습니다.
아메리칸리그
1. 캠 슐리틀러, 뉴욕 양키스 (총 160점; 1위 표 32장)
슐리틀러는 13일 서브웨이 시리즈 최종전에서 뉴욕 메츠 타선을 상대로 6이닝 동안 무실점 피칭을 선보이며 시즌 평균자책점을 1.95로 낮췄습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그에서 가장 뛰어난 기록일 뿐만 아니라, 메이저리그 규정 이닝 충족 투수 중 미시오로스키와 공동으로 가장 낮은 기록이기도 합니다. 슐리틀러는 최근 7경기 연속으로 1실점 이하 경기만을 기록하며 자신의 메이저리그 첫 풀타임 시즌을 화려하게 마무리하고 있습니다. 그는 지난 포스트시즌 아메리칸리그 와일드카드 시리즈에서 센세이션을 일으켰던 바로 그 공식인 '삼진아웃을 유도하는 세 가지 패스트볼 조합'으로 타자들을 계속해서 압도하고 있습니다. 10월 가을야구가 다가오는 가운데, 그의 화려한 앙코르 무대가 코앞으로 다가왔습니다.
2. 딜런 시즈, 토론토 블루제이스 (126점)
시즈는 지난해 11월 토론토 블루제이스와 체결한 7년 계약의 첫해부터 완벽 그 자체인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 그는 가장 최근 경기인 13일 볼티모어 오리올스전에서 9개의 삼진을 솎아내며, 올 시즌 9개 이상의 탈삼진을 기록한 경기를 13차례로 늘렸습니다. 이는 아메리칸리그 어떤 투수보다도 많은 기록입니다. 시즈의 통산 236개의 탈삼진은 개인 단일시즌 최다 기록 경신이자 메이저리그 전체에서 미시오로스키와 함께 공동 1위에 해당합니다. 올해 시즈는 치명적인 포심 패스트볼/슬라이더 조합에 더 균형 잡힌 구종 배합을 더해 상대 타선을 공략하는 다양한 방식을 구사하고 있습니다. 이것이 바로 시즈의 피안타율(.177)이 아메리칸리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 가장 낮은 이유 중 일부입니다.
3. 파커 메식, 클리블랜드 가디언스 (77점)
슐리틀러나 시즈와 같은 반열은 아닐지 몰라도, 메식은 루키 시즌에 부정할 수 없는 환상적인 활약을 펼치고 있습니다. 개성 있는 폼을 지닌 이 좌완 투수는 11일 미네소타 트윈스를 상대로 한 직전 등판에서 5.1이닝 동안 단 1실점만을 허용했으며, 치열한 페넌트레이스 혈전 속에서도 그것이 바로 메식이 해내는 방식입니다. 이번 시즌 5이닝 이상을 소화하면서 1실점 이하만 내준 경기가 슐리틀러와 시즈보다 많은 아메리칸리그 투수는 단 두 명뿐입니다. 메식의 2.51의 평균자책점은 메이저리그 전체 5위에 해당하는 기록입니다. 그의 성공 비결은 바로 포심 패스트볼입니다. 메식은 구속이 시속 94.3마일(약 151.8km)로 아주 빠르지는 않지만, 스타캐스트의 득점 가치(run value) 지표에 따르면 그의 포심은 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 개별 구종 중 하나로 꼽힙니다.
4. 드류 라스무센, 탬파베이 레이스 (52점)
금요일, 탬파베이는 주니어 카미네로의 극적인 끝내기 홈런에 힘입어 올 시즌 구단 중 가장 먼저 포스트시즌 진출을 확정 지었습니다. 잊지 말아야 할 점은 라스무센이 그날 탬파베이의 선발 투수로 등판해 1실점 투구로 7이닝을 가볍게 책임졌다는 사실입니다. 탬파베이가 승리한 것은 놀라운 일이 아닙니다. 그것이 바로 라스무센이 마운드에 올랐을 때 그들이 보여주는 방식이기 때문입니다. 탬파베이는 올스타 브레이크 이전부터 거슬러 올라가 그의 최근 선발 등판 10경기를 모두 승리로 장식했습니다. 31세의 우완 투수인 그는 세 가지 형태의 패스트볼 구종과 완벽한 제구력을 바탕으로 아메리칸리그 평균자책점(2.81), WHIP(0.92), 피안타율(.203) 부문에서 모두 상위 5위 이내에 이름을 올리고 있습니다.
5. 소니 그레이, 보스턴 레드삭스 (37점)
보스턴은 야구계 최고 수준의 투수진을 앞세워 포스트시즌 진출을 향해 순항하고 있습니다. 이 문장은 개막전 당시였다면 당연히 이해되었겠지만, 좌완 투수 개럿 크로셰가 4월 말 이후 부상으로 전력에서 이탈했다는 사실을 안다면 이야기가 다릅니다. 크로셰의 공백 속에서 그레이가 에이스 역할을 톡톡히 해냈습니다. 그는 27경기에 선발 등판해 17승 5패 평균자책점 2.76을 기록 중이며, 투수 승리 기록이 전부를 말해주는 것은 아니지만 아메리칸리그에서 그레이보다 더 많은 승리를 거둔 투수가 없다는 점은 주목할 만합니다. 그는 통산 세 번째 아메리칸리그 사이영상 투표 상위 5위 진입을 노리고 있습니다. 2023년 미네소타 소속으로 투표 2위를 차지했으며, 2015년에는 오클랜드 소속으로 3위에 오른 바 있습니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 리드 데트머스(LA 에인절스), 개빈 윌리엄스(클리블랜드 가디언스), 닉 마르티네즈(탬파베이 레이스), 마이클 와카(캔자스시티 로열스)
내셔널리그
1. 제이콥 미시오로스키, 밀워키 브루어스 (총 160점, 1위 표 32장)
'더 미즈'는 지난 8일 시카고 컵스를 상대로 6.1이닝 동안 탈삼진 9개를 솎아내며 단 1실점만 내주는 센세이션한 투구로 보기 드문 부진을 말끔히 씻어냈습니다. 압도적인 구위를 자랑하는 이 우완 투수는 평균자책점(1.95), 피안타율(.155), 탈삼진(236개)을 포함하여 거의 모든 주요 투수 통계 부문에서 내셔널리그 선두를 달리고 있습니다. 161.1이닝을 소화한 지금까지도 미시오로스키는 여전히 강력한 불을 뿜어내고 있습니다. 그는 이번 시즌 시속 100마일 이상의 공을 무려 1,010개나 던졌으며, 이는 이 부문 2위인 투수(메이슨 밀러, 468개)의 두 배를 훌쩍 뛰어넘는 수치입니다.
2. 크리스 세일, 애틀랜타 브레이브스 (106점)
나이를 가늠할 수 없는 이 불세출의 투수는 시즌 막판 내셔널리그 사이영상 레이스의 격차를 좁히기 위해 최선의 노력을 다하고 있습니다. 세일의 평균자책점 2.18은 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 좋은 기록이자, 37세의 이 베테랑이 2018년 이후 단일 시즌 기준 기록한 가장 낮은 수치입니다. 그는 최근 23경기 연속으로 3실점 이하 경기만을 치르며 놀라울 정도로 꾸준한 모습을 보여주었습니다. 이번 시즌 16경기 이상 연속으로 3실점 이하를 기록한 선발 투수는 그 외에 단 한 명도 없습니다. 세일은 향상된 구속 덕분에 세월을 역행하고 있으며, 선발 투수로 활약한 통산 그 어느 때보다 더 빠른 공을 뿌리고 있습니다.
3. 크리스토퍼 산체스, 필라델피아 필리스 (99점)
산체스는 최근 두 경기에서 총 9실점을 허용하며 이전 모의 투표보다 한 계단 내려앉았습니다. 하지만 이 마른 좌완 투수는 여전히 사이영상 후보로 손색이 없는 시즌을 만들어가고 있습니다. 산체스는 메이저리그 전체에서 두 번째로 많은 이닝(187.1이닝)을 소화했으며, 내셔널리그 규정 이닝 투수 중 5번째로 좋은 평균자책점(2.79)과 3번째로 좋은 FIP(수비 무관 평균자책점, 2.72)를 기록 중입니다. 야구 통계 전문 사이트 베이스볼레퍼런스(Baseball Reference) 기준 WAR에 따르면, 산체스는 7.6의 WAR을 기록하며 2026년 메이저리그에서 가장 가치 있는 투수로 자리매김했습니다.
4. 헤수스 루자르도, 필라델피아 필리스 (52점)
루자르도는 노동절에 내셔널리그 동부지구 선두인 애틀랜타를 상대로 거둔 눈부신 완봉승에 힘입어 최종 사이영상 모의 투표 명단에 이름을 올렸습니다. 이 좌완 투수가 마땅히 받아야 할 찬사를 받는 시점은 이미 한참 지났습니다. 루자르도는 최근 12경기에서 8승 1패 평균자책점 1.66을 기록하며, 7월 1일 이후 메이저리그 전체에서 가장 낮은 평균자책점을 마크했고 8월 내셔널리그 이달의 투수로 선정되었습니다. 지난 시즌 연마한 치명적인 스위퍼를 무기로 장착한 루자르도는 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 높은 탈삼진율(30.4%)을 기록하고 있습니다. 필리스 팬들은 루자르도가 어깨 통증으로 인해 직전 등판을 건너뛰어 가슴을 졸였으나, MRI 검사 후 본인은 "걱정하지 않는다"고 안심시켰습니다.
5. 야마모토 요시노부, LA 다저스 (43점)
우리는 이제 야마모토에게 너무나 많은 것을 기대한 나머지, 지난 9일 레즈전에서 보여준 7이닝 10탈삼진 역투 같은 최고의 피칭조차 당연하게 느껴질 정도입니다. 그는 여전히 할리우드(LA)에 어울리는 화려한 스타 군단 선발진의 에이스로서 26경기에 등판해 평균자책점 2.62를 기록하고 있습니다. 미시오로스키에 이어 내셔널리그에서 두 번째로 낮은 0.88의 WHIP과 .184의 피안타율을 기록 중인 야마모토만큼 주자 출루를 철저히 억제하는 투수는 드뭅니다.
기타 표를 얻은 선수들: 체이스 번스(신시내티 레즈), 에두아르도 로드리게스(애리조나 다이아몬드백스), 메이슨 밀러(샌디에이고 파드리스), 잭 휠러(필라델피아 필리스)

title: Red Sox rule out key reliever for rest of season, provide positive injury update on trade addition
author: Chris Cotillo; Chriscotillo; Ccotillo Com
body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Among a series of minor injury updates offered by Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy on Tuesday came some finality on one key reliever. Righty Justin Slaten, after further assessment by a renowned orthopedist in the Dallas area, won’t return to the Red Sox this year.
Slaten visited Dr. Keith Meister on Monday’s off day and testing on his injured elbow revealed “degenerative changes in the flexor mass,” according to Tracy. Slaten is set for a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection that is all but certain to rule out his return in 2026.
“It’s a big loss,” Tracy said, “at least now, with the finality of knowing we can’t have him back.”
Slaten was placed on the injured list with elbow inflammation in mid-August and dealt with recurring discomfort as he tried to resume throwing. As of the weekend, he was completely shut down from his progression. Now, he will receive the injection and rest in hopes of getting the issue fixed for 2027.
“Probably just means a chronic thing over time, but I’m speculating there,” Tracy said. “I just know that the conservative course of action is PRP, then he’s gonna rehab and go from there. Because of that, it’s probably going to cost him the rest of the season.”
Slaten appeared in 36 games for the Red Sox this year, posting a 4.60 ERA as a mid-relief option ahead of setup man Garrett Whitlock and closer Aroldis Chapman. For the third straight season, injuries were a big part of Slaten’s season. In 2024, he missed about six weeks due to elbow inflammation in July and August. Last season, he was out from June 1 to August 28 with a balky shoulder. This year, he suffered an oblique strain in early April and missed 31 games, then hit the IL again for the final six weeks.
Mead takes step forward
For the first time since having his left wrist broken by a wayward pitch in West Sacramento on July 27, Curtis Mead will do some offensive work in Boston on Wednesday. According to Tracy, Mead — who is out of a cast and has been doing defensive and baserunning drills for weeks — will hit lightly off a tee as he begins his swing progression.
“Mead will begin, tomorrow, introducing tee work,” Tracy said. “Obviously, we’ve talked a lot about the defensive stuff, being able to catch throws and he’s been doing that. Tomorrow, he’ll start doing some tee work with a light bat and then just kinda progress from there.”
With just 12 games left in the regular season, Mead is in a race against the clock to be fully ready for game action, a reality he acknowledged just last week. But it’s still notable that he’s ready to start taking swings in anticipation for potentially returning during the postseason if the Red Sox make a run.
Crochet throws again at Fenway
Left-hander Garrett Crochet took another small step toward a late-season return Tuesday, throwing a two-inning “up-and-down” bullpen (that includes a break simulating a between-inning breather) at Fenway Park. That session came four days after a one-inning high-intensity bullpen on the same mound.
“That went well,” said Tracy. “Everything went well.”
The next step for Crochet might be facing hitters in a live batting practice/simulated game setting but it’s very unlikely he’ll be ready to pitch in a rehab game before Triple-A Worcester’s season ends Sunday. A more likely scenario involves him getting into a simulated game or two and then making a relief appearance late in next week’s final homestand of the year.
“We’ll wait and see on the next steps,” Tracy said. “That was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see how he feels and go from there.”
Guerrero close to return, Kelly has setback
Right-hander Tyron Guerrero, out since September 1 with shoulder inflammation, is with the Red Sox in Arlington and is expected to be activated before Wednesday’s game. Lefty Raymond Burgos and righty Wyatt Olds are the two leading candidates to be sent down as Guerrero takes a roster spot.
“We’ll see how everything goes with that today,” Tracy said.
The return of Guerrero will give the Red Sox another high-octane option at the end of a bullpen that also includes lefty Erik Miller, Whitlock and Chapman (and won’t have Slaten for the rest of the year).
One reliever who won’t contribute the rest of the way is righty Zack Kelly, who has been out since early July with a stress reaction in the olecranon (bone at the tip of the elbow). Kelly had been throwing live BP sessions in Fort Myers and was close to a rehab outing but had a setback last week and will undergo updated imaging this week.
Rafaela progressing
Center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) has said his goal is to rejoin the Red Sox for this weekend’s series against the Rays and that is still in play. He’s back in Boston and going through strength tests on his leg while ramping up his running program.
“Started to increase running volume today,” Tracy said. “Nothing new to report there. He’ll continue to do that over the next 2-3 days and we’ll see where he’s at.”
The Red Sox could be careful with Rafaela and welcome him back early next week when the Guardians are at Fenway Park.
Houck, Oviedo on track for rehab outings
Right-hander Tanner Houck is pitching for the WooSox at Polar Park on Tuesday as planned. His outing was planned as a shorter relief outing (he entered in the seventh, following six strong innings for starter Jedixson Paez) and he’s expected to make another appearance over the weekend in a longer stint on the mound.
Right-hander Johan Oviedo is still on track to make a rehab start in Worcester on Thursday.

“Mead will begin, tomorrow, introducing tee work,” Tracy said. “Obviously, we’ve talked a lot about the defensive stuff, being able to catch throws and he’s been doing that. Tomorrow, he’ll start doing some tee work with a light bat and then just kinda progress from there.”

But it’s still notable that he’s ready to start taking swings in anticipation for potentially returning during the postseason if the Red Sox make a run.
Crochet throws again at Fenway
Left-hander Garrett Crochet took another small step toward a late-season return Tuesday, throwing a two-inning “up-and-down” bullpen (that includes a break simulating a between-inning breather) at Fenway Park. That session came four days after a one-inning high-intensity bullpen on the same mound.
“That went well,” said Tracy. “Everything went well.”
The next step for Crochet might be facing hitters in a live batting practice/simulated game setting but it’s very unlikely he’ll be ready to pitch in a rehab game before Triple-A Worcester’s season ends Sunday. A more likely scenario involves him getting into a simulated game or two and then making a relief appearance late in next week’s final homestand of the year.
“We’ll wait and see on the next steps,” Tracy said. “That was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see how he feels and go from there.”
Guerrero close to return, Kelly has setback
Right-hander Tyron Guerrero, out since September 1 with shoulder inflammation, is with the Red Sox in Arlington and is expected to be activated before Wednesday’s game. Lefty Raymond Burgos and righty Wyatt Olds are the two leading candidates to be sent down as Guerrero takes a roster spot.
“We’ll see how everything goes with that today,” Tracy said.
The return of Guerrero will give the Red Sox another high-octane option at the end of a bullpen that also includes lefty Erik Miller, Whitlock and Chapman (and won’t have Slaten for the rest of the year).
One reliever who won’t contribute the rest of the way is righty Zack Kelly, who has been out since early July with a stress reaction in the olecranon (bone at the tip of the elbow). Kelly had been throwing live BP sessions in Fort Myers and was close to a rehab outing but had a setback last week and will undergo updated imaging this week.
Rafaela progressing
Center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) has said his goal is to rejoin the Red Sox for this weekend’s series against the Rays and that is still in play. He’s back in Boston and going through strength tests on his leg while ramping up his running program.
“Started to increase running volume today,” Tracy said. “Nothing new to report there. He’ll continue to do that over the next 2-3 days and we’ll see where he’s at.”
The Red Sox could be careful with Rafaela and welcome him back early next week when the Guardians are at Fenway Park.
Houck, Oviedo on track for rehab outings
Right-hander Tanner Houck is pitching for the WooSox at Polar Park on Tuesday as planned. His outing was planned as a shorter relief outing (he entered in the seventh, following six strong innings for starter Jedixson Paez) and he’s expected to make another appearance over the weekend in a longer stint on the mound.
Right-hander Johan Oviedo is still on track to make a rehab start in Worcester on Thursday.

title: Reliever Slaten (elbow) expected to miss the rest of the season
author: Perla Paredes
body:
ARLINGTON -- Right-handed reliever Justin Slaten’s season is over, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy announced ahead of Boston’s three-game series opener against the Rangers at Globe Life Field on Tuesday night.
According to Tracy, Slaten met with Dr. Keith Meister, an orthopedist in the Dallas area, and an evaluation revealed “degenerative changes in his flexor mass” in his right elbow.
“Probably just means a chronic thing over time, but I’m speculating there,” Tracy said. “I just know that the conservative course of action is [a platelet-rich plasma injection]. He’s going to rehab and go from there, but because of that, it’s going to probably cost him the season.”
“As we sit here right now, we were operating and moving forward, planning on having to operate without him,” Tracy said. “This maybe adds some finality to the fact that, ‘OK, now the chances of getting him back are slim.’”
The 29-year-old Slaten posted a 4.60 ERA with 39 strikeouts across 31 1/3 innings over 36 appearances for Boston.
“It’s a big loss,” Tracy said. “At least now the finality of knowing we can’t have him back. But you guys have seen the way he can come in and pitch in those big-moment cleanup innings, to get you out of the sixth, seventh inning. We’ve seen him do that, so he’s an important arm. But we have to deal with it and move on.”
Slaten and Garrett Whitlock served as the Sox’s top right-handed setup men when both went down last month. Whitlock returned from the IL on Aug. 29.
When Slaten and Whitlock first went down, Tracy believed he had enough arms to navigate the bullpen. That depth, however, continues to be tested.
Right-hander Tyron Guerrero, who landed on the IL on Sept. 1 with right shoulder inflammation, was expected to be activated Wednesday but experienced muscle cramping in his lower back Tuesday, delaying his return. According to Tracy, the team does not know when Guerrero will be activated.

title: Boston Red Sox Announced Ceddanne Rafaela Update Before Rangers Series
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The Boston Red Sox begin a series on Tuesday night with the Texas Rangers with just 13 regular-season games remaining.
Ahead of the matchup, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy spoke to the media and gave several updates on some of the players currently injured and on the IL.
One of those players is star outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who has been sidelined with a right quadriceps strain since early September.
Red Sox Announce Rafaela Update
There wasn’t any major development in Rafaela’s overall status, but Tracy noted that he began doing increased running volume on Tuesday. He didn’t have anything further to report on a potential timeline, but the injury doesn’t seem overly serious at this point, and Rafaela likely won’t need a crazy ramp-up once he is able to return to the field.
“Rafa started doing increased running volume today, so nothing new to report there. He’ll continue to do that over the next two, three days and we’ll see where he’s at,” Tracy said pregame.
Chad Tracy provides some #RedSox injury updates ⬇️
– Crochet threw today, everything went well
– Guerrero eligible tomorrow
– Rafaela started to increase running volume today, nothing new to report
– Houck is throwing tonight
– Slaten has “some degenerative changes in the flexor… pic.twitter.com/M04YHBmZCP
— NESN (@NESN) September 15, 2026
Rafaela’s 2026 Season
It’s been a tremendous season for Rafaela in his fourth year with the Red Sox.
The Red Sox named Rafaela an All-Star for the first time in his career, and the 25-year-old has hit .282 across 135 games and 535 at-bats. He has recorded 67 runs, 151 hits, 16 home runs, and 70 RBIs while slugging .443 with a .760 OPS.
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston enters Tuesday with an 82-68 overall record, which, as long as they don’t have a late-season collapse, should put them in line to be the second Wild Card team in the American League playoff picture.
There remains a chance they jump the New York Yankees, but they’re 5.0 games behind them for second place in the AL East and the top Wild Card spot. They’re also 8.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the division and the No. 1 overall seed in the AL.

title: Boston Red Sox’ Garrett Crochet Continues to Build Towards Return
author: Roundtable Sports
body:
The 2025 American League Cy Young Award runner-up has been on the injured list since April.
Video Transcript
What's up everyone?
Zach Coe here for Roundtable at Fenway Park.
The Red Sox are getting ready to open up a three-game set down in Arlington, Texas with the Texas Rangers.
But earlier today, right here at Fenway Park, Garrett Crochet threw a 30-pitch bullpen as he continues to work his way back from left shoulder inflammation that landed him on the injured list all the way back in May.
Tuesday's session marks the fourth time that Crochet's thrown live off of a mound, all of them in bullpen sessions, and each one he's ramped up the intensity and workload, culminating in today's session where he threw about 30 pitches here on the mound at Fenway.
Crochet isn't likely to get into any rehab assignment games as Triple-A Worcester ends their season on Sunday.
The next steps for him remain to be determined as the team waits to see how he bounces back from today's 30-pitch session.
But he remains hopeful that he's gonna be able to rejoin this Red Sox pitching staff in a multi-inning relief capacity as they work their way towards the playoffs.
Of course, the first couple games of the Wild Card series begin two weeks from tonight.

title: Red Sox reliever Justin Slaten to miss rest of season with ‘degenerative’ arm issue - The Boston Globe
author: Tim Healey
body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Reliever Justin Slaten’s season is all but over after the discovery of a “degenerative” arm issue, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said Tuesday before a 4-2 loss to the Rangers.
Before the series opener against the Rangers, Slaten went with team medical staff to visit Keith Meister, a highly regarded orthopedic and sports medicine surgeon based in Arlington.
Meister diagnosed the reliever, who had been out with what the club called right elbow inflammation, with a more serious problem.
“There’s some degenerative changes in the flexor mass,” Tracy said. “So that’s substantially different news.”
The flexor is in the forearm and connects to the elbow. Slaten will receive an injection of platelet-rich plasma, which is supposed to stimulate healing. Tracy called it “the conservative course of action.”
Already, with Slaten’s pain lingering well beyond what the Red Sox figured would be a brief shutdown period when he went on the injured list on Aug. 16, he was trending toward not having time to return this season.
“This maybe adds some finality to the fact,” Tracy said. “We were already operating that way, but you still held out hope. ‘Hey, if it can turn the corner and [with] what he’s able to do out of that bullpen. . . . So yeah, it’s a big loss — at least now, the finality of knowing we can’t have it back.”
For Slaten, who turned 29 on Tuesday, it is another in a string of injuries that have limited his impact. Since reaching the majors in 2024, he has missed time because of elbow, shoulder, and oblique issues.
This year, the righthander had a 4.60 ERA overall and a 2.84 ERA in the two months before getting hurt.
The Red Sox’ top setup options for lefthanded closer Aroldis Chapman remain righthander Garrett Whitlock, lefthander Erik Miller, and righthander Tyron Guerrero. They expect Guerrero back from the IL as soon as Wednesday.
“[Slaten is] an important arm,” Tracy said, “but we have to deal with it and move on.”
Crochet builds up workload
Back at Fenway Park, Garrett Crochet on endured his heaviest workload yet in his bid to return for the playoffs, a 30-pitch bullpen session across two simulated innings.
“Everything went well,” Tracy said. “That was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see over the next couple of days how he feels and go from there.”
Among other rehabbing pitchers: Tanner Houck made his third rehab appearance and first for Triple-A Worcester, striking out three of four batters (and walking the other). He threw 22 pitches but only 11 strikes.
The Sox’ plan calls for Houck to pitch for Worcester again late this week, throwing 50 or more pitches in a much longer relief appearance. For playoff purposes, they are keeping their options open, experimenting with Houck in short and long relief.
Progress for Mead
Seven weeks after fracturing his left wrist in his first game with the Red Sox, Curtis Mead is starting a hitting progression.
The infielder is due to begin “tee work” with an “underloaded,” lighter-than-normal bat on Wednesday, Tracy said. An ability to swing comfortably has held back Mead, who for weeks has been throwing/playing catch (including recently actually catching the ball thrown back to him).
Also in a race against the calendar, Mead appears unlikely to return this year unless the Red Sox play deep into the postseason
The running man
Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) has “started to increase running volume” and will continue to do so the next several days, Tracy said. The center fielder has said he hopes to return this weekend when the Red Sox visit the Rays . . . Tracy and his staff gathered for a group dinner Monday, their first time doing so since Kansas City in mid-May. “So to be able to get all of us together and have a meal, it was a nice off day,” he said. Who paid? “The Red Sox.”
Tim Healey can be reached at timothy.healey@globe.com. Follow him @timbhealey.

ARLINGTON, Texas — Reliever Justin Slaten’s season is all but over after the discovery of a “degenerative” arm issue, Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said Tuesday before a 4-2 loss to the Rangers.
Before the series opener against the Rangers, Slaten went with team medical staff to visit Keith Meister, a highly regarded orthopedic and sports medicine surgeon based in Arlington.
Meister diagnosed the reliever, who had been out with what the club called right elbow inflammation, with a more serious problem.
“There’s some degenerative changes in the flexor mass,” Tracy said. “So that’s substantially different news.”
The flexor is in the forearm and connects to the elbow. Slaten will receive an injection of platelet-rich plasma, which is supposed to stimulate healing. Tracy called it “the conservative course of action.”
Already, with Slaten’s pain lingering well beyond what the Red Sox figured would be a brief shutdown period when he went on the injured list on Aug. 16, he was trending toward not having time to return this season.

So yeah, it’s a big loss — at least now, the finality of knowing we can’t have it back.”

title: Wilyer Abreu advantage could be key to Red Sox's playoff push vs Rangers
author: Katie Manganelli
body:
The Boston Red Sox have four series between them and the postseason, which they are all but certain to make. The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees have already clinched their spots and the Red Sox shouldn't be far behind.
They don't have an easy final two weeks ahead, however. Boston will face either a playoff team or playoff hopefuls during the home stretch and they'll be just as hungry as the Sox are to clinch their spot, maintain their standing or improve it.
The final four series begin with the Texas Rangers, who have the American League's third Wild Card spot in their sights — they sit half a game behind the Toronto Blue Jays, the first team out, before their September 15 series opener against Boston. Texas should be playing some of its best baseball with a playoff berth on the line, but the Red Sox have a secret weapon on their side to try and take it off its game: Wilyer Abreu.
The outfielder's success against the Rangers verges on "ownership." Over 17 games against Texas in his career, Abreu is slashing .436/.484/1.018 with five doubles, nine home runs and 22 RBI.
Wilyer Abreu's success against Rangers could be a huge difference maker for Red Sox at the perfect time
His dominance over Texas began in August 2024, Abreu's rookie season, when he hit three homers in one series against it, including a two-homer game. He logged two more two-home run games against the Rangers in 2025 (Opening Day and May 7).
Abreu plays particularly well at Globe Life Field, the Rangers' home ballpark and where they'll face the Sox from September 15-17 for their season series finale. The 27-year-old boasts a shocking 2.035 OPS through eight appearances in Arlington, Texas, and the Red Sox would certainly love him to carry their offense enough to clinch a playoff berth this series.
Boston has some tough pitching matchups ahead, including a potential series-opening date with Jacob deGrom (3.80 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, 186 strikeouts in 149.1 innings pitched) (subscription required). It's also scheduled to face former Washington Nationals starter MacKenzie Gore and possibly Nathan Eovaldi, though the schedule isn't yet confirmed. Eovaldi and Gore haven't been as successful this year as they have in the past, but Eovaldi presents a challenge every time he takes the mound.
Abreu's success against the Rangers hasn't yet reached Rafael Devers-Yankees-Gerrit Cole territory (and it might never feel as good since the Yankees are the Yankees), but he's inching closer with every series. Maybe the yearly two-home run game at Globe Life Field comes right on time to lift the Red Sox into postseason certainty.

title: Boston Red Sox Quickly Announce Caleb Durbin News Before Rangers Series
author: Michael DeRosa
body:
On Tuesday, the Boston Red Sox kick off their series against the Texas Rangers.
The Red Sox are entering this series red-hot. They won each of their last two games against the Kansas City Royals and are looking to extend their winning streak against Texas.
Now, the Red Sox have announced some news regarding Caleb Durbin before their series against the Rangers.
Caleb Durbin Dropping in the Red Sox’s Batting Order
After batting seventh in the Red Sox’s last game against the Royals, Durbin will be hitting eighth against the Rangers.
Jarren Duran will be hitting seventh for Boston with Durbin being dropped in their batting order.
Here is the Red Sox’s full batting order, as reported by Underdog MLB: R. Anthony LF M. Gasper DH A. Rutschman C W. Contreras 1B W. Abreu RF T. Story SS J. Duran CF C. Durbin 3B N. Sogard 2B

title: 「答えは明確」吉田正尚、復帰してもPS落選か 現地メディアが断言「ロースターから外れるべき」
body:
「答えは明確」吉田正尚、復帰してもPS落選か 現地メディアが断言「ロースターから外れるべき」
吉田の置かれている立場は厳しい(C)Getty Images
レッドソックスの吉田正尚は、左太もも裏の張りのため負傷者リスト（IL）入りとなり1か月が経過した。現在もコンディションの回復には至っておらず、今季中の復帰は困難との見方も伝えられている。
また、ポストシーズン進出も視界にとらえるレッドソックスでは、すでに10月の戦力に関する話題も現地メディアを通して伝えられる中で、背番号7には極めて厳しい声が向けられているようだ。
現地時間9月14日、球団の情報を発信する『FANSIDED BOSOXINJECTION』が吉田の起用法を論じる特集記事を配信した。同メディアは、吉田が60日のILには入っていないため、回復の状況次第ではポストシーズンでのメンバー入りもあり得ると指摘する。
その一方で、「たとえヨシダが復帰できたとしても、必ずしもプレーオフのロースターに入れるべきだということにはならない」と主張。今後、26人のロースターを選考する際での“当落線上”の選手と吉田の入れ替えは、「必要無し」と同メディアは訴える。
さらに、ロ―スター外の候補として、ミッキー・ガスパーやニック・ソガードの名前を挙げながらも、「ヨシダのために、ガスパーやソガードをプレーオフのロースターから外すべきではない」と断言。それぞれのパフォーマンスを比較し、吉田については、「87試合に出場して打率.274、出塁率.347、長打率.399、5本塁打。決して悪い数字ではないが、レッドソックスが求める長打力を満たすものとは言い難い」と説明。他にも、「重度のハムストリング負傷から復帰することも考えれば、外野手として戦力になることも期待しにくい」と強調している。

title: Red Sox’s Kutter Crawford May Be Closer to Returning Than Expected
author: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
body:
Over the last few weeks, the Boston Red Sox have gotten positive updates left and right about injured starting pitchers.
First and foremost, Garrett Crochet has been throwing and is trending towards a late-season return in Boston's bullpen, barring a setback. Tanner Houck has been on a minor league rehab assignment and is trending up. Plus, the current expectation is that Johan Oviedo is nearing a minor league rehab assignment as well. Now, it sounds like another hurler is trending up as well. On Tuesday, Tommy Cassell of the Worcester T&G Sports reported that there have been "some rumblings" that Kutter Crawford could join Triple-A Worcester throughout the week as well.
"And there are some rumblings that Kutter Crawford could be in Worcester this week, too," Cassell wrote. "The 30-year-old righty has been sidelined since March with right wrist and forearm issues and made one rehab stint with Worcester on April 11 before being shut down again. Crawford hasn’t been confirmed yet whether he will pitch in Worcester."
Kutter Crawford Is Trending Up
How about that?
Crawford hasn't been talked about in a long time. Now, it seems like the righty could potentially be in Worcester this week. Things move quickly in baseball, to say the least.

title: MacKenzie Gore Starts vs. Red Sox Rookie Jake Bennett
body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — MacKenzie Gore starts Wednesday night for the Texas Rangers against the Boston Red Sox, who have rookie left-hander Jake Bennett scheduled. First pitch at Globe Life Field is 7:05 p.m. CT on Rangers Sports Network.
Gore’s 31 starts are the most in the majors. In his first season with Texas, he is 8-11 with a 4.62 ERA and has struck out 172 batters over 161 2/3 innings. He was an All-Star with the Washington Nationals in 2025.
Saturday, Texas activated Nathan Eovaldi from the injured list and moved him to the bullpen. That left Gore, Jacob deGrom, Kumar Rocker, and Cal Quantrill as the Rangers’ starters.
MacKenzie Gore’s Last Start In Phoenix
Gore last pitched Friday at Chase Field. The Arizona Diamondbacks scored 4 runs on 4 doubles against him in the fifth inning, and he was charged with 4 runs on 5 hits in 4-plus innings. He walked 3 and struck out 2. Arizona won 9-1, and Texas went 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position.
One night earlier, the Rangers lost 4-3 in Seattle after leading 3-0. Rangers manager Skip Schumaker put the two losses together after Friday’s game.
“You’ve got to flush it quickly and try to go about it in a different way tomorrow,” Schumaker said. “Brutal couple of days. There’s no sugarcoating it. But we have a chance to flush it tonight and to win tomorrow.”
Texas won the next two games, 6-2 on Saturday and 7-6 on Sunday.
On Aug. 26 at Rate Field, the Chicago White Sox scored 4 runs on 8 hits against Gore in 3 2/3 innings. He walked 4 in the 10-4 loss. Before that start, Texas had won nine straight games Gore started. He was 2-1 with a 3.32 ERA over his previous eight outings dating to July 12.
deGrom had allowed 8 runs in Chicago the night before, tying a career high, and neither starter finished four innings.
“It starts with starting pitching,” Schumaker explained that night. “I’ve said since day one that the health and production of our starting pitching was going to carry us. We acquired Gore and we knew we had deGrom and [Eovaldi]. We felt pretty good about it. These last two starts were not what they wanted; not what we were thinking was going to happen after winning the first game here.”
“That’s not what we thought we’re going to get,” Schumaker continued. “I don’t think they would tell you [they expected] that either.”
Jake Bennett’s Rookie Season With The Red Sox
Bennett, 25, is 9-7 with a 3.69 ERA. The 6-foot-6 left-hander was a second-round pick of the Nationals in 2022 out of the University of Oklahoma. Boston acquired him from Washington in the offseason. Gore pitched for the Nationals from 2023 to 2025.
Last Wednesday against the Los Angeles Angels at Fenway Park, Bennett allowed 6 runs on 9 hits over 5 1/3 innings in a 6-4 loss.
Boston is 82-68 and third in the American League East. The Red Sox hold an American League wild-card spot with 12 games left. Texas is 74-76 and one game behind the Houston Astros in the American League West, and Houston holds the tiebreaker.
In Tuesday’s opener, deGrom faces Boston left-hander Patrick Sandoval. Right-hander Sonny Gray starts Thursday’s finale for the Red Sox, and Texas has not announced its starter for that game.

title: MLB award predictions 2026: MVPs Ohtani and Judge will be dethroned
author: Jesse Yomtov
body:
MLB award predictions 2026: MVPs Ohtani and Judge will be dethroned
The 2026 Major League Baseball season has less than two weeks to go, and most of league's major awards have runaway favorites – with new faces expected to win the MVP and Cy Young honors in each league.
The Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong will certainly dethrone Shohei Ohtani for the NL MVP award, snapping Ohtani's three-year reign that dates back to his final season with the Los Angeles Angels. In the AL, the Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez is in the running for the Triple Crown and should win the award over the Tampa Ray Rays' Junior Caminero, with back-to-back winner Aaron Judge hampered by an injury this season.
Both expected Cy Young winners are in their second MLB seasons: Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees and Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers. Each right-hander sports an ERA below 2.00 entering Tuesday and have fans amped about the next generation of aces in MLB.
Here's our predictions for the 2026 MLB awards:
AL MVP: Yordan Alvarez, Astros
Triple Crown incoming? The 29-year-old has proven himself as one of the greatest sluggers of the era and should win this award easily, having already set a career-high with 38 home runs. He's the runaway favorite, but Houston getting back into the postseason would even further ice this for Alvarez.
Also in the running: Junior Caminero (Rays), Bobby Witt Jr. (Royals)
NL MVP: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs
With Shohei Ohtani injured this summer, PCA has locked this up as he closes in on the seventh 40-40 season in MLB history. The 24-year-old is putting together one of the greatest years ever, with a 9.3 fWAR while leading the National League in slugging and OPS.
Also in the running: Shohei Ohtani (Dodgers)
AL Cy Young: Cam Schlittler, Yankees
We knew Cam Schlittler was good after his impact as a rookie in 2025, but nobody could have fathomed the 25-year-old would be this good in his sophomore season. The right-hander is having one of the greatest pitching seasons could be the first Yankees pitcher with a sub-2 ERA since Ron Guidry in 1978. Even more impressive is his leading the AL in innings (184.2) and starts (31).
Also in the running: Dylan Cease (Blue Jays)
NL Cy Young: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers
A controversial All-Star selection as a rookie last season, The Miz has been by far the NL's best pitcher at age 24, leading the league in ERA (1.95), strikeouts (236) and WHIP (0.80).
Also in the running: Chris Sale (Braves)
AL Rookie of the Year: Kevin McGonigle, Tigers
Things didn't go as planned for Tarik Skubal's final season in Detroit, but McGonigle's breakthrough is the major positive to take away from this year. The Tigers signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150 million extension and the infielder who was 21 on opening day is currently approaching 7 WAR on the season.
Also in the running: Parker Messick (Guardians), Munetaka Murakami (White Sox)
NL Rookie of the Year: Sal Stewart, Reds
Stewart has been invaluable for the Reds, primarily playing the corner infield positions while also seeing time at second base, racking up 31 home runs with 107 RBIs and 15 steals.
Also in the running: JJ Wetherholt (Cardinals), Nolan McLean (Mets)
